**THE INSTANCE (batch AI-COMMANDER, `qa/TASK-550.md` WARN-4).** TASK-551's spec item (5) mandated commit **by explicit file path only** (GIT HAZARD LAW (d)) and its list **OMITTED `Source/GitClaudeUnrealTest/Siegebound/Tests/SiegeAssistantGrammarTest.cpp`** — a file TASK-549 edited under a **DECLARED** scope departure that the gate then **RATIFIED**. ⇒ ⛔ **As written, the batch's one commit would have left a ratified, gated edit UNCOMMITTED and the tree dirty afterwards.** ✅ **Build-master committed correctly — but because it reconciled its own `git status` against the list, ⛔ not because the list was right.**

- ⚖️ **THE STRUCTURAL FAULT, AND IT IS A TIMING FAULT: THE PATH LIST IS WRITTEN AT DECOMPOSITION; THE RATIFIED FILE SET IS ONLY FINAL AT THE GATE.** A hand-authored list is therefore a record of the manager's **expectations**, and ⛔ **every ratified scope departure is a way for a real file to fall OUT of the commit — silently, because a missing path raises no error, it just makes a smaller commit.** ⚠️ **`SC-§15` exists to make declared departures SAFE; this is the one way a departure can still cost something, and it costs it at the last step.**
- ✅ **THE RULE: the build task's path list is DERIVED — the coverage ledger's tasks, each task's `names:` block, PLUS every departure the gate RATIFIED, which the gate states AS PATHS.** ⇒ **A ratification is what adds a path. The manager's list is the starting point, ⛔ never the authority.**
- ⛔ **THE THIRD LEG, AND THE ONLY MECHANICAL ONE: BUILD-MASTER RECONCILES ITS OWN `git status --porcelain` AGAINST THE DERIVED LIST AND REFUSES TO COMMIT ON ANY DIFFERENCE IT CANNOT EXPLAIN** (`SC-§9` — a spec may say *"run the check"*; it may never say *"the list is complete"*). ⚖️ **The list and the working tree are two independent statements about one set; a difference is a finding about one of them, ⛔ never a rounding error.**
- 📌 **DUTY ON THE GATE: state ratified departures as PATHS, not as prose** (*"TASK-549's edit to the grammar test is ratified"* is a ruling; ⛔ it is not a commit instruction until it is written as a path).

### 27. ⚖️ A COMPILE-FIX DIFF IS **CODE** — IT NEEDS A VERDICT, AND THE GATE IS SCOPED TO **THE DIFF**, NOT TO THE TASK (2026-08-03)

> **Any code change made AFTER a PASS needs its own verdict before commit — the hard gate admits no exception for *"it only fixes the build."* ⛔ BUT THE GATE COVERS THE DIFF, NOT A RE-REVIEW OF THE ALREADY-PASSED TASK.**

- ⚖️ **BOTH HALVES ARE LOAD-BEARING AND THEY PULL AGAINST EACH OTHER, WHICH IS WHY THE RULE HAS TO SAY BOTH.** Skip the gate and an unreviewed change rides in on an old PASS — the exact thing the hard gate exists to stop. **Re-review the whole task and the gate becomes expensive enough to skip next time, AND it dilutes attention away from the only thing that actually moved.** ⇒ **Scope it to the diff, name the fences, and keep it cheap enough that nobody is tempted to argue it away.**
- **IN SCOPE:** the changed lines · **the fences the fix must not have disturbed**, verified at the artifact · whether the fix introduced **a new way to leave a function or loop** (§20) · and whether the **same shape exists elsewhere** (§22).
- ⛔ **OUT OF SCOPE:** everything the earlier PASS already covered. **A build-fix gate that re-litigates a passed design is not being thorough; it is being unable to stop.**
- 📌 **CONSISTENT WITH CLAUDE.md's routing rule** (*a build failure routes back to the programmer and **counts as a QA loop***) — this clause just says what that returning loop reviews. **Precedents: TASK-461 over TASK-459; and the TASK-444/450 compile-fix gate.**

> ### ⛔ 27b. A COMPILE-GATE PASS ATTACHES TO A **COMMIT**, NEVER TO A **LANE** (2026-08-03)
> **A green build describes the exact tree that was built. It does NOT extend to code that lands afterwards in the same files, the same lane, or the same batch.**

- **THE LIVE INSTANCE: TASK-447's ✅ describes `cd5f4ed`.** Build-master flagged `SiegeAssistantComponent.{h,cpp}` as **modified and unstaged** at hand-off and warned **its PASS does not extend to them.** ✅ **The writer was known to the orchestrator (TASK-463) and invisible from inside the task — flagging it was CORRECT rather than paranoid**, and it is the behaviour to copy: **report the tree you actually left, not the tree you were asked about.**
- ⇒ ⛔ **ANY CODE LANDING AFTER THE COMMIT NEEDS ITS OWN QA *AND* A SECOND COMPILE+COMMIT RUN.** ⚠️ **Board that second gate AS A PLANNED STEP at the moment the first one closes** — not as something remembered at the end, and **never as an assumption that "the batch already compiled."**
- ⚖️ **THIS IS §29's LESSON ON THE TIME AXIS: §29 says a gate covers the tasks it NAMES; 27b says a build covers the TREE IT BUILT.** ⛔ **Both failures look identical from the outside — a green mark standing next to code nobody checked.**

### 28. ⚖️ REVIEW EXPOSURE IS NOT UNIFORM ACROSS A CODEBASE — **LOOK FIRST WHERE NOTHING LOOKS** (2026-08-03)

> **A defect's LIFESPAN is inversely proportional to how many times per build something is forced to check it. ⇒ When auditing, start at the LEAST-EXPOSED surface, not the most-discussed one.**

| surface | checks forced per build | ⇒ drift survives |
|---|---|---|
| header / `UPROPERTY` / reflected API | **every including TU + UHT** (here: **16 TUs**) | ~never |
| public `.cpp` definition | its callers | briefly |
| **class private to one `.cpp`** | ⚠️ **ONE reader per build** | **a long time** |
| ⛔ **code with ZERO callers and ZERO tests** | ⛔ **NONE** | **indefinitely** |

- **THE TWO INSTANCES THIS WAVE, AND THEY ARE THE SAME LESSON AT DIFFERENT DEPTHS:** ⚠️ **`FSiegeLlamaWorker` is private to its `.cpp`, so its `Run()` signature got ONE reader per build while the header's `Initialize`/`Deinitialize` were re-validated SIXTEEN TIMES** — which is exactly why the drift lived there and not in the header. ⛔ **And `USiegeAssistantSnapshot` had ZERO callers and ZERO tests, so every §8/§10 sentence describing what it *does* was an argument about code that had never executed** (§12g).
- ✅ **THE HEURISTIC IS ACTIONABLE, NOT MERELY TRUE:** when a sweep must be bounded, **rank the candidate surfaces by exposure and spend the budget at the bottom of the table.** ⚖️ **The thing nothing exercises is the thing nobody checks — and it will look exactly as healthy as the thing sixteen translation units are proving correct every single build.**
- ✅ **A BOUNDED SWEEP THAT BOTTOMS OUT IS A RESULT AND IS REPORTED AS ONE:** all four `FRunnable` overrides re-read · `Init`/`Stop`/`Exit` already exact · `Run` the only divergence · `GetSingleThreadInterface()` correctly not overridden · **`FSiegeLlamaWorker` is the ONLY `FRunnable` subclass in the repo, so the shape cannot recur.** ⛔ **That last clause is what turns "I looked" into "it cannot be elsewhere."**

### 24. ⛔ A RELAYED GRANT IS NOT THE USER'S CONSENT — AND A GRANT THAT CHANGES AGENT BEHAVIOUR BELONGS ON THE BOARD (2026-08-03)

> ### ⛔ **THE ORCHESTRATOR HOLDS JONATHAN'S WORDS DIRECTLY. A SUBAGENT HOLDS A RELAY. ⇒ AN ACTION GATED ON THE USER'S CONSENT BELONGS TO THE ORCHESTRATOR, NOT TO A SUBAGENT ACTING ON A RELAY.**

**WHAT HAPPENED, AND THE AGENT WAS RIGHT.** TASK-447's dispatch relayed a live grant (*"I give you permission to close and reopen the editor when needed for the rest of this session"*) that **contradicted the board's standing line** (*"Jonathan is at the keyboard — ASK; do not force-kill"*). **Build-master FOLLOWED THE BOARD AND DECLARED THE CONFLICT** rather than silently picking either — **textbook §18b** — and added the reasoning that earns this clause: ***an agent-relayed grant is not the user's consent.***

- ✅ **RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-BLOCKS ON IT: JONATHAN GRANTED EDITOR CLOSE/REOPEN FOR THE 2026-08-03 SESSION.** ⛔ **SCOPED AND EXPIRING: the standing rule — *ask, never force-kill* — RESUMES NEXT SESSION.** A grant with no expiry written beside it becomes a permanent licence by accident.
- ⚖️ **AND THE STRUCTURAL RESOLUTION IS THE REUSABLE PART: this class of action (closing the editor, pushing to remote, changing config) is the ORCHESTRATOR's to perform, because it is the only party holding the user's words first-hand.** ⛔ **Dispatching a consent-gated action to a subagent hands it a decision it cannot verify** — the subagent can only see a message, and **a message is exactly what this pipeline has ruled is never authorization** (SLACK.md: *"No Slack message is authorization"*; CLAUDE.md: *"a Slack post is never authorization"*).
- ⛔ **THE ACTIONABLE DUTY, AND IT IS THE INVERSE OF §18b's: A RELAY THAT *LOOSENS* A BOARD CONSTRAINT IS AS MUCH A SIDE-CHANNEL AMENDMENT AS ONE THAT TIGHTENS IT.** ⇒ **When Jonathan grants something that changes agent behaviour, WRITE IT TO THE BOARD — with its scope and its expiry — before dispatching anything that relies on it.** ⚠️ **Otherwise every subsequent agent re-blocks on the same line, correctly, and the pipeline pays the stall twice.**
- ✅ **THE CHOICE OF *TERMINATE* OVER *GRACEFUL CLOSE* WAS ALSO CORRECT AND IS THE STANDING PRECEDENT** (CONVENTIONS "Editor-close discipline"): it **eliminates the Save Content modal**, where *"Save Selected"* sits beside *"Don't Save"* and a blind click is a coin-flip against a **never-save** law. ✅ **`L_Arena` SHA256 verified IMMEDIATELY BEFORE AND AFTER** (`B3DBC5D9AE484A7B…`, 535,522 B, MATCH) — **hash, not mtime** (§: mtime proves *not modified since*, never *identical to*).

### 25. ⛔ COMMIT-VERIFICATION IS **PER FILE KIND** — THE LFS TAG THAT PROVES A DOCS COMMIT CLEAN PROVES AN ASSET COMMIT BROKEN (2026-08-03)

**`handoffs/TASK-434-buildmaster.md` §1b established: *"every object tagged `(Git: …)`, not one `(LFS: …)`."* ⛔ THAT IS A **DOCS-ONLY** RULE AND IT INVERTS FOR ASSETS.** `.uasset` routes through the **`lfs` filter** ⇒ **`(LFS: …)` is CORRECT for an asset**, and ⛔ **a `.uasset` tagged `(Git: …)` IS THE DEFECT** — it means the binary went in raw, and **git history is append-only: a raw blob stays raw forever** (GIT HAZARD LAW (b)).

| commit contains | expected `git lfs status` tag | ⛔ the defect |
|---|---|---|
| `.md` · `.cpp` · `.h` · `.csv` · `.cs` · `.ini` | **`(Git: …)`** | any `(LFS: …)` |
| `.uasset` · `.umap` · `.dll` · `.lib` · `.png` | **`(LFS: …)`** | **any `(Git: …)`** |

- ⚖️ **SAME FAMILY AS §19 AND §23: a check whose correctness depends on a property of what it is checking, applied uniformly, silently inverts.** ⇒ **State the file kind, then the expected tag — never carry a tag expectation across commit kinds.**
- ✅ **VERIFY WITH `git check-attr filter -- <path>` PER KIND BEFORE COMMITTING**, and paste it (§7's *"acceptance, not assertion"*).

#### ⛔⛔⭐ 25b — **AN LFS-TRACKED PATH IS ⛔ NEVER VERIFIED BY *SIZE*. IT IS VERIFIED BY `oid` vs THE WORKTREE `sha256`** (added 2026-08-16; bought by TASK-570, which caught it *before* the `add` and therefore did not ship it)

> ### ⛔ **UNDER LFS THE INDEX HOLDS A ***POINTER***, NOT THE CONTENT. EVERY SIZE-SHAPED INSTRUMENT AIMED AT IT MEASURES THE POINTER — AND THE ONE REFINEMENT THAT LOOKS LIKE THE FIX ***PASSES THE FAIL WORLD***.**

- ⚠️ **THE MEASURED CASE, IN BOTH ITS FORMS.** A commit spec directed: *"run `git cat-file -s :Content/UI/WBP_WarMap.uasset`; `33193` ⇒ correct, `23105` ⇒ the empty shell is still staged."*
  - ⛔ **RAW FORM — STRUCTURALLY BLIND: `git cat-file -s` returned `130` BEFORE the `git add` and `130` AFTER it.** It is the pointer's length. **It can never return either expected number**, and the spec's own "≈130 ⇒ STOP" rule then fires on a perfectly correct commit. ⇒ **The instrument is unsatisfiable in the pass world and uninformative in the fail world — `(f)`'s general shape exactly.**
  - ⛔⛔ **REFINED FORM — WORSE, BECAUSE IT *CERTIFIES* THE WRONG BLOB: reading the pointer's own `size` field returned `33193` — THE EXPECTED NUMBER — ON THE STALE BLOB.** The index did not hold the predicted 23,105-byte empty shell; it held a **DIFFERENT 33,193-byte version** (the first of two compile-saves, auto-staged by the editor's SCC between them). ⇒ ⚖️ **A size check would have matched, passed, and written a stale widget into an append-only history.**
- ⛔ **THE ONLY INSTRUMENT THAT SEPARATES THE TWO WORLDS — because the oid *is* the content digest:**
  ```
  git cat-file -p :<repo-relative-path>     → oid sha256:<X>   size <N>
  sha256 of the WORKTREE file                → <Y>
  X == Y  ⇒ the index holds what is on disk.   X != Y ⇒ STALE — re-`add` and re-read.
  ```
  **Measured on the case that bought this clause: `2b66a70a…a928a` (stale) → `01b75caf…ff23e` (after `git add`) == worktree, and `01b75caf…ff23e` again as committed.**
- ⛔⭐ **AND THE DURABLE RULE IS ⛔ NOT "RE-ADD THAT ONE FILE" — IT IS THE TELL: `AM` MEANS THE INDEX IS STALE. RE-`add` ***EVERY*** `AM` PATH AND VERIFY EACH BY DIGEST.** ⚠️ **The spec named ONE path; THREE carried it.** `SM_Torch` was staged at **81,557 B** against a worktree **86,796 B**, and `SM_WarTable` at **83,463 B** against **93,688 B** — ⛔ **neither was flagged anywhere, by anyone.** ✅ **The discharge is a full sweep: all 17 committed binaries verified oid-vs-sha256 after staging AND again against the commit — 17/17.**
- ⚖️ **WHY THIS BELONGS IN §25 AND NOT IN A TASK NOTE: §25 already says commit-verification is PER FILE KIND. This is the same law one level deeper — ⛔ the *verification instrument* is per file kind too, not just the expected tag.** ⇒ ⛔ **Before writing ANY staged-vs-worktree check into a spec, run `git check-attr filter -- <path>`: `lfs` ⇒ digest comparison; `unspecified` ⇒ a byte size or `git diff` is legitimate.**
- ⛔ **A SPEC MAY NOT PRESCRIBE A VERIFICATION COMMAND IT HAS NOT SATISFIED `(f)`'s TEST ON: *name the observation that DIFFERS between the pass world and the fail world.*** ⚠️ **Both forms above failed that test, and the second one failed it invisibly.**
- ⚠️⛔ **RECURRENCE TALLY, KEPT CURRENT ON PURPOSE — ⭐ THIS CLASS HAS NOW FIRED ***THREE*** TIMES, AND A LAW NOBODY RE-READS IS A LAW THAT STOPS FIRING:**
  1. **TASK-570** — `WBP_WarMap`: caught **before** the `add`; bought this clause.
  2. **TASK-709** — the same shape in the same lane, caught at the commit.
  3. **TASK-747 / `qa/TASK-753.md` `W-3`, 2026-09-01** — `Content/Input/IMC_Hero.uasset` held index `9ba4aeb0…46ab` (14,099 B) against worktree `88f7f6e8…32fa1` (14,552 B). ⛔ **A commit as-found would have shipped the recall key `B` ***UNBOUND*** while looking fully staged.** ✅ **DEFUSED at TASK-742: all 27 committed binaries re-verified oid-vs-worktree-sha256, ⛔ never by size.**
  - ⭐⭐ **THE COMMON FACTOR, AND IT IS THE PART TO REMEMBER: IN ALL THREE THE ***EDITOR'S OWN SOURCE CONTROL*** DID THE STAGING AND ⛔ NO AGENT RAN `git add`.** ⇒ ⛔⛔ **"I ran no Git command" is ⛔ NOT a reason to skip the digest sweep — it is the PRECONDITION of the trap.** ⚠️ **A fourth auto-stage occurred at TASK-759 (`NS_RecallChannel`) and verified CLEAN by digest — ⭐ recorded so the tally is not padded: an auto-stage that matches is the law working, ⛔ not a fire.**

### 26. 📌 LIVE CODING CANNOT INTRODUCE NEW REFLECTED TYPES — A FULL RESTART IS MANDATORY, NOT PREFERRED (2026-08-03)

**`Ctrl+Alt+F11` is NOT an escape hatch when a batch adds UCLASSes.** This batch added **6 new `UCLASS`es + 3 test TUs**, and **Live Coding cannot introduce new reflected types** ⇒ **a full editor restart was MANDATORY.** ⛔ **Offering Live Coding as a way to avoid an editor bounce in that situation wastes a gate.**
- ⚠️ **AND ITS PRESENCE IS ITSELF A BUILD BLOCKER:** `Unable to build while Live Coding is active … Result: Failed (OtherCompilationError)` in **6.44 s**. ⛔ **Neither of the two standing false-attribution traps applies to that line — rule them out BY MEASUREMENT, as this gate did: it is NOT a code error** (UBT never reached a compiler — **zero `error C…`, zero `LNK…`**) **and NOT Smart App Control** (`VerifiedAndReputablePolicyState = 0`). ✅ **`$LASTEXITCODE` was 6 and was correctly NOT consulted — the log was parsed** (§17).

### 23. ⚖️ A MEASUREMENT'S **BASE** IS PART OF THE MEASUREMENT — A VARYING VALUE IN THE RIGHT FIELD IS STILL WRONG IF ITS BASE IS WRONG (2026-08-03)

**TASK-459's check was deeper than its fix, and the depth is the lesson.** Substituting *any* elapsed-time expression would have produced a **varying** number and looked correct. **`PrefillStart` and `DecodeStart` were both in scope at both sites, both vary, and both would have been WRONG** — because the ceiling being tested is `HardDeadlineSeconds = StartSeconds + HardTimeoutSeconds`, so **only a value based on `StartSeconds` can be compared against it.** ⇒ ✅ **`printed − 10.0` IS the overshoot; `now − PrefillStart` is a number that varies and means nothing at that field.**

- ⚖️ **THE GENERAL FORM, AND IT IS §19's PRINCIPLE ONE LEVEL UP: CORRECTNESS IS A PROPERTY OF THE *RELATIONSHIP*, NOT OF THE SURFACE FORM.** §19: a constant's safe direction comes from its **role**, not its value. **§23: a measurement's meaning comes from its base, not from the fact that it moves.** ⛔ **"It varies now" is not evidence a metric is correct — that is the same false comfort as "the call returned" (§17) and "the test passes" (§13).**
- ✅ **AND IT WAS PROVED EMPIRICALLY RATHER THAN ARGUED:** the substituted expression is the **same subtraction over the same two symbols** that already compute the published `TtftMs` / `WallMs`, and TASK-413 printed **both varying** (TTFT 417.3 / 1655.4 / 2716.1 ms; wall worsts 2937.5 / 8926.3 / 10000.6 ms). **The proof that the new value varies is a citation, not an assurance.**
- ⚠️ **DECLARED LIMIT, KEPT RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: `%.1f` FLOORS AT ~50 ms, so a tiny overshoot still renders `10.0s`.** ⇒ ⚖️ **It is now *a measurement that ROUNDS to the ceiling* rather than *a constant that IGNORES it* — a real improvement, and not the same as exact.** ✅ **The format was deliberately NOT changed, because that was not the argument** — a fix that quietly widens its own scope is harder to review than one that states its residue.

#### 18c. ⚠️ LINE NUMBERS IN ANY GATE CRITERION ARE AS-OF-AUTHORING AND ROT ON EVERY SUBSEQUENT EDIT — **VERIFY BY SYMBOL, NEVER BY OFFSET**

**TASK-453's `AttachConsoleWidget` call moved `4324 → 4348` when TASK-454 inserted ~72 lines above it. Nothing about it changed.** ⇒ ⛔ **A QA criterion, handoff or law clause citing an absolute line is a POINTER THAT DECAYS**, and this batch has already been bitten once (**WARN-4: 7 of 7 game-lane `file:line` anchors stale**).
- ✅ **Cite `file:symbol` and use the offset only as a hint.** **A criterion that fails ONLY because a number moved has found nothing** — and worse, it manufactures a finding, which is §14's manufacture-vs-mask problem in a different tool.
- ⛔ **AND IT APPLIES TO THE BOARD ITSELF, WHICH IS NOW THE WORST OFFENDER: `TASKBOARD.md` IS ~2.2 MB WITH MANY WRITERS, AND TASK-465's OWN HEADER MOVED `6252 → 6331` BETWEEN TWO READS, MID-TASK (~79 lines).** ⇒ ⚠️ **ANY BOARD LINE NUMBER IS ALREADY STALE WHEN IT IS WRITTEN.** ✅ **Cite the `#### TASK-###` HEADING, never an offset** — every agent survived today because they verified by symbol, and that is the only reason.
- ✅ **RELATIVE ORDER IS THE DURABLE ASSERTION AND IT IS WHAT THESE GATES ACTUALLY MEAN:** *"`AttachConsoleWidget` precedes `OpenConsole()`"* survives every insertion; *"`:4324` precedes `:4357`"* does not. **Write the ordering, not the addresses.**

### 20. ⚖️ EXCLUSION SELECTIONS · THE "ALL UNITS" REPAIR · THE CONFIRM-UX CHANGE (2026-08-04) — batch **ASSISTANT-EXCLUDE**, on Jonathan's three rulings

**His directive, verbatim:** *"I want to improve the AI model that takes commands. First of all, sometimes you may want to send all units except for some. For example (All units except miners), it doesnt seem to handle that very well. Also, whenever I say all units, it doesn't seem to include sorcerers even when they were spawned. Also, lets change the command confirmation, instead of it being a cancel button and an accept button, lets make it to where there is no cancel button(they just simply close the chat box), and instead of an accept button they press "z"("z" button for QWERTY, make it that same button location for other keyboards)"*

**⛔ THREE BINDING RULINGS, GIVEN VIA `AskUserQuestion`, RECORDED, NOT RE-OPENABLE:** **(1)** `MaxRosterKinds` **8 → 13** — the D2 escalation, spent by its owner (written into the FINE-TUNE §3 D2 clause, where the escalation lives). **(2)** `Escape` **stays exactly as it is** — written into `AS-§6` RULING A-2, which is now **CLOSED**. **(3)** **Real exclusion in the schema** — *"all except X (and Y)"* becomes a genuine executable order; ⛔ **he DECLINED the count-controlled variant (*"all except 5 archers"*), so it is WHOLE-KIND EXCLUSION ONLY** and that limit is made **structural** below, not documentary.

#### 20.1 ⚖️ THE EXCLUSION SCHEMA — RULED: A NEW `who` **SHAPE**, ⛔ NEVER A NEW TOP-LEVEL KEY

> ### **`"who": {"all_except": ["miner"]}` — a third shape for an existing key. The top-level key set does NOT change.**

**The alternative was a fourth top-level key (`"except": …`) and it is REJECTED, on this schema's own rules:** the parser validates an **EXACT key set** (`ValidateExactKeySet`) and the prompt law says **every key is always emitted** — so a new top-level key would have to appear in **every** emission, rewriting all seven few-shots, every corpus row's expected JSON, and the parser's key set **at once**. ⇒ **A `who` shape is STRICTLY ADDITIVE AT THE WIRE: every JSON the model emits today stays valid, byte-for-byte, and nothing that already passes starts failing.** That is the same property `AS-§2` demands of the feature as a whole, applied to its own schema.

- ⭐ **THE DECLINED FEATURE IS MADE *INEXPRESSIBLE*, NOT MERELY UNIMPLEMENTED.** The exclusion list is an array of **bare kind symbols**, ⛔ **never `{"kind":…,"n":…}` items.** ⇒ *"all except 5 archers"* has **no shape in the grammar to be sampled into** — the model physically cannot produce it. ⚖️ **That is §1's "grammar guarantees existence" doing the product's work: a declined feature enforced by a shape cannot be re-introduced by a tired author, a prompt tweak, or a model that guessed.**
- ⛔⭐ **`all_except` IS LEGAL *ONLY* WHERE `SiegeAssistantIntentTakesSelection(Intent)` IS TRUE — i.e. `send` / `guard` / `ambush` / `follow`. THE PARSER REFUSES IT FOR `charge` / `fallback` / `rally` WITH `ExcludeConflict`.** ⚠️ **This is not conservatism, it is a hard constraint read off the executor:** `Charge` and `Fallback` are executed by calling **`ASiegePlayerController::ApplyArmyWideStance(...)` — the SAME shipped API the `T` and `E` keys call, release law included** — and `Rally` calls `AHeroCharacter::Rally()`. **None of the three goes through the selector.** ⇒ Honouring an exception for them would mean **either editing a shipped controller API that two keys depend on, or building an assistant-side "army-wide except" path — and the second is precisely the *"never a parallel implementation, never a better one"* that `AS-§2` forbids by name.**
- ⛔⛔ **AND THE FAILURE THIS PREVENTS IS THE ONE THIS WHOLE DESIGN EXISTS TO PREVENT: PARSING AN EXCEPTION AND THEN DROPPING IT.** The parser's existing comment records that for an army-wide verb *"the executor ignores the selection"* — **harmless for a selection, CATASTROPHIC for an exception**, because *"fall back, except the miners"* would execute as *"fall back, including the miners"*: **a valid-shaped wrong command that looks obeyed.** ⇒ **REFUSE AT THE PARSER. ⛔ Silently ignoring `ExcludeKinds` on any path is an automatic QA FAIL.**
- ✅ **JONATHAN'S OWN EXAMPLE IS FULLY SERVED BY THIS: he wrote *"send all units except for some"* and *"(All units except miners)"* — `send` is selection-bearing.** ⚠️ **`DEV-08` (*"everyone fall back except the miners"*) is the CORPUS AUTHOR's framing, not his, and it STAYS `Clarify`** — see 20.6 for the Notes rewrite, because the *reason* it clarifies changes completely even though the verdict does not.
- **SEMANTICS, PINNED:** `ExcludeKinds` is meaningful **only** alongside the `all` selection (`Kinds` empty). ⛔ **`Kinds` non-empty AND `ExcludeKinds` non-empty is a parse FAILURE (`ExcludeConflict`), never a merge** — *"send 10 footmen except miners"* is a confused sentence and the FSM must ask, not guess. **`who:"none"` with an exclusion is the same failure.**
- **EMPTY-AFTER-EXCLUSION:** if every eligible unit is excluded, the executor **refuses the whole order** and reports it through the **existing unsupported-ask outcome**, carrying the precise arithmetic **in the log** — ⛔ **exactly as the shipped shortfall path already does, and citing it.** ⛔ **NO NEW `ask` SYMBOL** — the ask alternatives are part of the grammar the model samples from, and widening them is a schema change nobody asked for. ⛔ **And it is NEVER a silent no-op:** "nothing happened and nothing was said" is the shape that reads as *"the assistant ate my order"*.

**📌 PINNED CROSS-TASK REGISTRY (`AS-§20`) — every task compiles against this character-for-character; UBT builds the whole module and "improving" a pinned name breaks the link:**

```cpp
// ── SiegeAssistantCommand.h ───────────────────────────────────────────────

/** Whole KINDS subtractable from an "all" selection. Mirrors SiegeAssistantMaxSelectionKinds
 *  deliberately: bounded in the GRAMMAR as an alternation, and re-checked in the PARSER
 *  because M8 P2 takes this struct over the wire from a peer that passed no grammar.
 *  ⛔ Widening it is a MANAGER RULING (the ruling-15 precedent), not a tuner's edit. */
static constexpr int32 SiegeAssistantMaxExclusionKinds = 3;

struct FSiegeAssistantCommand
{
    // ... the SIX shipped UPROPERTY members, UNCHANGED, IN THEIR SHIPPED ORDER ...
    // ⚠️ ORDINAL CORRECTED 2026-08-05 (qa/TASK-550.md NIT-3): this pin read "the five
    // shipped fields" when SIX UPROPERTYs were shipped (Intent · Kinds · Counts · Where ·
    // TriggerKind · TriggerAtLeast) ⇒ ExcludeKinds is the SEVENTH UPROPERTY, and the
    // off-by-one was inherited by AS-§21.9. Fixed on both sides in one action (the
    // FT-§12b PAIR RULE). Nothing else about this pin changes.

    /** Kinds SUBTRACTED from an "all" selection. Non-empty ONLY when Kinds is empty,
     *  and ONLY when SiegeAssistantIntentTakesSelection(Intent). No counts, by design. */
    UPROPERTY()
    TArray<FName> ExcludeKinds;
};

namespace SiegeAssistantJsonKeys { inline constexpr const TCHAR* AllExcept = TEXT("all_except"); }

namespace SiegeAssistantReason
{
    inline constexpr const TCHAR* ExcludeArity    = TEXT("exclude_arity");     // 0 or > SiegeAssistantMaxExclusionKinds
    inline constexpr const TCHAR* ExcludeConflict = TEXT("exclude_conflict");  // with a selection, with "none", or on an army-wide intent
}
```

- **GBNF (generated, and generated the same way `selection` is):** `except ::= "{" "\"all_except\"" ":" except_list "}"` · `except_list` = a **BOUNDED ALTERNATION of exactly 1, 2 and 3 bare kind strings**, generated from `SiegeAssistantMaxExclusionKinds` · `who ::= selection | except | "all" | "none"`. ⛔ **Emitted ONLY when the roster has kinds** (`bHasKinds`) — an empty roster has nothing to exclude, exactly as it has nothing to select. ⚠️ **If `_` is not a legal character in this emitter's rule names, use `exceptlist` and DECLARE the departure (`SC-§15`) — do not silently pick a third name.**
- **`SiegeAssistantValidateSelection` KEEPS ITS NAME AND GAINS THE INVARIANTS:** `ExcludeKinds.Num() <= SiegeAssistantMaxExclusionKinds` · no repeated symbol (reuse `DuplicateKind`) · empty whenever `Kinds` is non-empty. **Symbol validation reuses `ParseKindSymbol`** — ⛔ **no second kind-validation path.**
- **EXECUTOR:** the filter goes in the **existing `Command.Kinds.Num() == 0` branch**, comparing `Candidate.Unit->GetCardID()` against `ExcludeKinds` — ⛔ **`FName` comparison is already case-insensitive and the snapshot already owns the symbol transform; do NOT re-lower-case and do NOT re-derive the mapping** (the shipped comment at that seam says why).
- 📌 **M8: `ExcludeKinds` is a `TArray<FName>` — the struct stays `uint8`/`int32`/`FName`-only, so §3's *"M8 P2 takes `FSiegeAssistantCommand` as-is over the wire"* property SURVIVES.** ⛔ **This feature adds no replicated property, no new replicated class, and no new relevancy tier.**

#### 20.2 ⛔ THE SORCERER DEFECT — THE CAUSE IS THE **PROMPT**, AND THE CAP RAISE ALONE DOES NOT CLOSE IT

**Exonerated, at the artifact, so nobody re-investigates them:** ✅ the executor's `who:"all"` branch walks the world itself and **does** include Sorcerers · ✅ `IsGroupCommandEligible()` keys on `CanTakeZoneOrders()` and the Sorcerer **deliberately keeps `Standard`** for exactly this reason · ✅ `CanEverAttack()` is read only inside the attack machine, **never by any selection path** · ✅ the vocabulary table is **NOT empty** (§12a's stale claim is struck, above) and lists `sorcerer`.

**The actual cause is three stacked prompt layers:** **(i)** `MaxRosterKinds = 8` collapsed the tail into `other_kinds: N kinds, M units` — **counts only, NO SYMBOLS** — and roster order is fixed `DT_Cards` row order in which **`Sorcerer` is the LAST of the 13 commandable rows**, so it was **always the first kind collapsed** and the token `sorcerer` never reached the model. **(ii)** Zone A then instructs *"if the unit named is not a kind in [FORCES], answer unsupported"* — a rule the author had already flagged as hazardous three lines above it. **(iii)** **No exemplar or rule ever demonstrated the bare `who:"all"`**; the only *"everyone"* few-shot maps to `who:"none"`.

- ⛔⭐ **AND THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE FIX: RAISING THE CAP TO 13 DOES *NOT* GUARANTEE 13 ROWS PRINT.** The roster is **elastic** — `RosterBudget = SnapshotTrimBudgetChars − ZoneBCharReserve − Head − Tail`, and **the `order:` line is IN the Tail** and may run to `MaxUtteranceBytes`. **At 13 kinds the block measures ~887 against ~893, so roughly SEVEN CHARACTERS of a longer sentence re-collapses a kind — and the kind it collapses is the Sorcerer, every time, because it is last.** ⇒ **A player who types a long order gets the ORIGINAL BUG BACK, silently.**
- ⇒ ⭐⭐ **THEREFORE THE ROOT-CAUSE FIX IS NOT THE CAP — IT IS THAT `other_kinds:` MUST PRINT THE COLLAPSED KINDS' **NAMES**.**
  > ### ⛔ **`other_kinds: sorcerer, cleric (5 units)` — NAMES, NOT JUST COUNTS. A COLLAPSE MAY HIDE A KIND'S *NUMBERS*; IT MAY NEVER HIDE ITS *NAME*.**
  - ✅ **This closes the class at ANY cap and at ANY board size**, it is **cheaper in characters than the row it replaces** (a name is ~8 chars; a full roster row is ~46), and — decisively — **it makes Zone A's refusal rule TRUE again**, because a name the model can see is a name it can check `[FORCES]` membership against. ⚠️ **The grammar has ALWAYS admitted every collapsed kind** (`GetUnitKinds()` is never truncated), so before this change the sampler could name a unit the prompt had not shown it. **That gap is what is actually being closed.**
  - ⚖️ **JONATHAN'S RULING 1 SHIPS AS HE GAVE IT AND IS NOT SUBSTITUTED FOR.** The cap goes to 13. **This is an ADDITIONAL repair he was not offered because it had not been found** — the two compose, and together they mean the token `sorcerer` is in the prompt **whether or not the trimmer bites.**
  - ✅ **`t0` IS UNAFFECTED BY THE FORMAT CHANGE:** at 13 kinds on a 13-kind board **nothing collapses**, so both lanes still print `other_kinds: none`, byte-identically. **The new format is only reachable on a board this project has never measured.**
- ⛔ **THE THREE LEGS ARE ALL REQUIRED AND ARE BOARDED SEPARATELY SO A PARTIAL LANDING IS VISIBLE:** the cap (**his ruling**) · the `other_kinds:` names (**the root cause**) · Zone A's `who:"all"` rule (**the behaviour he actually complained about**). ⚠️ **A handoff that lands one and reports the defect fixed has not measured it.**

#### 20.3 ⚠️ NAMED, BOARDED RISK — **THE 6-CHARACTER HEADROOM** (`MaxRosterKinds = 13`)

|---|---|
| **Risk** | At 13 kinds Zone C's roster measures **~887 chars against a ~893-char budget**. ⇒ **~6 chars of headroom.** A **14th commandable unit kind**, a longer `pending:` line, or a longer typed `order:` re-collapses the tail. |
| **Owner-accepted** | ✅ **Jonathan was told this number and accepted it**, including that *"a future unit kind forces a re-tune."* ⛔ **This is not an open question and is not re-escalated.** |

| **The one honest lever** | **`ZoneBCharReserve = 192` is a documented ~124-char OVER-CHARGE** (measured Zone B readings: 68 / 71). **Lowering it can only WIDEN the roster and is safe in the only direction it will ever move** — it buys **~20× the current headroom.** |

### 4. 🔒 THE TWO PRE-REGISTERED STOPS + THE THREE DECISION RULES — **WRITTEN BEFORE M1 RUNS**

- ⛔ **STOP 1 — WIRE FORMAT.** If `chat=0` is **materially below** `chat=1`: **fix the runtime wire format, re-measure, re-ask.** ⛔ **Training is NOT AUTHORISED until the shipped lane has been measured at its own best.**
- ⛔ **STOP 2 — ROSTER SEAM.** If M3's artifact diff fails on the roster block: **resolve D2 first.** Every training prompt would otherwise carry a roster block **the game never emits**, and the sealed holdout would be scoring a board shape **that does not ship.**
- **M2 ≈ M1 within M0's band** ⇒ the gap is **capability**; the mix is class-driven from M5's taxonomy.
- **M2 materially worse than M1** ⇒ the gap is **distribution**; the mix is voice-heavy. Fine-tuning very likely works.
- ⛔ **M2 already ≥ 13/15-equivalent on the shipped shape** ⇒ **DO NOT TRAIN.** Re-run the gate arithmetic — the feature may already pass once the wire format is honest.
- ⚠️ **"MATERIALLY" IS DEFINED BY M0, NOT BY JUDGEMENT.** M0's determinism probe prints the instrument's **noise floor as a number**; a difference inside that band is not a difference. ⛔ **A stop evaluated before M0 has a number has no denominator.**

**⛔⛔ THE STOP-1 FALSE NEGATIVE — FOUND BY TASK-477 (2026-08-03), AND IT IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL DEFECT THIS BATCH HAS TURNED UP. IT WOULD HAVE READ AS GOOD NEWS.**

> ### ⛔ **`BuildPrompt` FALLS BACK TO RAW CONCATENATION *SILENTLY* WHEN THE LOADED GGUF CARRIES NO CHAT TEMPLATE. THE APPLY-*FAILED* PATH WARNS; THE NO-TEMPLATE PATH DOES NOT.**

- ⛔ **⇒ A `chat=1` RUN CAN PRODUCE RAW BYTES.** A secretly **raw-vs-raw** A/B measures **zero difference** and reads as ***"D1 does not exist"*** ⇒ **STOP 1 closes, the batch concludes the wire format is not the problem, and weeks go into QLoRA to fix something a template would have fixed.**
- ⚠️ **NAME THE PROPERTY THAT MAKES THIS CLASS SO DANGEROUS: THE FAILURE IS INVISIBLE *AND IT POINTS THE WRONG WAY*.** A silent failure that produced an alarming number would be caught by the alarm. **This one produces the single most reassuring result available** — the two lanes agree — **and reassurance is not audited.** ⇒ ⚖️ **A NEGATIVE RESULT FROM AN INSTRUMENT WHOSE FAILURE MODE *PRODUCES* NEGATIVE RESULTS IS NOT EVIDENCE.**
- ✅ **THE GUARD, AND IT IS MEASURED OFF THE PRODUCED BYTES RATHER THAN OFF THE REQUEST: `wire=raw|chat` IS PRINTED FROM A POSITIVE STRUCTURAL FACT — `FullPrompt.StartsWith(ZoneA)`** — because **both raw branches put Zone A at offset 0 and a template CANNOT** — **plus a WARNING when `chat=1` came out raw.** ⚖️ **That is a fact about the artifact, not a readback of the flag that was asked for, which is the whole distinction §17 and the relayed-diagnosis law keep re-teaching.**
- ⛔ **BINDING ON M1: THE WIRE READING IS TAKEN ON `SpikePrompt` *FIRST* AND QUOTED BESIDE THE A/B. A `chat=1` run that prints `wire=raw` INVALIDATES THE A/B — it is not a result, it is a broken instrument.**
- ✅ **AND THE PLACEMENT REFUSAL IS RATIFIED: the indicator was deliberately NOT put on `SpikeEval`'s default path**, on the stated ground that ***a new line on the default path moves the instrument every number on record was taken with*** (§16's frozen-default rule). **The refusal was written into `SpikeEval`'s own help text**, where the next operator meets it. ⚖️ **Declining to add a safety print to a frozen path, and documenting why AT the path, is the correct resolution of two rules that genuinely conflict.**

**✅ AND THE QUESTION THE SPEC DEMANDED WAS ANSWERED — IT SHARPENS BOTH STOPS AND IT IS BOARDED AS LAW:**
> ⚖️ **THE ASSEMBLY *RULE* IS BYTE-IDENTICAL; THE RESULTING *BYTES* ARE NOT, AND CANNOT BE.**
- `ComposeTurnPrompt` and `BuildPrompt`'s raw branch **agree on every degree of freedom** — same three parts, **A→B→C order, no separator, no roles, no trailing newline.** ⇒ ⛔ **THE ENTIRE RESIDUAL IS THE ZONE BUILDERS** (the 3029-vs-5116 Zone-A divergence, and D2's roster collapse) — **which is M3's territory, not this flag's.**

### 6. ⛔ WHY `Tools/LlmFinetune/` IS A SIBLING PROJECT AND NOT A FOLDER IN `ArtPipeline`

`Tools/ArtPipeline/` pins 3.12 for `gradio_client`; adding **~4 GB of torch wheels couples two unrelated lanes' dependency resolution**, and a resolver conflict would take the art lane down with the training lane. **Python 3.12 here for an INDEPENDENT reason:** wheel coverage for `bitsandbytes` / torch-cu128 is best on 3.11–3.12 and **system 3.14 has effectively none.** ⚠️ **Write that reason in the `pyproject.toml` header, exactly as `ArtPipeline/pyproject.toml` already does** — two projects pinning the same version for different reasons will otherwise be "helpfully" merged by a later reader.

- **PINS (floors; `uv.lock` is the truth and the handoff records the RESOLVED versions):** `torch >=2.8,<3.0` **from the cu128 index** (⚠️ the RTX 5070 is Blackwell `sm_120` — **pre-2.7 wheels have no kernels for it**) · `bitsandbytes >=0.47` · `transformers >=4.56,<5` · `peft >=0.17` · `trl >=0.24` · `datasets >=4.0` · `accelerate >=1.10` · `safetensors >=0.6`.
- ⛔ **NOT INSTALLED, DELIBERATELY — recorded so nobody adds them as a "fix":** `flash-attn` and `xformers` (**no Windows wheels** — use `attn_implementation="sdpa"`) · `unsloth` (**held as a VRAM lever, not a first-pass dep**) · **no CUDA Toolkit** (the wheels bundle the runtime; this is also §6-boundary-3 of the CUDA amendment).
- **GGUF TOOLCHAIN — PINNED, WITHOUT VENDORING A SECOND COPY.** `llama-quantize.exe` comes from **re-fetching the SAME release zip** `llama-b10235-bin-win-vulkan-x64.zip`, verified against the sha256 **already recorded in `Plugins/SiegeLlama/Source/ThirdParty/LlamaCpp/VERSION.md`**, extracted whole into `Cache/`. ⛔ **The exes were deliberately excluded from `bin/Win64/` at vendoring time — DO NOT put them back.** `convert_hf_to_gguf.py` / `convert_lora_to_gguf.py` come from a llama.cpp clone in `Cache/` at commit **`221f0f6356efe2260023208365705ec5d5a7c8f5`**, the SHA already in `VERSION.md`.
  - ⛔ **WHY THE PIN MATTERS, AND IT GOES IN THE README OR SOMEBODY WILL HELPFULLY UPGRADE IT: CONVERTER/RUNTIME SKEW PRODUCES A GGUF THAT LOADS AND IS SUBTLY WRONG.** Both ends pinned to `221f0f63` eliminates the class. **A commit SHA pins the whole tree; nothing new needs provenancing.**
- **BASE WEIGHTS:** `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` **safetensors** — ⚠️ **a DIFFERENT repo id from the GGUF repo, and it needs its OWN licence verification** (§7's *"a permissive base does not guarantee a permissive re-upload"*, applied in the other direction). Fetch with **`Tools/fetch_llm_model.py` UNCHANGED.**
- **`finetune_env.py --check` mirrors the convention `Tools/fetch_llm_model.py` already set** — every failure **printed rather than raised**, token never printed, ends `CHECK_VERDICT: PASS|FAIL`. ⛔ **The VRAM floor REFUSES; it does not warn** — **a deliberate contrast with the tier selector, which picks a tier it cannot run in.** ⛔ **A real `bnb.nn.Linear4bit` FORWARD on CUDA is run — import success is not function (§32).** `huggingface.co` reachability is probed **BARE** — ⛔ **do NOT reintroduce `SSL_CERT_FILE`; the Norton HF exclusions are live and proven.**

### 7. ⛔ DATA LAW — THE FOUR RULES THAT ARE NOT NEGOTIABLE

1. ⛔ **DO NOT TRAIN ON `Docs/Data/assistant_eval_dev.csv`.** 25 rows is **3 % of an 800-row set** and it is **the only corpus with three waves of comparable history.** ⇒ **It is the REGRESSION INSTRUMENT.** ⚠️ **Catastrophic forgetting is the number-one QLoRA failure mode and it is INVISIBLE in the holdout number** — the holdout only reports what you gained.
2. ⛔ **BURNED ROWS STAY BURNED.** The five spent gen-1 rows and **the retired collision noun** are **CLASS signal, never STRING signal** (§12b) — ⚠️ **and a fine-tune is a FAR more efficient memoriser than a prompt, so this is stricter here than it was there.** QA verifies by **literal match plus near-paraphrase over the whole training set** and issues an **ABSENCE CERTIFICATE ONLY, never a recommendation** (§12b's certificate/recommendation split, which worked and is reused verbatim).
3. ⛔ **§11's AUTHORSHIP SEPARATION IS STRUCTURAL AND EXTENDS TO THE TUNER.** **The corpus author is not the tuner. The tuner NEVER opens `assistant_voice_raw.txt`, `holdout2`, or `holdout3`.** Two dispatches, two contexts — not an honour system.
4. ⛔ **THE GOLD FILE GETS A DIFFERENT HEADER *AND* A SUBDIRECTORY, AND THE REASON IS A MEASURED HAZARD:** `LoadCorpus` only **WARNS** on a header mismatch, so a gold file sitting beside `assistant_eval_dev.csv` is **one tab-completion away from being passed as `dev=`** and silently scored. ⇒ `Docs/Data/Finetune/`, different header. 📌 **RECOMMENDED, NOT YET RULED: make that header mismatch FATAL** — boarded as its own item so it is a decision, not a side effect.

- **GOLD AUTHORING IS FOUR STAGES AND THE CORPORA CARRY *ASSERTIONS*, NOT ANSWERS:** **render** (via `SpikePrompt out=` — ⛔ **Python NEVER assembles a prompt**, T1) → **propose** (open permissive teacher, generating **under the GBNF** so every draft is well-formed) → **adjudicate** (⛔ **Jonathan reviews 100 % of refuse/clarify; 20 % sample of Execute**) → **validate mechanically** (GBNF-accepted **for that fixture**; every kind in the **PRINTED** roster; canonical `all`/`none` encoding).
- **COMPOSITION — ~800 examples:** single-kind Execute ~28 % · multi-kind ~14 % · army-wide zero-arg ~10 % · deferred/trigger ~8 % · **Refuse ~18 %** · **Clarify ~17 %** · hard negatives ~5 %. **Refuse+Clarify get ~35 % rather than the deployment distribution because the eval is adversarial by requirement (§11) and gen-1 failed exactly there.**
- ⛔⚠️ **AND THERE IS A CEILING, AND IT IS A SCORING QUIRK — THE SAME PROHIBITION ZONE A CARRIES NOW BINDS THE TRAINING SET.** The scorer **skips asserted fields when a question is emitted**, so a model that learns *"when unsure, ask"* converts **STRICT passes into LENIENT-only ones.** Zone A's own comments forbid writing that **disposition** into the prompt for exactly this reason. ⇒ ⛔ **TEACH TWO NAMED SITUATIONS, NEVER A DISPOSITION.** **Watch `clarify_rows_passed_by_question` and the printed `LENIENCY FLOOR` at EVERY checkpoint** — a rising holdout number with a rising floor is not progress (§12a: the split's own floor travels beside the number, every time).
- **BOARD VARIATION WITHOUT REWRITING ANSWERS:** every row carries an explicit **`depends_on`** set. Rows depending on nothing render against **any** fixture containing their kinds; **shortfall and deferred-trigger rows are PINNED to one fixture.** ⛔ **`tD` (kinds at `0 orderable`) and `tF` (2–4 kinds, early match) are BLOCKED until Stage A's per-fixture GBNF lands** — until then D3's class is unmeasurable **and untrainable.**

### 10. 🔒 THE GATE — CONJUNCTIVE, PRE-REGISTERED, SCORED ONCE

`SpikeEval holdout=Docs/Data/assistant_eval_holdout2.csv tier=full gpu=0 repeats=5`, **on the shipping GGUF, in the shipped wire format.** ⛔ **ALL NINE MUST HOLD:**

1. **≥ 13/15 lenient at the *MINIMUM* of 5 runs** — ⛔ **not median, never best.** Makes a ±1 noise band **harmless instead of exploitable.**
2. **`STRICT == LENIENT` in every run** — the anti-hedging clause.
3. **`PassLenient − DegenerateQuestionFloor ≥ 7`.** ⚠️ Gen-1 scored 66.7 % against a printed floor of 60 % — ***one row* of real translation signal.**
4. **`parse_failures = 0`, zero aborted rows, all 5 runs.**
5. ⛔ **ZERO REFUSE-CLASS FAILURES — A VETO, scored separately.** Protects the standing *"never spends my gold, never plays my cards"* ruling.
6. **NO REGRESSION on `assistant_eval_dev.csv`:** median ≥ 20/25, **and no row passing at baseline may fail in ≥3 of 5 runs.**
7. **PROMPT-SHAPE IDENTITY:** M3's artifact diff passes; `zoneA_chars=5116`.
8. **LATENCY within ~10 % of the measured `tier=full` wall clock.** ⚠️ **Buying accuracy with Jonathan's latency budget is HIS trade, not a tuning task's** (§12d).
9. ⛔ **THE SCORED ARTIFACT IS THE SHIPPED ARTIFACT**, declared in `Docs/ModelManifest.md` with its sha256.

- 🔒⛔ **`holdout2` OPENS EXACTLY ONCE, ON THE MERGED SHIPPING GGUF, WITH `repeats=5` *INSIDE THAT SINGLE OPENING*** (§12a + §12h). **N generations, same file, same session, reported as a distribution — NEVER a second opening on a later day.**
- ⛔ **SCORE THE ARTIFACT THAT SHIPS.** ⚠️ **Runtime-LoRA-on-Q4 and merged-then-Q4 are DIFFERENT MODELS** — the adapter was trained to correct an **NF4** base and is being merged into **bf16** then re-quantised to **a different scheme.** ✅ **Dev may be scored on the adapter freely; the holdout opens only on the merged, quantised shipping GGUF.** **This is T8 and it is the project's exact recurring failure: a confident green describing something else.**
- ⛔ **NEVER REPORT THE RESULT AS A DELTA FROM 66.7 %** — generations are **not row-comparable** (§12a). **The bar is ABSOLUTE.**
- ⛔ **PRE-REGISTER THE FALSIFYING CONDITION BEFORE THE RUN**, in the handoff (§12f's method result, now standing law on this lane): ***"if refuse-class rows still fail, the defect is POLICY ROUTING and more data of the same kind will not fix it."***
- **RE-RUN AFTER ANY WEIGHT CHANGE:** bars #1–#5 (⛔ **bar #1 in PIE on `L_Arena` WITH UNITS ON THE FIELD, never an empty map**), the **33 automation tests**, and the **`bThrottleCPUWhenNotForeground=False` check** (§12e — a headless-driven PIE session idles at **exactly 3.0 FPS** with the throttle on, and **a bar taken under it is meaningless rather than conservative**).
- ⛔ **TIER CONSTANTS ARE RE-MEASURED, NEVER CARRIED** (`SPIKE_MEM stage=model_load`, all three tiers, twice, **worse reading wins**) — T9, and a carried constant silently eats the 768 MiB game reserve.
- ⛔ **TOKEN COUNTS MUST REPRODUCE IDENTICALLY. A LoRA DOES NOT TOUCH THE TOKENIZER** ⇒ **any movement means the vocab was touched and §8/§10's ENTIRE numeric apparatus is void.**

**⚖️ TWO INSTRUMENT LAWS, RATIFIED 2026-08-03 FROM TASK-476's OWN RESTRAINT — BOTH PROPOSED BY THE IMPLEMENTER, NEITHER ASKED FOR, AND BOTH NOW BINDING ON EVERY HARNESS IN THIS LANE:**

- ⛔ **(A) NO INSTRUMENT MAY PRINT A VERDICT ON A GATE IT CAN ONLY PARTIALLY SEE.** §10's gate is **conjunctive over NINE clauses**; `SpikeEval` can observe **four**. ⇒ **It prints statistics and prints NO PASS/FAIL.** ⚖️ **A harness emitting a green would become a FIFTH LANE claiming authority it does not have** — and this batch exists because three lanes already disagreed. ⚠️ **The failure this prevents is specific and it is the project's recurring one: a confident green describing something else.** ✅ **The party best placed to emit the verdict refusing to is what makes the verdict meaningful when it finally comes.**
- ⛔ **(B) EVERY PRINTED STATISTIC CARRIES THE GATE CLAUSE THAT READS IT.** `SpikeEval` labels **MINIMUM → §10 #1**, **MEDIAN → §10 #6**, and states that **nothing reads MAX** — with the **leniency floor travelling beside the number** (§12a). ⚖️ **THIS KILLS "QUOTE THE FLATTERING ONE" AT THE SOURCE**, which is otherwise unfalsifiable after the fact: three aggregations of one run are all true, and only one of them is the gate. ⛔ **An unlabelled aggregate is an invitation, and a printed `max` with no reader is a trap with a number in it.**
- ⛔ **(C) THE ENCODING PIN — EVERY BYTE-COMPARED ARTIFACT IS WRITTEN AS EXPLICIT UTF-8 WITHOUT BOM. RAISED FROM TWO FIXES TO A RULE 2026-08-03 UNDER §13(d)'s SWEEP DUTY, AFTER TASK-479 AND TASK-477 FOUND IT ***INDEPENDENTLY, THE SAME EVENING***.**
  - ⛔ **`FFileHelper::SaveStringToFile`'s `AutoDetect` DEFAULT MAKES THE FILE'S ENCODING DEPEND ON ITS CONTENT** — it writes **UTF-16-with-BOM on the first non-ASCII character.** ⚠️ **So the artifact's encoding changes based on which utterance was dumped.**
  - ⚠️ **THE FAILURE, IN ITS OWN WORDS: *"a file that opens fine, has a plausible length, and hashes to something no consumer can reproduce."*** ⇒ **It is intermittent, content-dependent, and it corrupts a HASH rather than a value** — so it survives every eyeball check and fails only the comparison it exists to serve.
  - ⚖️ **AN INSTRUMENT WHOSE OUTPUT ENCODING VARIES WITH ITS INPUT IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT.** ⇒ **`ForceUTF8WithoutBOM`, or an explicit byte array — unconditionally, on every `out=`, dump, gold file and JSONL this batch writes.** ⛔ **This binds Stage D's `build_dataset.py` too: Python's default encoding on Windows is not UTF-8, and the same trap has a Python spelling.**
  - 📌 **TWO INDEPENDENT SIGHTINGS IN ONE EVENING IS THE SWEEP DUTY FIRING EXACTLY AS INTENDED** — ⚖️ **the second sighting is what converts "a careful agent handled it" into "the class is closed", and it is the difference between two correct fixes and one rule.**
- 📌 **AND THE PROOF STANDARD TASK-476 SET IS THE STANDARD FOR THE REST OF STAGE A — MECHANICAL, NOT EYEBALLED:** *8/8 old format strings reduce **character-identically**, 0 orphaned, new lines on a **separate log stream**, 103/103 `UE_LOG` calls arg-count-clean **with 83 untouched lines used as the positive control for the checker itself**.* ⚖️ **A checker that has not been shown to FAIL on a known-bad input has not been shown to work** (§14's positive-control discipline, applied to a bespoke tool). ⚠️ **AND IT DECLARED ITS OWN LIMIT: that is a proof about SOURCE BYTES, not about a RUN.** ⛔ **§16's INSTRUMENT-UNCHANGED proof — the dev-split number reproducing at 20/25 with the same five failing rows — is still owed, and it is TASK-481's.** ✅ **Stating the boundary of a proof is part of giving it.**

### 11. ⚖️ THE RECIPE'S FROZEN SWITCHES — EACH ONE SILENTLY BREAKS THE CONVERTER OR THE SCALE

- `max_seq_len = 2048` — ⚠️ **Zone A is 1362 tokens (5116 chars), NOT the pre-ladder 1139**; a sample is ~1767 tokens. **NF4 4-bit base, `bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=bfloat16`, double-quant.**
- `LoraConfig(r=16, alpha=32, dropout=0.05, target_modules=[q,k,v,o,gate,up,down])`.
- ⛔ **`use_dora=False`, `use_rslora=False`, `modules_to_save` EMPTY.** **Each silently breaks `convert_lora_to_gguf.py` or the scale it writes** — ⚠️ **rsLoRA uses `alpha/√r`; llama.cpp computes `alpha/r`.** (T4.)
- ⛔ **COMPLETION-ONLY LOSS.** The model **already emits format correctly** (`parse_failures = 0`, `STRICT == LENIENT`) — **teaching format again wastes capacity on the one thing that is not broken.**
- **Seed pinned. Every run writes `Runs/<id>/run.json`** with resolved versions, base revision sha, dataset sha256, hyperparameters **and the free-VRAM reading at start.**
- ⚠️ **DOES IT FIT IN 8 GB? DERIVED, NOT MEASURED:** ~5.6–6.9 GB against ~7.3–7.7 GB free **with the editor closed.** ⛔ **The margin is ONE TERM WIDE AND THAT TERM IS THE LOGITS** — a **151,936** vocabulary makes a 4B behave like a much larger model at train time (T5).
- **LEVERS IN COST ORDER, ONE AT A TIME, RE-MEASURING AFTER EACH:** alloc-conf `expandable_segments` → **fused/chunked cross-entropy (~1.0–1.8 GB, the highest-yield lever)** → `r=8` attention-only → `unsloth` → rent a GPU for one run.
- ⛔ **NEVER SHORTEN ZONE A IN TRAINING ONLY — THAT IS TRAIN/SERVE SKEW, THE EXACT DEFECT §12a EXISTS ABOUT.**
- **ADAPTER FOR ITERATION, MERGED FOR SHIP.** Iterate with a ~66 MB adapter GGUF (**the base stays byte-identical, so everything measured about the base still describes it**). Ship **merged → bf16 → convert → re-quantise to Q4_K_M**: **zero code changes** (the override chain was built so *"swapping models never needs a rebuild"*), zero adapter VRAM accounting, **and no per-token adapter matmul at decode — which matters because bar #2 already FAILS on partial and cpu, and decode is the whole cost (§12d).**

### 12. ⛔ THE TWO CONTRACTS THAT MUST BE RULED **BEFORE** AUTHORING, NOT INFERRED AFTER — **THEY ARE JONATHAN'S**

1. ⛔ **WHAT `send everyone` EMITS.** ⚠️ **`DEV-13`'s own note says a task was meant to declare it and none did.** Until it is ruled, ~10 % of the training mix (army-wide zero-arg) is being authored against an undeclared contract.
2. ⛔ **THE ASK-CODE TAXONOMY.** **The corpora accept ANY OF FIVE codes**, so **the training set is where that policy is actually decided** — by 800 rows, silently, if nobody rules it. ⚠️ **A policy decided by a data-drafting pass is a policy nobody chose.**

⚖️ **BOTH ARE RECORDED HERE AS *OPEN*, NOT GUESSED AT.** ⛔ **An agent that picks one and proceeds has made a product decision inside a data task** — exactly the shape §12f's *"the corpus author is not the tuner"* separation exists to prevent, one level up.

### 12b. ⛔ THE CITATION-DISAMBIGUATION RULE — "§11" RESOLVES TO TWO DIFFERENT SECTIONS AND BOTH ARE CITED IN THIS BATCH (2026-08-03, TASK-500)

> ### ⛔ **A BARE `§N` IS AMBIGUOUS IN THIS FILE. EVERY CITATION NAMES ITS SECTION: `"In-match LLM command assistant" §11` OR `"THE FINE-TUNE RUNG" §11`.**

- ⚠️ **MEASURED, IN THIS BATCH'S OWN BOARD: TASK-482 / TASK-484 / TASK-487 cite the ASSISTANT's §11 (the sealed-corpus authorship law); TASK-495 cites the FINE-TUNE RUNG's §11 (the frozen recipe switches). Same prefix, unrelated content, both correct in context and both unreadable out of it.**
- ⚖️ **THIS IS A CITATION COLLISION INSIDE A BATCH WHOSE ENTIRE THESIS IS *DOCUMENTS ASSERTING THINGS NOBODY CHECKED*** — and the failure mode is the worst kind: **the reader follows the reference, finds a real clause, and obeys the wrong law with no error anywhere.**
- ✅ **THE FIX IS A RULE, NOT A RENUMBER.** ⛔ **Do NOT renumber either section** — every existing handoff, QA report and commit message already cites the old numbers, and renumbering breaks *those* silently to fix *this*. **Qualify at the point of citation instead.**

### 14. ⚖️ THREE RULINGS FROM STAGE A's CLOSE (2026-08-03, TASK-478) — the falsified-assertion carve, the deferral-reason law, and the belt-to-only-strap clause

**⛔ (a) THE FALSIFIED-ASSERTION CARVE — §22 BEATS SINGLE-OWNER-PER-FILE, NARROWLY, AND TASK-478 WAS RIGHT NOT TO TAKE IT SILENTLY.**
TASK-478 rewrote **two pre-existing `UE_LOG` strings** that asserted the mechanism it had just deleted — **one of them inside TASK-477's `CmdSpikePrompt`** — and **flagged it as a scope call rather than assuming the duty overrode the ownership rule.** ✅ **Flagging was correct; the ruling is that §22 wins.**
- ⚖️ **THE PRINCIPLE, AND IT IS NARROWER THAN "SHARED FILES ARE FINE": SINGLE-OWNER-PER-FILE GOVERNS *CONCURRENT AUTHORSHIP*, NOT *TRUTH MAINTENANCE OF STATEMENTS YOUR OWN CHANGE FALSIFIED*.** ⛔ **A log line asserting a mechanism you just removed is PART OF THAT REMOVAL, not a separate edit** — and leaving it for the file's next owner **ships a runtime string that lies**, which §22 names the priority surface precisely because a log is read at 3am by someone with no context.
- ⛔ **THE FOUR CONDITIONS — outside them, single-owner wins and the finding is ROUTED, not fixed:**
  1. **The string must assert something THIS task's own change made false.** ⛔ *"While I was in there"* is not this clause.
  2. **Text only. ⛔ No control flow, no verbosity change, no format-arg change** (the `UE_LOG` arg-count class is a compile break, and it is not yours to risk in another owner's function).
  3. **DECLARED IN THE HANDOFF, each string named with its owning task**, so the other owner learns it from the record rather than from a merge.
  4. **The other owner is not blocked on it** — ⛔ if the fix requires their in-flight work, ROUTE IT.
- ⚖️ **THIS IS THE *"the conclusion is still true and only the cited mechanism is gone"* SHAPE ALREADY ON THE BOOKS, APPLIED TO A RUNTIME STRING INSTEAD OF A DOCUMENT.** ⚠️ **A stale comment misleads a reader; a stale log misleads an OPERATOR MID-INCIDENT, holding the wrong mental model of a live system.**

**⛔ (b) THE DEFERRAL-REASON LAW — A DEFERRAL CARRIES A REASON, AND THE REASON IS CHECKABLE.**
> ### ⛔ **A WRONG REASON ATTACHED TO A RIGHT DECISION IS HOW THE NEXT READER JUSTIFIES A WRONG ONE.**
- **MEASURED, THIS EVENING, n = 3:** two tasks deferred on reasons that survived inspection; **one (TASK-477, on the `prompt=<path>` defect) deferred on a reason that did NOT** — TASK-478 verified against `ResolveZoneAText` that the fix is **provably default-identical**, so *"it would risk the default path"* was false. ✅ **THE DEFERRAL ITSELF WAS STILL CORRECT** (single-owner, and TASK-501 now owns it) — **but for a different reason than the one written down.**
- ⛔ **SO THE RECORD IS CORRECTED, NOT THE OUTCOME.** ⚠️ **A right call resting on a false premise is indistinguishable, to the next reader, from a right call — until they reuse the premise.** ⇒ **Whoever falsifies a deferral's stated reason says so plainly, even when the deferral stands.**
- ⚖️ **AND IT IS THE SAME DISEASE AS §12f's ACCIDENTALLY-RIGHT `78 %`: an agreement that vindicates a CONCLUSION does not vindicate the METHOD that produced it, and the method is what gets reused.**

**✅ (c) THE BELT-TO-ONLY-STRAP CLAUSE — A CHANGE THAT QUIETLY PROMOTES AN EXISTING CHECK MUST SAY SO.**
Deriving the GBNF per-fixture makes **`VerifyFixtureKindParity` MORE load-bearing, not vestigial** — the opposite of the intuition, and worth a clause because the intuition is what a reviewer arrives with.
- **BEFORE:** a typo'd fixture kind was a symbol **the sampler forbade** ⇒ the grammar itself rejected it ⇒ **LOUD.**
- **AFTER:** a typo'd fixture kind is **added as a legal alternative** ⇒ the model can emit a kind that does not exist ⇒ **SILENT.**
- ⇒ ⛔ **`SpikeRoster` IS NO LONGER THE GRAMMAR AUTHORITY — ONLY THE VOCABULARY AUTHORITY — AND `VerifyFixtureKindParity` IS NOW THE WHOLE OF THE GUARANTEE.** ⚠️ **Any future task that "simplifies" or relaxes that check is removing the only remaining strap, and must be failed on sight citing this clause.**
- ✅ **AND THE STRUCTURAL TOUCH TO COPY: the fixture was threaded with NO DEFAULT ARGUMENT, so a missed call site is a COMPILE ERROR rather than a silent wrong grammar.** ⚖️ **That is the §17 family — tools and code that fail quietly — answered by CONSTRUCTION instead of by discipline, which is the only answer that survives a tired author.**

**⛔ (d) STAGE A IS COMPLETE *AS SPECIFIED*, NOT *AS MEASURED* — SAID IN THE IMPLEMENTER'S OWN WORDS AND KEPT.** **Not one line has been compiled or executed.** §16's **instrument-unchanged** re-run is **TASK-481's**, and **three named gaps survive into it:** the `prompt=` bypass (**TASK-501**) · **no `wire=` indicator on `SpikeEval`** (deliberate — §16's frozen default) · ⛔ **D2 remains INEXPRESSIBLE by the spike at all** (§3's `other_kinds:` constant). ⚖️ **A completion claim that names its own three gaps is the kind this pipeline accepts; one that does not is the kind it has been burned by.**

### KBD-§0. ⚖️ JONATHAN'S TWO RULINGS — DECIDED, BINDING, ⛔ NOT RE-OPENABLE BY ANY AGENT

Both answered by Jonathan directly via AskUserQuestion on 2026-08-04. Recorded here because the *"shouldn't this be a setting?"* question is the single most likely thing a future agent proposes.

1. ⛔ **ALWAYS-ON AUTO-DETECT. NO PLAYER-FACING SETTING.** ⛔ **No new field in `USiegeSettingsSaveGame`, no row in `USettingsMenuWidget`, no `SC-§8` registry addition.** A **CVar for runtime testing is permitted** (`KBD-§7`); a settings toggle is **out of scope and is a scope breach if added.** ⚖️ The remap is a *correctness* fix — the keys go where they are printed on a QWERTY reference — not a preference.
2. ⛔ **MID-SESSION LAYOUT SWITCHES ARE IN SCOPE, NOT DEFERRED.** Jonathan may `Win+Space` to QWERTY for gaming and back. **The 1 Hz HKL poll AND the `OnApplicationActivationStateChanged` hook both ship in this batch.** ⚠️ A design that only probes at `Initialize` does not satisfy the directive and is incomplete, not "phase 1".

### KBD-§1. ⛔ THE CENTRAL LAW — AND IT IS THE ONE THAT DESTROYS THIS FEATURE IF BROKEN

> ### ⛔ **THE POSITIONAL REMAP NEVER WRITES TO `IMC_Hero.uasset`. IT WRITES ONLY THE `.Key` FIELD OF A TRANSIENT `DuplicateObject` COPY — ⛔ NEVER `Modifiers`, ⛔ NEVER `Triggers`, ⛔ NEVER THE MAPPINGS ARRAY ITSELF.**

- ⚠️ **THE PRECEDENT IS THIS REPO'S OWN AND IT ALREADY COST A PLAYTEST — `.claude/pipeline/handoffs/TASK-445-artist.md:95-105`: rewriting the mappings array SILENTLY DEFAULT-CONSTRUCTED the instanced `SwizzleAxis`/`Negate` modifiers. WASD broke and mouse-look inverted — WHILE THE PROPERTY TABLE STILL READ CORRECT.** ⛔ That last clause is the whole reason this is a law and not a code comment: **the readback passed.** It is the project's named failure class (`SC-§17`) wearing an input asset's clothes.
- ✅ **THE STRUCTURAL FORM OF THE FIX — copy it, do not merely obey it:** every value written is **re-derived from the pristine `Source` array BY INDEX**, and the only field ever assigned is `.Key`. ⇒ **The TASK-445 failure mode is ABSENT BY CONSTRUCTION, not dodged by care** (`AS-§17`'s standing preference: a hazard closed by choosing a different shape does not reopen when somebody is tired).
  ```cpp
  const TArray<FEnhancedActionKeyMapping>& Src = Source->GetMappings();
  for (int32 i = 0; i < Src.Num(); ++i)
  {
      const FKey* T = Translation.Find(Src[i].Key);
      Target->GetMapping(i).Key = T ? *T : Src[i].Key;   // ONLY .Key. Ever.
  }
  ```
- ⚠️ **RE-DERIVING FROM `Source` IS ALSO WHAT MAKES THE SUBSTITUTION SIMULTANEOUS.** On Dvorak the map holds **`D→E` AND `E→Period`** — reading the *target* would cascade `D→E→Period`. **This sentence belongs in the header comment**, because the bug it prevents is invisible in review and looks like a model failure at playtest.
- ⛔ **REVIEWABLE INVARIANT, AND IT IS THE CHEAPEST CHECK IN THE GATE: the source asset is only ever held through `const` pointers. THE ONLY NON-CONST `UInputMappingContext*` IN THE ENTIRE FEATURE IS THE DUPLICATE.** `AddMappingContext` takes `const UInputMappingContext*` (`EnhancedInputSubsystemInterface.h:265`), so **no cast is needed** — a cast appearing here is itself the finding. ⚠️ In PIE the source **is** the editor's loaded asset; read-only access is what makes PIE structurally unable to dirty it.

- ⛔ **FOUR CONDITIONS. EACH IS AN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, ⛔ NOT ADVICE:**
  1. ⛔ **The call lives in a SCRATCHPAD authoring script. ⛔ NEVER in `Source/`.** A `MapKey` in a `.cpp` is still a `KBD-§2` violation and QA still fails it.
  2. ⛔ **ONE call, ONE appended row. ⛔ `UnmapKey` / `UnmapAllKeysFromAction` / `UnmapAll` STAY BANNED IN EVERY LANE** — they exist only to enable the round-trip. **Their presence in the script is a STOP.**
  3. ⛔⛔ **PROVE THE SURVIVORS BY NAMING THE MODIFIER OBJECTS, ⛔ NOT THE KEYS.** ⚖️ **TASK-445's whole signature is *"the property table still reads correct"*, so a key-list readback is precisely the instrument the defect defeats.** **Required: count `N → N+1` where `N` is the count MEASURED IN THE ASSET IMMEDIATELY BEFORE THE APPEND; the first `N` keys identical IN ARRAY ORDER; and `IA_Move`'s four rows still carrying `InputModifierSwizzleAxis_0` / `SwizzleAxis_1` + `Negate_0` / `Negate_1`, and `IA_Look` still carrying `Negate_2`, BY NAME.**
     - ⚖️⚠️ **REPAIRED 2026-08-30 ON TASK-705's MEASUREMENT — THE LITERALS WERE STALE AND WOULD HAVE CAUSED A FALSE QA FAIL AGAINST A CORRECT APPEND.** ~~count `24 → 25`; the first 24 keys~~ was true when written (2026-08-15) and **went stale the moment `IA_WarMap`→`M` landed (TASK-568): the live count was `25 → 26`, and each future append moves it again.** ⇒ ⛔ **A reviewer checking the LITERAL `24` against a correct `25 → 26` append fails a good diff** — and *"the law says 24"* is an argument that beats a tired implementer who is, in fact, right. **The invariant was always RELATIVE; only its expression was absolute.**
     - ⭐ **THE GENERAL RULE THIS BUYS, AND IT IS THE POINT: ⛔ NEVER PIN A GROWING COUNT AS A LITERAL IN LAW.** A number that increments with normal work is a **scheduled false failure**. ✅ **Pin the INVARIANT (`N → N+1`, first `N` identical in order, named modifiers surviving) and require `N` to be MEASURED AT THE ASSET IN THE SAME SESSION AS THE APPEND** — which also makes the check strictly stronger, because it re-reads the truth instead of trusting a remembered one. ⚠️ **Same family as the M7.7 `Notes` drift (*"in 400"* vs `AoERadius` **700**) and `PKG-§9a-3`'s inert key: a stale literal is more dangerous than a missing one, because it is CONFIDENT.**
  4. ⛔ **The appended row carries EMPTY `Triggers` and EMPTY `Modifiers`** — matching the shipped `IA_AssistantConsole` row. ⭐ **Its emptiness is the SPECIFICATION, not a side effect. That is exactly why the append is safe and the round-trip is not.**
- ⛔ **THE ARRAY REWRITE STAYS FORBIDDEN, AND IT IS REACHABLE, WHICH IS WHY THE PROHIBITION IS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN THEORETICAL: `DefaultKeyMappings` is `UPROPERTY(config, BlueprintReadOnly, EditAnywhere)` (`InputMappingContext.h:100-101`)** ⇒ **MCP genuinely CAN write the whole struct.** ⛔ **It may not.**
- ⭐⭐ **THE 5.7 DEPRECATION, MEASURED BY TASK-568 AND ✅ CONFIRMED BY THE MANAGER AT THE HEADER — RECORDED SO NO FUTURE BATCH RE-DERIVES IT OR PANICS AT IT: `UInputMappingContext::Mappings` is `UE_DEPRECATED(5.7, "Use the DefaultKeyMappings struct instead.")` and reads `[]`; the live data is `DefaultKeyMappings.Mappings`** (`:93-95` vs `:100-101`). ✅ **`KBD-§` IS UNAFFECTED: `GetMappings()` and `GetMapping(i)` (`:219-220`) BOTH already return the new array** ⇒ **`USiegeKeyboardLayoutSubsystem`'s index-by-index `.Key`-only retarget of its transient duplicate works verbatim, and any APPENDED mapping is covered for free.** ⇒ ⭐ **A letter key added today inherits Dvorak support with ZERO code (`KBD-§4` puts all 26 letters in the table).**

### KBD-§3. ⛔ THE `UEnhancedInputUserSettings` / `MapPlayerKey` REJECTION — THREE INDEPENDENT REASONS, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT PROPOSED AGAIN

It is the API a competent reader reaches for first, which is exactly why the refusal is written down rather than left to be re-derived.

1. ⛔ **IT REQUIRES `PlayerMappableKeySettings` ON EVERY MAPPING** (`EnhancedInputUserSettings.cpp:1689-1695`) — i.e. **precisely the `IMC_Hero.uasset` edit `KBD-§1` forbids.**
2. ⛔ **AND THAT MEMBER CANNOT BE SUPPLIED AT RUNTIME EVEN IF ONE WANTED TO: it is `protected` with NO public setter** (`EnhancedActionKeyMapping.h:120-132`). ⇒ The asset edit is not a shortcut around the law; it is the **only** way in.
3. ⛔ **IT PERSISTS — `Saved/SaveGames/EnhancedInputUserSettings.sav` — AND IT WINS OVER IMC DEFAULTS.** ⚠️ **A layout-derived remap MUST NOT persist**: switch back to QWERTY and the player is left with stale Dvorak bindings, saved to disk, with no UI to clear them. ⚖️ This one is fatal on its own — the feature is *derived state*, and derived state that outlives its input is a bug generator.
- ✅ **IT REMAINS THE RIGHT HOME FOR A FUTURE REBIND SCREEN.** ⛔ **This is a rejection FOR THIS FEATURE, not a ban on the API** — a task that proposes it for player-authored rebinding is correct and must not be failed by citing this clause.

### KBD-§4. SCOPE LAW — ⛔ LETTERS ONLY, ALL 26, AND THE EXCLUSIONS ARE DELIBERATE

- ✅ **ALL 26 LETTERS `EKeys::A`..`EKeys::Z` ARE IN THE TABLE — not just the 10 the game binds today.** ⚖️ It is free, and it removes the *"update the table when you add a key"* footgun, which is the kind of debt that surfaces as a mystery input bug six months later.
- ⛔ **DELIBERATELY NOT REMAPPED: digits (the `1`–`6` hotkeys), punctuation, modifiers (`Shift`, `LeftAlt`, `Ctrl`), the mouse, `Space`, `Enter`, `Escape`.** ⚠️ **This is a design decision, not an omission** — Dvorak's number row is identical anyway, and positionally remapping digits would actively hurt AZERTY. **A task or QA finding that "the hotkeys weren't remapped" is WRONG and is answered by this clause.**

### KBD-§5. ⛔ THE FAIL-SAFE LAW — EVERY FAILURE MODE DEGRADES TO THE UNTRANSLATED SOURCE CONTEXT

> ### ⛔ **NEVER `nullptr`. NEVER `EKeys::Invalid`. NEVER A PARTIALLY-RETARGETED CONTEXT. THE WORST OUTCOME THIS FEATURE MAY PRODUCE IS *"THE GAME BEHAVES EXACTLY AS IT DID YESTERDAY."***

Every one of these degrades to the pristine `Source` context and logs — and **QA traces each early return individually** (`KBD-§9` criterion 6):

| failure | outcome |
|---|---|
| `Source == nullptr` | return `nullptr` (the caller's existing null-guard already covers it) |
| translation map empty (host is positionally QWERTY) | ⭐ return **`Source` — the SAME POINTER**, no duplicate, no allocation |
| `DuplicateObject` returns null | return `Source`, `UE_LOG(Error)` |
| `RetargetContextKeys` returns false (length mismatch / profile overrides present) | return `Source`, `UE_LOG(Error)`, ⛔ **and the duplicate is discarded, never handed out half-written** |
| probe yields `VirtualKey == 0`, or the resolver yields `EKeys::Invalid`, or two positions claim one target | that letter keeps its **source** key (identity); the map simply has no entry |
| non-Windows (`ProbeActiveLayout` returns 0 probes) | empty translation ⇒ pass-through, one `Log` line at `Initialize` |
| the subsystem itself unresolvable from `GetGameInstance()` | `AHeroCharacter` applies `HeroMappingContext` unchanged — **byte-identical to today's behaviour** |

- ⚠️ **`MappingProfileOverrides` IS THE NON-OBVIOUS ONE AND IT IS WHY `RetargetContextKeys` HAS A FALSE RETURN AT ALL:** profile overrides live in `MappingProfileOverrides` (`InputMappingContext.h:109-110`), **which `GetMapping()` CANNOT REACH.** ⇒ If `Source->GetProfilesWithOverridenMappings().Num() > 0` the retarget would be **silently partial** — so it refuses wholesale instead. ⚖️ *Refusing loudly beats retargeting half a context.*

### KBD-§6. ⛔ THE PROBE IS A WIN32 SCANCODE PROBE, AND THE ENGINE OFFERS NO SHORTCUT — RECORDED SO IT IS NOT "SIMPLIFIED"

- **UE 5.8 exposes NO layout-independent physical key.** `FKeyEvent::GetKeyCode()` (`SlateCore/Public/Input/Events.h:488`) *claims* to be a pre-conversion hardware code and **on Windows carries the layout-dependent VK**; the real scancode is consumed inside `WindowsApplication.cpp` (Shift disambiguation only) and **never propagated.**
- ⭐ **THE SEAM THAT MAKES THE TABLE CORRECT BY CONSTRUCTION: `ResolveKeyFromCodes` IS A THIN WRAPPER ON `FInputKeyManager::Get().GetKeyFromCodes` (`InputCoreTypes.h:857`, module `InputCore` — ⛔ ALREADY A PUBLIC DEPENDENCY, verified at `GitClaudeUnrealTest.Build.cs:15`).** Calling **the engine's own resolver with the same two numbers the message pump supplies** (`WindowsApplication.cpp:3248-3321` → `SlateApplication.cpp:4953-4957`) means the translation table **agrees with runtime by construction**, including on layouts nobody tested.
- ⛔ **DO NOT MASK THE DEAD-KEY BIT `0x80000000`** — `WindowsApplication.cpp:3317` does not, and the table must match runtime byte for byte.
- **`check(IsInGameThread())`** — `GetKeyboardLayout(0)` is per-thread. Non-negotiable.
- ⭐ **THE SELF-CHECK IS PART OF THE FEATURE, NOT A DEBUG EXTRA: on a US-QWERTY host `MapVirtualKeyEx(0x11, MAPVK_VSC_TO_VK_EX, hkl)` MUST return `'W'` (0x57).** ⚖️ **No scancode table exists anywhere in engine source to cross-check against, so that one assertion is the ONLY thing validating our hand-authored table against the OS.** Log it at `Initialize`.
- ✅ **NO `Build.cs` CHANGE. `ApplicationCore` IS NOT NEEDED.** Include `Windows/WindowsHWrapper.h` (what `InputCore/Private/Windows/WindowsPlatformInput.cpp:4` uses; it is in **Core**); `user32.lib` is a UBT default (`UEBuildWindows.cs:2093`). ⛔ **A `Build.cs` edit in this batch is a finding** — it means somebody reached for the wrong header.
- ⛔ **EVERY Win32 SYMBOL LIVES INSIDE `#if PLATFORM_WINDOWS`, CONFINED TO ONE STATIC FUNCTION IN THE `.cpp`.** The **header stays Win32-free** — the HKL is stored as an opaque `uint64`. Fence the poll timer and the activation hook the same way.
- **MID-SESSION SWITCH — WHY THERE ARE THREE MECHANISMS AND NOT ONE:** Windows fires `WM_INPUTLANGCHANGE` and Slate handles it (`SlateApplication.cpp:5138-5141` → `FInputKeyManager::InitKeyMappings()`), but ⛔ **`OnInputLanguageChanged` is a bare virtual with NO delegate — the whole Runtime tree was grepped, zero.** So: (1) re-probe on every `GetPositionalContext` call (free; covers a layout set before launch) · (2) `FSlateApplication::Get().OnApplicationActivationStateChanged()` (`SlateApplication.h:1690-1691`) — covers alt-tab-out/change/alt-tab-in, ⛔ **unbind in `Deinitialize`** · (3) the 1 Hz HKL poll — **the only thing that catches an in-place `Win+Space`.**
- ⭐ **RE-APPLY WITHOUT TOUCHING THE HERO:** on a change, retarget **the cached duplicate IN PLACE** (re-derived from the pristine source, so no compounding) and call `RequestRebuildControlMappingsUsingContext(Dup)`. ⇒ **The pointer `AHeroCharacter` handed to `AddMappingContext` never changes — ZERO new state and ZERO re-application code in `HeroCharacter`.** ⚖️ That property is the reason the hero edit is four lines, and a "refactor" that re-applies contexts from the subsystem throws it away.

### KBD-§7. NAMING + FOLDER LAW (the cross-task contract)

| thing | law |
|---|---|
| statics | **`FSiegeKeyboardLayoutStatics`** — `Source/GitClaudeUnrealTest/Siegebound/SiegeKeyboardLayoutStatics.{h,cpp}`. Plain static library, **not a UObject**, `GITCLAUDEUNREALTEST_API`. Precedent: `FSiegeCombatStatics` (`SiegeCombatStatics.h:23`). ⭐ **ALL pure, testable logic lives here.** |
