### WR-§7 ⛔ THE 30-GOLD ENEMY REVEAL — **A GAMEPLAY-ECONOMY CHANGE, NOT A UI FEATURE**

- **`EnemyRevealCost`** — `int32`, `EditDefaultsOnly`, default **30**, on `ACommanderNpc`, carrying a `// GDD §…` comment. ⛔ **A MECHANIC RULE ⇒ a UPROPERTY default, ⛔ NEVER a `cards.csv` column** (the §3.0 mechanic-rules-aren't-card-stats law).
- ⛔⛔ **THE STANDING RULING *"THE AI NEVER SPENDS GOLD"* IS UNTOUCHED, AND THIS SECTION SAYS SO IN LAW SO NOBODY LATER "FIXES" IT.** ⚖️ **The spend is initiated by the PLAYER'S OWN CLICK on a UI button, executed on the AUTHORITY through the existing `ASiegePlayerState::SpendGold`, and it is ⛔ UNREACHABLE FROM EVERY ASSISTANT COMMAND PATH — no intent, no `who`, no `where`, no executor branch can reach it.** ✅ **QA CRITERION: grep the assistant executor for any reveal/gold call and report ZERO.** ⚖️ **The player spending gold at a map his AI happens to stand next to is not the AI spending gold, and the distinction is written down because it will look like a violation to someone reading fast.**
- **RPC shape (M8 law: `Server<Verb><Noun>` / `Client<Verb><Noun>`):** **`ServerRequestEnemyReveal()`** (Reliable, `WithValidation`) on `ASiegePlayerController` → the authority calls `SpendGold(EnemyRevealCost)` → on success builds the dot list → **`ClientReceiveEnemyReveal(const TArray<FVector2D>& Dots)`**.
- ⚖️ **FROZEN-SNAPSHOT RULING (the default that ships):** the revealed dots are a **SNAPSHOT taken at purchase** and ⛔ **do NOT track moving enemies.** ⚖️ **Jonathan's own sentence presupposes it — *"pay another 30 gold to reveal the NEW locations"* only makes sense if the first set went stale.** ⚠️ **FLAGGED to him; the alternative (live-until-close) is one bool.**
- ⛔ **CLEARED ON CLOSE, ALWAYS.** Closing the map DISCARDS the snapshot; re-opening shows no red dots until paid again. ⛔ **No persistence across opens. ⛔ No persistence across Play Again / match reset.**
- ⛔ **NET-ZERO REFUSAL:** insufficient gold ⇒ the button refuses **BEFORE any gold moves**, with a HUD line. ⛔ **Never a partial spend, never a silent no-op** (the shipped refusal doctrine).
  - ⭐⛔ **AMENDED 2026-08-15, RULING `W4-R2` — THIS CLAUSE NOW CARRIES ITS OWN OBSERVATION INSTRUMENT, BECAUSE IT WAS FOUND WITHOUT ONE.** ⚠️ **TASK-564 reported that the refusal had NEITHER a unit test NOR a PIE row: the spend and the clear-on-close were both covered, but *"insufficient gold ⇒ refuses before any gold moves"* had never been watched trip.** ⇒ ⛔ **`SC-§32` in its purest form — a guardrail nobody has watched trip is a guardrail nobody has tested, and a refusal path that silently spends is INVISIBLE until it has taken a player's gold.**
  - ✅ **THE INSTRUMENT IS A PIE ROW, ⛔ NOT A UNIT TEST, AND THE REASON IS THE SAME ONE WAVE 2 ESTABLISHED:** the spend lives on the AUTHORITY through `ASiegePlayerState::SpendGold`, so a unit test would have to stand up a world, a controller and a player state — at which point it asserts the engine's replication, ⛔ not our refusal. **The row is `TASK-569` (q).**
  - ⛔ **AND THE ROW MEASURES THE *BALANCE*, NOT THE BUTTON: read gold before, attempt, read gold after, and require the two figures to be IDENTICAL.** ⚖️ **"Nothing appeared to happen" is not evidence of net-zero — a spend followed by a failed reveal looks exactly the same on screen and is the actual defect this clause exists to prevent.**
- ⚠️⛔ **HONEST LIMITATION, RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: THE REVEAL IS AN ECONOMY/UI GATE, ⛔ NOT AN ANTI-CHEAT BOUNDARY.** On a listen server the client already holds the enemy actors under Tier-B relevancy. ⛔ **Do not describe it as concealment, and do not build a hiding mechanism on this claim.**

### WR-§8 📌 M8 DECLARATION — ⛔ **DO NOT COPY THE LAST THREE BATCHES' BOILERPLATE. IT IS FALSE HERE.**

⛔ **This batch adds NO replicated property, NO new replicated class and NO new relevancy tier — but it DOES add TWO RPCs** (`ServerRequestEnemyReveal` / `ClientReceiveEnemyReveal`) on `ASiegePlayerController`, because gold is authority-owned. ✅ **Ally dots need nothing new: own-team actors are already relevant to their own client.** ⚠️ **`ATorch` and `ACommanderNpc` are TIER C (purely local/cosmetic props with no gameplay truth) and DECLARE it in a header comment** — the declaration duty is *"tier not declared is a QA FAIL"*, and Tier C is a declaration, not an exemption.

### SC-§35 ⛔⛔ THE ANIM-OWNER LAW — **AN ANIMBLUEPRINT IS A CONTRACT WITH ITS OWNER'S CLASS, ⛔ NOT A DECORATION ON A SKELETAL MESH** (added 2026-08-16; bought by TASK-569 row (m), repaired by TASK-591)

⛔ **THE MEASURED DEFECT THAT BOUGHT THIS LAW, STATED WITH ITS ARITHMETIC:** `ACommanderNpc` — an **`AActor`** (`CommanderNpc.h:129`) — was assigned `/Game/Characters/ABP_Footman.ABP_Footman_C` in its own C++ constructor (`CommanderNpc.cpp:32`). That ABP's EventGraph calls **`TryGetPawnOwner()`**, which returns **None** on a non-Pawn owner, so **both** its `Set GroundSpeed` and `Set bIsMoving` nodes failed **every frame, on every instance**: ⛔ **1,806 Blueprint runtime errors in 49 s with 2 NPCs alive** (903 per node). ⭐⭐ **IT COMPILED CLEAN, PASSED 111/111 TESTS AND CLEARED *TWO* QA GATES.**

1. ⛔ **A `USkeletalMeshComponent` on a non-`APawn` actor may NOT be given an AnimBlueprint that queries its owner as a Pawn.** ⇒ **Any code assigning a `TSoftClassPtr<UAnimInstance>` MUST state, in a comment at the assignment, WHICH OWNER CLASS THE ABP ASSUMES.** ⚖️ **An ABP is not a texture. It runs a graph against an owner, and the owner's class is half of its contract — an unstated half is an unchecked half.**
2. ✅ **THE SANCTIONED SHAPE FOR A NON-PAWN PROP THAT MUST IDLE IS SINGLE-NODE PLAYBACK** — `SetAnimationMode(EAnimationMode::AnimationSingleNode)` + `PlayAnimation(<UAnimSequence>, /*bLooping=*/ true)`. ⭐ **A single-node instance HAS NO GRAPH, so it is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of this defect class** — that is the reason it is preferred, ⛔ not convenience.
3. ⛔ **THE REPAIR IS MADE AT THE CONSUMER, ⛔ NEVER AT THE SHARED ABP.** `ABP_Footman` is the ENTIRE rigged fleet's locomotion asset (`SummonedUnit.cpp:60`, and `ASummonedUnit : public ACharacter` ⇒ ⛔ **its use is CORRECT and must not be disturbed**). ⚖️ **Null-guarding a fleet-wide asset's graph to fix one prop's misuse trades a 2-file code diff for a shared-asset edit whose blast radius is every unit in the game.**
4. ⛔⛔ **"NULL-SAFE" IS NOT "OWNER-SAFE", AND THIS IS THE ROW MOST WORTH RE-READING.** The author of `CommanderNpc.h:313-322` reasoned CAREFULLY about null-safety and shipped the defect anyway: the case considered was ***the ABP is MISSING*** (⇒ ref pose, never a crash); the case that fired was ***the ABP RESOLVED and assumed a Pawn***. ⇒ **Both cases must be named at the assignment. A guard against absence says NOTHING about a present-but-wrong asset.**
5. ⛔⛔ **THE INSTRUMENT IS PIE, AND THERE IS NO SUBSTITUTE — `SC-§32` AT ITS SHARPEST.** This defect class is invisible to the compiler, to `warnings_as_errors`, to the automation suite and to code review: it needs a **live anim update on a spawned actor**. ⇒ ⭐ **A BATCH IN WHICH NO TASK RAN PIE HAS OBSERVED *NOTHING* ABOUT RUNTIME, however green its gates.** ✅ **STANDING RULE: any batch that spawns a NEW ACTOR CLASS into the world owes ONE PIE session with a MESSAGE-LOG READ, and that row may ⛔ NEVER be waived on the grounds that the compile is clean.**
6. 📌 **AND THE CLASS-CONVERSION TEMPTATION IS REFUSED IN ADVANCE:** *"make the actor a Pawn so the ABP is happy"* is ⛔ **the wrong direction.** It inverts the dependency (the prop bends to the asset), and on this codebase it would additionally place the prop into every pawn-shaped query in the project — `GetPawnIterator`, AI perception, targeting — making a decorative NPC **acquirable as a target** to buy an idle animation. ⇒ ⛔ **Fix the assignment, ⛔ never the hierarchy.**

### SC-§36 ⛔⛔ A COMMENT NAMING ANOTHER TASK AS THE BINDER IS A ***DEBT***, ⛔ NOT A WIRING (added 2026-09-01; bought by TASK-748 → TASK-750, caught by TASK-750)

⛔ **THE MEASURED DEFECT THAT BOUGHT THIS LAW:** `AHeroCharacter` declared `OnHeroRecallArrived` and shipped a warning that reads *"The teleport-home owner must bind this delegate **(TASK-750)**"* (`HeroCharacter.cpp:1333`). ⭐ **The design was RIGHT** — the hero deliberately must not learn where home is (`HeroCharacter.h:146`) — **and the delegate was correctly declared, correctly broadcast (`:1348`) and correctly guarded (`IsBound()` at `:1310`, with `BuildArrival` refusing to move or heal when unbound).** ⚠️⚠️ **BUT ⛔ NOBODY BOUND IT.** ⇒ **a completed 10-second recall channel would have teleported and healed ⛔ NOTHING** — the player spends the channel, survives the interrupt window, and arrives **nowhere**. ✅ **TASK-750 caught it and bound it** (`SiegeGameMode.cpp:466`, handler `:470`, routed through the **same `GetHeroStartTransform` the respawn path uses** at `:493` — ⛔ never `ResetHero()`).

1. ⛔⛔ **A COMMENT IS ⛔ NOT A BINDING. IT COMPILES, IT READS AS INTENT, AND IT WIRES ⛔ NOTHING.** ⚖️ **The naming of a future task inside a comment creates the *feeling* of a completed handoff while leaving the actual edge unbuilt** — and the task named may never have been told.
2. ⛔⛔ **AND THE SHARPEST EDGE: ⛔ NOTHING FAILS IF THE DEBT IS NEVER HONOURED.** No compile error, no link error, no red test — a well-guarded unbound delegate degrades **quietly and correctly** into doing nothing. ⭐ **The better the guard, the more silent the omission.** ⚠️ *This is the `TOWER-§8.5` swept-stall class and the `MARK-§ M-4` `ClearMarks()`-with-no-caller class in a third costume: a correct mechanism that is never actually driven.*
3. 📌 **THE DUTY, AND IT IS THE MANAGER'S AS MUCH AS THE PROGRAMMER'S:** a task that declares an extension point another task must fill ⇒ ⛔ **the obligation goes on the BOARD, in the named task's spec, as an explicit numbered item** — ⛔ **never only in a source comment.** ⭐ **If the consuming task's spec does not mention it, it is ⛔ not specified**, and the handoff must say so loudly enough that the manager boards it.
4. ✅ **THE CONSUMING TASK MUST ASSERT THE BINDING EXISTS**, ⛔ not merely that the code path is correct when bound. **An `IsBound()` guard is a fail-safe, ⛔ not a wiring, and a test that only exercises the bound path proves nothing about the shipped game.**
5. ⭐ **PRECEDENT — THREE IN ONE BATCH, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A LAW AND ⛔ NOT A NOTE:** `OnHeroRecallArrived` (unbound delegate) · `USiegeMapMarkSubsystem::ClearMarks()` (**shipped with no caller**, TASK-744) · `AClimbableTower::CanTeamAscend()` (⭐ **written as a statement of the collision matrix with ⛔ NO caller and passed QA in that state** — it waited for `TOWER-§8.6` to give it one). ⚖️ **Three unwired-but-correct surfaces in one wave is a process signal, ⛔ not three coincidences.**

### SC-§37 ⭐⭐ WHERE A VALUE'S CORRECTNESS IS INVISIBLE TO REVIEW, THE TEST MUST **MEASURE THE PROPERTY**, ⛔ NEVER RESTATE THE VALUE (added 2026-09-01; the pattern promoted from TASK-745)

⚖️ **`SHIP-§9`'s standard — *"can this assertion actually FAIL?"* — applied to DATA rather than to gates.** ⛔ **A test that asserts `Colour == <the same literal the code holds>` proves ⛔ NOTHING: it restates the value and fails only if someone edits both halves inconsistently.** ⭐ **A test that measures the *property the value exists for* fails when the value stops doing its job — which is the only failure anyone cares about.**

⭐ **THE WORKED EXAMPLE THAT BOUGHT IT — and it defends a trap `WM-§8e` could previously only WARN about:** `WM-§8e` records that `WarMapWidget.cpp` deliberately holds `FLinearColor` constants in **two different colour spaces**, and rules that a constant whose space is not named is not shippable. ⚠️ **But a comment cannot stop an "sRGB correction" — it can only reproach one afterwards.** TASK-745 instead wrote a test that **measures the mark colour's contrast against BOTH ends of the terrain ramp: 3.81:1 (dark) and 3.85:1 (light), against a 3.84:1 theoretical flat-colour ceiling** derived from `WM-§8c`. ⇒ ⭐⭐ **an sRGB "correction" of that constant collapses the light end to ~1.3:1 and turns a SILENT, INVISIBLE colour-space error into a RED TEST.**

1. ✅ **THE RULE: if a value's wrongness would be invisible in a diff and invisible at review, the test asserts the MEASURED PROPERTY** — contrast ratio, clearance, ratio-to-a-ceiling, reachability — ⛔ **not the literal.**
2. ⭐ **PREFER A PROPERTY WITH A DERIVED CEILING.** Measuring *"3.81 against a ceiling of 3.84 computed from the ramp"* is stronger than *"≥ 3.0"*: it re-derives the target from the same inputs the value was tuned against, so it survives a change to the thing being contrasted against.
3. ⛔ **AND STATE THE LIMIT HONESTLY.** TASK-745 recorded that a contrast ratio and a channel distance are **necessary, ⛔ not sufficient** — this is ⛔ not a colour-blind simulation, a deuteranope may read magenta and red closer than the numbers do, and **the shape tells carry that case.** ⚖️ **A measured property is evidence, ⛔ not proof, and Jonathan's eye remains the acceptance** (`AS-§6 A(e)`).
4. 📌 **SCOPE — ⛔ this is ⛔ NOT a mandate to test every constant.** It binds where **three** things hold: the value is tuned rather than arbitrary · a plausible "fix" would silently break it · and the breakage is invisible to compile, review and the naked eye at review time. ⚖️ *Those are exactly the conditions under which a comment is not enough.*

### SC-§36.1 ⛔⛔⛔ **THE DECOMPOSITION CLAUSE — A TASK THAT BUILDS A SURFACE AND A TASK THAT CALLS IT ARE BOARDED ***TOGETHER***, OR THE DECOMPOSITION ITSELF CARRIES THE DEBT** (added 2026-09-02; bought by TASK-777, and ⛔ it is the MANAGER's failure, ⛔ not the implementer's)

> ### ⚖️⭐⭐ **`SC-§36`'s SHARPEST INSTANCE YET, AND IT IS SHARPER THAN THE THREE THAT BOUGHT THE PARENT LAW — BECAUSE ⛔ NOBODY EVEN WROTE A COMMENT NAMING A FUTURE BINDER. ⛔ THERE WAS ⛔ NOTHING TO FIND.**

⛔ **THE MEASURED FACT:** TASK-777 built `AClimbableTower::TryBeginContactClimb(ACharacter*, float)` (`ClimbableTower.h:402`, `ClimbableTower.cpp:661`), tested it, and shipped it. ✅ **Manager-verified by grep at source, ⛔ not on relay: it has ⛔ ZERO callers in `Source/` — the only other occurrences of the name are its own declaration and three comments.** ⇒ ⛔⛔ **THE SURFACE IS COMPLETE, ITS TESTS PASS, AND THE FEATURE SIMPLY DOES NOT HAPPEN.**

1. ⚖️⭐⭐ **⛔ NOTHING FAILED, AND THAT IS THE ENTIRE POINT.** ⛔ No compile error · ⛔ no link error · ⛔ no red test · ⛔ no warning · ⛔ no reviewer question. **A trigger with no caller is indistinguishable, from every gate we own, from a trigger that works.** ⚖️ *`SC-§36` clause 2 said the better the guard, the more silent the omission. This says something worse: the better the SURFACE, the more complete the illusion.*
2. ⛔⛔ **THIS WAS A ⛔ DECOMPOSITION FAILURE, ⛔ NOT AN IMPLEMENTER FAILURE, AND IT IS RECORDED THAT WAY DELIBERATELY.** ⭐ **TASK-777 did ⛔ NOT reach out of its fence to manufacture a caller — ⛔ correct** (the caller belongs in `ASummonedUnit::Tick`, explicitly outside its grant: *"⛔ No body changes"*). ⭐ **And it did ⛔ NOT give the tower a tick to route around the fence — also correct, and it ENFORCED that refusal with a test** that reflects over `AClimbableTower`'s members and errors on any `Timer`/`Tick`/`Poll`/`Interval` token (`Tests/SiegeClimbableTowerTest.cpp:1197`, under `…DeclaresTheClimbCompletionUFunctionAndNoPollingSubstitute` at `:1112`). ⚖️ **An implementer that stays inside a fence AND fences itself against the tempting escape has done its job perfectly. The gap was in the BOARD, and the board is mine.**
3. ✅⭐⭐ **THE RULE, AND IT BINDS THE MANAGER AT DECOMPOSITION TIME, ⛔ NOT THE PROGRAMMER AT HANDOFF TIME:** ⛔ **a task that builds a callable surface and the task that calls it are boarded ⛔ IN THE SAME WAVE, each naming the other by ID, or the surface is ⛔ NOT boarded at all.** ⭐ **If the caller lives in a file the surface's task may not touch, that is ⛔ not a reason to defer it — it is the ⛔ PROOF that a second task is required, and it must be written in the same sitting.**
4. 📌 **THE CHECKABLE TELL, so this is a gate and ⛔ not a good intention: for every `public` function a task adds, its `names:` block must name ⛔ EITHER the call site in the same task ⛔ OR the TASK-### that owns it.** ⛔ **A `public` surface with neither is a decomposition defect and the board must not accept it.** ⚖️ *`SC-§36` clause 3 already said the obligation goes on the board — this clause says WHEN: at decomposition, ⛔ never retroactively when a handoff is kind enough to notice.*
5. ⭐ **AND CREDIT WHERE IT IS OWED, BECAUSE IT IS THE PROCESS WORKING:** the gap was found and escalated **by the implementer, in its own handoff, under `SC-§36` clause 3, with the grep pasted.** ⛔ **That is ⛔ not a substitute for boarding it correctly the first time** — ⚖️ *`SC-§36`'s own precedent list already warned that three unwired surfaces in one wave is a process signal, and this is the fourth.*

## Damage types (C++)
- UDamageType subclasses named `USiegeDamageType_<Kind>`, all declared in `Source/GitClaudeUnrealTest/Siegebound/DamageTypes.h/.cpp`
- Kinds: `Melee`, `Projectile`, `Siege` (**added M4, TASK-054**), `Spell` (**added M5, TASK-098**)
- Damage-vs-fortification scaling (GDD §3.0) reads `DamageEvent.DamageTypeClass`: Projectile = 50%, Melee/default = 100%, **`Siege` = 200%**. **M4 ruling:** the 200% applies to BOTH the castle (`ACastle::TakeDamage`) AND buildings (`ABuilding::TakeDamage`) — Siege units (Profile=Siege: Ogre, Sapper) tag their attacks with `USiegeDamageType_Siege`. Units and the hero always take the listed damage (no scaling). Attackers tag projectile/siege damage; melee needs no tag.
- **M5 ruling — `Spell` = 50% in `ACastle::TakeDamage` ONLY** (mirrors the M2 Projectile precedent, NOT the M4 Siege both-rule): buildings/units/hero take FULL listed spell damage — Lightning (200) must kill an Arrow Tower (150 HP), it is "the tower-killer" per GDD §4. All spell damage is applied with `USiegeDamageType_Spell`.

## Spells & Set III (M5)
Added 2026-07-08 (TASK-097..109; GDD §3.5/§3.11/§4 Set III/§7). Spells have NO actor blueprints — they resolve through code (see resolver). Crystal Tower is a normal building card (existing `BP_Building_<CardID>` / `SM_<CardID>` laws apply: `BP_Building_CrystalTower`, `SM_CrystalTower`; card art `T_CardArt_<CardID>` law applies to all 6 new CardIDs).
- **Set III CardIDs (row names, character-for-character):** `Fireball`, `FrostNova`, `Lightning`, `BattleCry`, `Pickpocket`, `CrystalTower`.
- **Spell resolver:** `USpellLibrary` (UBlueprintFunctionLibrary) in `Source/GitClaudeUnrealTest/Siegebound/SpellLibrary.h/.cpp` — the ONE home for spell resolution, shared by `ASiegePlayerController` (targeting mode) and `ASiegeBotController` (M5 bot rules). Entry point pinned: `static bool USpellLibrary::ResolveSpell(UWorld* World, FName CardID, const FCardRow& Row, ETeamId CasterTeam, const FVector& TargetPoint)`. Null-safe everywhere; no friendly fire (§3.0).
- **FCardRow M5 columns (typed one-per-concept, sparse; registry continues the M4 list):**
  - `SpellEffect` (`ESpellEffect` enum, `None`) — dispatch token: `None` / `AoEDamage` (Fireball) / `Freeze` (FrostNova) / `TopTargetsDamage` (Lightning) / `AllyBuff` (BattleCry) / `GoldSteal` (Pickpocket). Declared in CardRow.h. CSV cells use the enum value names.
  - `EffectDuration` (float, 0) — timed-effect seconds (FrostNova 4, BattleCry 8).
  - `MaxTargets` (int32, 0) — top-N target count (Lightning 3).
  - `GoldSteal` (int32, 0) — gold stolen, capped at what the victim has (Pickpocket 10).
  - `ChainTargets` (int32, 0) — Chain keyword arrives as its typed column per the M4 deferral note: total targets hit per attack (CrystalTower 3).
  - `ChainFalloff` (int32, 0) — flat damage reduction per bounce (CrystalTower 5 ⇒ 15/10/5 with Dmg 15).
  - Spells REUSE `Damage` (Fireball 100, Lightning 200) and `AoERadius` (Fireball 300, FrostNova 350, Lightning 400, BattleCry 400) — no duplicate radius/damage columns.
- **Mechanic rules (UPROPERTY defaults with GDD § comments, NOT CSV — M2/M4 precedent, e.g. Rally/Charge magnitudes):** BattleCry magnitudes (+50% attack speed, +25% move speed), `ChainBounceRadius` = 350 (bounce search radius from the previous target — GDD doesn't specify; manager-defined), freeze non-stacking refresh rule.
- **Targeting mode (§3.5/§7):** spells target ANYWHERE on the map (no half restriction); the ground reticle is TRACE-projected onto whatever surface is under the cursor (terrain-ready for M4.5 hills — LAW, not a follow-up); LMB confirms (gold deducted at confirm — card-leaves-hand-at-CONFIRM law), RMB/Esc cancels free. **Exception (manager ruling):** `GoldSteal` spells resolve INSTANTLY on play (no reticle for a global effect — recorded deviation from §3.5; CardType stays Spell).
- **Spell VFX (code contract):** every spell resolve spawns `/Game/VFX/NS_Spell_<CardID>` (Niagara, Content/VFX/), soft path COMPOSED from the CardID (mirrors the BP soft-class-path law), null-safe: missing system ⇒ log once, resolve anyway. Crystal Tower's chain visual is `/Game/VFX/NS_ChainZap`. Donor-duplicate authoring from Variant_Combat Niagara systems is acceptable at M5 (template-donor rule); §6 one-frame readability bar.
- **Targeting reticle material:** `M_SpellReticle` (Content/Materials/, DeferredDecal domain — M_CenterlineStripe recipe), soft-referenced by the targeting-mode code, null-safe (missing ⇒ no visual, targeting still works, log once).
- **Spell VFX element re-skin (M7, TASK-187):** the fire/ice spell systems are RE-SKINNED to the imported `Content/Fire_Magic/` + `Content/Ice_Magic/` Niagara packs AT THEIR EXISTING code-contract paths — `/Game/VFX/NS_Spell_Fireball` (← `Fire_Magic/VFX_Niagara/NS_Fire_Magic_Explosion` or `_AOE`) and `/Game/VFX/NS_Spell_FrostNova` (← `Ice_Magic/VFX_Niagara/NS_Ice_Magic_Shockwave`/`_Frozen`/`_Snowstorm`). **NO rename, NO new data column:** `USpellLibrary::ResolveSpell` COMPOSES the path from the CardID (SpellLibrary.cpp:77-78), so the re-skin MUST land at these exact placeholder paths (a data column cannot point at a `Fire_Magic` asset). This is a VFX LOOK-SWAP, NOT a new card — Fireball (cards.csv row 24, `DeckCount 2`, in deck) + FrostNova (row 25, `DeckCount 0`, NOT in the default deck — see flag) already exist from M5.

The §6 audio hooks (TASK-179, C++, null-safe) play a sound at each gameplay event via the COMPOSED soft path `/Game/Audio/S_<Event>` — a code contract (like the `SM_<CardID>` / `NS_Spell_<CardID>` string laws), null-safe (missing ⇒ silent + log once). The 14 event cues are the cross-discipline contract; the artist authors a SoundCue at each EXACT path (character-for-character = the TASK-179 list). This folder did NOT exist before M7 — the cues must be AUTHORED at `/Game/Audio/`.

## Material & Niagara lane laws
- **Custom-HLSL BAN (codified 2026-07-22 from TASK-245; previously lived only in orchestrator memory + the TASK-239 handoff):** NEVER use a Custom HLSL node in materials on this project — under the Substrate + HW-RT stack it detonates shader permutations and wedges the editor (TASK-239: 0-for-2, ~4 h lost; the stock-node rebuild compiles in seconds — TASK-245 proof). STOCK NODES + PARAMETERS ONLY; parameter iteration never recompiles. Evidence: handoffs/TASK-239.md.
- **UE 5.8 Niagara/material lane notes (pointer):** three engine findings from the TASK-245 session — the sprite-VF TexCoord bug, per-instance ObjectPositionWS behavior, and the dead attributeBindings lane — are documented in `handoffs/TASK-239.md` (FINAL SESSION). Read before authoring sprite-based Niagara or per-instance material logic.
- **Instanced-mesh material flag law (codified 2026-07-22, TASK-249):** any material consumed via `FScatterLayer.OverrideMaterial` (or ANY runtime HISM `SetMaterial`) MUST set `bUsedWithInstancedStaticMeshes=true` — without it the HISM silently renders the gray WorldGridMaterial default. TASK-249 evidence: the first wired seed rendered gray with `OverrideMaterials[0]` correctly set; the flag fixed it. Evidence: handoffs/TASK-249.md.

### ⛔⛔ NIAGARA INERTNESS — THREE FINDINGS, ONE OF THEM A LIVE CONTENT DEFECT (added 2026-09-01; TASK-747 · `qa/TASK-753.md` W-5 · TASK-759)

- ⛔⛔ **A NIAGARA SYSTEM DUPLICATED VIA MCP / `EditorAssetLibrary` IS ***SILENTLY INERT*** — AND ⛔ NO HASH, STATE OR PROPERTY CHECK CAN DETECT IT. ⭐ ONLY PIXELS CAN.** It loads, reports the correct class, resolves the correct dependencies, spawns a component that reports ⛔ no error — and renders **nothing**. ⚠️⚠️ **`is_active()` and `is_visible()` return `true` for the inert duplicate too ⇒ a state readback proves ⛔ NOTHING.** ✅ **The repair is opening it ONCE in the Niagara editor** (that is what triggers the compile), then an **EXPLICIT single-path save**. ⛔⛔ **AND THE `.uasset` BYTES ARE ***UNCHANGED*** BY THE REPAIR** — measured `a082d797…` before and after ⇒ **the compiled data is DDC-side, ⛔ not package-side** ⇒ ⛔ **a sha / mtime / `git status` check cannot tell a working system from a dead one.** ⇒ ⛔ **EVERY NEW `NS_` DUPLICATE IS CONFIRMED ON PIXELS AT INTEGRATION** (`AS-§6 A(e)`, `SHIP-§9c`), ⛔ never on a readback. ✅ **Done correctly for `NS_RecallChannel` at TASK-742 — proven on pixels in PIE, explicitly ⛔ not on `is_active()`.**
- ⛔⛔ **`NS_CastleDebris` IS INERT — AND THE DUPLICATION IDIOM IS ⛔ ***EXONERATED*** FOR IT: ITS DONOR `NS_Damage` RENDERS NOTHING EITHER.** Measured with a **calibrated three-way control in one frame** (TASK-759): CONTROL `NS_Fire_Magic_Orb` `active:true` at **every** age with real bounds `262/164/164`; **DONOR `NS_Damage` and SUBJECT `NS_CastleDebris` both `active:false` at EVERY age** (0.02 · 0.1 · 0.3 · 0.6 · 1.2 · 2.5 · 5.0) with **identical degenerate bounds `244/128/128`**; **pixels agree** (`handoffs/TASK-759-C`). ⭐⭐ **THE DECISIVE STEP: opening it in the Niagara editor — the repair for the duplication defect — did ⛔ NOT revive it.** ⇒ **`Castle.cpp:1394` has ALWAYS burst an empty system at every crumble threshold** (and `:1393`'s *"null-safe until `NS_CastleDebris` lands"* is stale — it landed, and it is empty). ⚖️ **A live CONTENT defect, ⛔ unrelated to the recall/ghost features** — boarded as **`TASK-768`**.
- ⚠️⚠️ **AND THE READING THAT MUST ⛔ NOT BE OVER-READ, BECAUSE IT ALREADY WAS ONCE: *"DEAD AT SYSTEM AGE 10.0"* IS A ***CHANNEL-SURVIVAL*** MEASUREMENT, ⛔ NOT A RENDER TEST.** TASK-747/759's age-10.0 sweep existed to find an effect **still running when a 10-second channel ends**; ⭐ **a one-shot burst that has correctly finished by then reads `active:false` BY DESIGN.** ⇒ ⛔ **the five `/Game/VFX/NS_Spell_*` and `NS_ChainZap` reading `false` at 10.0 is ⛔ NOT evidence that they render nothing** — and `handoffs/TASK-238.md` records `NS_Spell_Fireball` + `NS_Spell_FrostNova` **PIE-verified at the gameplay camera**, which is the stronger evidence and points the other way. ✅ **The only admissible verdict is the CALIBRATED MULTI-AGE sweep TASK-759 used on `NS_CastleDebris`** — a known-good control in the same frame, ages spanning the effect's **own** lifetime, and pixels. ⛔⛔ **Nobody writes *"the spell VFX are dead"* into law, a spec, a handoff or a Slack post until that sweep says so (`TASK-768`).** ⚖️ *An instrument aimed at one question does not get to answer a different one — `SHIP-§9`'s class, pointed at ourselves a second time.*
- 📌 **`FAB-008` is the standing answer for a purpose-built looping channel effect:** the project owns **no** effect authored to last a channel — 20 systems staged and age-scrubbed, **only 5 survive 10.0 s**, and 3 of those are opaque ice-shard meshes disqualified on pixels.

## Textured mesh law (TRELLIS.2 art pipeline)
Added 2026-07-07 (TASK-082..088, Jonathan-approved plan: automated TRELLIS.2 → Blender → UE5 pipeline). Governs game-ready textured meshes produced by `Tools/ArtPipeline/` (pilot scope: Footman, Archer, Castle; the remaining M7 blockouts follow this template). `<AssetName>` = CardID for card actors, `Castle` for the castle.
- **Active pipeline assets:** Footman · Archer · Castle (pilot, TASK-082..088) + **Ogre** — pulled forward from the M7 batch by Jonathan's 2026-07-14 directive (TASK-147..152). NO new naming pattern: the Ogre follows this law verbatim — `SM_Ogre` (same-path overwrite of the blockout) / `T_Ogre_D|_N|_ORM` / `MI_Ogre_PBR` from `M_AssetPBR` / slots [`TeamRegion`, `OgrePBR`], UNIT path (feet-center, ≤15k tris, 1024² bakes, ≤4 generated hulls, `ucx:null`). Concept casing note: the drop arrived lowercase `ogre.png`; the AssetName is PascalCase `Ogre` (reconciled at TASK-147). The remaining 15 blockouts stay deferred to M7.
- **Concepts:** the ACCEPTED concept image for each produced asset is committed at `Content/RawAssets/Concepts/<AssetName>.png`. Working inputs live in `Tools/ArtPipeline/Inbox/<AssetName>.png` and intermediates in `Tools/ArtPipeline/Cache/<AssetName>/` — both gitignored.
- **Stage 0 — concept generation (M7, Jonathan-AUTHORIZED 2026-07-16; TASK-184 build / TASK-185 run):** concepts may be AUTO-GENERATED by `Tools/ArtPipeline/concept_generate.py` — a text→image client that mirrors `trellis_generate.py`'s structure, HF_TOKEN ENV-ONLY secret-handling (guard-secrets `hf_` law), and CLI/exit-code discipline (drives an HF text-to-image Space/model via the existing HF PRO token). Per-CardID art-direction prompts live in `Tools/ArtPipeline/concept_prompts.json` (art-director-authored). Output = `Tools/ArtPipeline/Inbox/<CardID>.png` (PascalCase AssetName = CardID — the existing Inbox law; the tool writes PascalCase directly, so no casing reconcile is needed). Jonathan may review/REPLACE any generated concept before its TRELLIS Stage-1 wave consumes it (OPTIONAL / NON-blocking — TASK-167). This REPLACES the hand-drop concept gate for the 16 M7 blockouts. `concept_generate.py` is `Tools/**/*.py` = CODE → the tooling QA gate applies before commit.
- **✍️ FLUX.1-dev PROMPT LAW (added 2026-08-01; learned the expensive way across 8 rolls at TASK-369 — binds every entry in `concept_prompts.json`).** Two rules, both measured on real rolls, not style advice:
  - **(1) WRITE IN POSITIVE FORM ONLY — IN-PROMPT NEGATIONS *SUMMON* THEIR TOKENS.** `negative_prompt` is **dropped entirely** by FLUX.1-dev (it is guidance-distilled, so there is no CFG channel to carry it), which means every defence has to live in the positive prompt — and negating there **backfires**. Demonstrated on roll 2: *"not rounded pauldrons"* → **got rounded pauldrons**; *"absolutely NO branching antler rack"* → **got a branching antler rack**. Rolls 3+ were rewritten with **zero** negations and immediately behaved. **Never write "no X" / "not X" / "without X" — describe the thing you DO want instead** ("flat slab mantle" beats "no rounded pauldrons"). The `negative_prompt` field stays authored in `concept_prompts.json` for a future CFG-model swap; **it is inert today and must never be relied on.**
  - **(2) HARD STYLE CLIFF AT ≈1.6k CHARACTERS — KEEP ENTRIES ≲1,600.** The shared style block (*"Warcraft Rumble tier, 2.5–3 heads tall, hand-painted"*) sits at the **END** of every entry, so a long prompt dilutes exactly the tokens that keep the roster coherent. At **2,007 chars** (roll 3) the tail washed out and the roll lost the roster style, the chunky proportions **and** two identity props at once. Back at **~1,570** (rolls 4–6) the style returned. The other **18 shipped concepts are 700–900 chars**, which is why this never surfaced before — the cliff is only reachable on an unusually specified subject. If an identity genuinely needs more than ~1,600 chars, **cut description, not the style tail** (or move the style block to the front and re-validate).
  - **Reproducibility:** a shipped concept entry pins its winning **seed** so `concept_generate.py <Asset> --force` reproduces it byte-for-byte (Sorcerer = seed 71022, 1,573 chars). Record the roll count and both gate verdicts in the handoff.
- **Mesh swap:** the refined FBX exports to the EXISTING blockout path `Content/RawAssets/<AssetName>.fbx` and imports OVERWRITING `/Game/Meshes/SM_<AssetName>` in place — same-path swaps keep every code/BP soft reference (including the placement-ghost `/Game/Meshes/SM_<CardID>` string contract) intact. NEVER delete+recreate the SM asset.
- **Textures:** `/Game/Textures/T_<AssetName>_D` (sRGB) · `T_<AssetName>_N` (normal) · `T_<AssetName>_ORM` (packed Occlusion/Roughness/Metallic, LINEAR — sRGB off). PNG sources checked in at `Content/RawAssets/Textures/<AssetName>/`. Bake sizes: 1024² units / 2048² buildings.
- **Two-slot material contract (requires ZERO C++ changes):** every pipeline mesh has EXACTLY two material slots, in order — **slot 0 named `TeamRegion`** (a minority face-set: trim/banners/accents; the BeginPlay team recolor hardcodes `MI_TeamColor_<Team>` onto slot 0 — SummonedUnit.cpp:146 / Building.cpp:80 / Castle.cpp:125 — and keeps working unchanged; author `MI_TeamColor_Blue` as the design-time placeholder), **slot 1 named `<AssetName>PBR`** assigned `MI_<AssetName>_PBR` (Content/Materials/Instances/), an instance of the master **`/Game/Materials/M_AssetPBR`** whose texture parameters are named exactly `BaseColor`, `Normal`, `ORM`. The placement ghost tints ALL slots (already true today).
- **Mesh settings:** **Nanite OFF** on pipeline meshes (ruling). UV layer named exactly `UVMap`. Tri budgets: units ≤15k, castle ≤40k (per `pipeline_manifest.json`). Origins: units feet-center, buildings ground-center. Export axis contract: `axis_forward='-Z'`, `axis_up='Y'`, `apply_unit_scale`, FACE smoothing. Collision: units ≤4 simple hulls; buildings author explicit `UCX_SM_<AssetName>` geometry — the castle UCX must be wall-footprint-exact (M1 plinth ~410-unit dead-zone lesson) with bounds within ±10% of the blockout.
- **Tooling law:** `Tools/**/*.py` is CODE — the full QA gate applies before commit. **`HF_TOKEN` is ENV-ONLY**: read from the environment at runtime; never written to any file, never passed on argv, never echoed/logged (guard-secrets hook carries the `hf_` pattern). Heavy Blender refine runs HEADLESS via `blender.exe --background --python` through Bash — the live Blender MCP bridge has a 30 s socket cap and is for <30 s inspection/preview only.
- **Fab quarantine:** marketplace packs land in `Content/Fab/<Pack>/` and are READ-ONLY donors (the Variant_* rule applies: soft-reference or duplicate-into-/Game/, never edit in place). Acquisition is HUMAN-ONLY via `.claude/pipeline/fab/FAB-REQUESTS.md` (FAB-### entries: requested → approved → fulfilled → integrated; Jonathan fulfills via the Epic Launcher). Agents never browse/buy/download Fab.
- **Lane isolation:** this pipeline NEVER writes `Content/RawAssets/CardArt/` or `/Game/UI/CardArt/` — those belong to the card-art chain (TASK-077..081, "Card artwork (hand UI)" law).
- **M7 batch scope (16 remaining blockouts, TASK-166..173):** the M7 art pass upgrades ALL remaining un-textured blockouts through this law verbatim. UNIT path (feet-center, ≤15k tris, 1024² bakes, two-slot `[TeamRegion, <CardID>PBR]`, ≤4 hulls, `ucx:null`): `Knight`, `Miner`, `Cavalry`, `Cleric`, `Longbowman`, `MilitiaMob`, `Pikeman`, `Sapper`. BUILDING path (ground-center, 2048² bakes, authored `UCX_SM_<CardID>` wall-footprint-exact hulls, two-slot `[TeamRegion, <CardID>PBR]`): `ArrowTower`, `Wall`, `BombTower`, `BallistaTower`, `Barracks`, `DeepMine`, `CrystalTower`. Each same-path overwrites `/Game/Meshes/SM_<CardID>` (soft-ref parity, never delete+recreate). Concepts arrive at `Tools/ArtPipeline/Inbox/<CardID>.png` (PascalCase AssetName = CardID; casing reconciled at TASK-166) — the source-of-concepts gate (TASK-167) precedes all Stage-1 generation. Footman/Archer/Castle/Ogre are already shipped and are NOT re-run.
- **GoldNode emissive economy-prop VARIANT (M7 ruling, TASK-166/171):** `SM_GoldNode` IS in the M7 batch (all 16 upgraded) but is the ONE exception to the two-slot TeamRegion contract — it is the §"Team contract" team-color EXCEPTION (gold nodes carry emissive glow regardless of team; `AGoldNode` never runs the BeginPlay slot-0 recolor and is a level prop, not a card actor). It therefore takes a SINGLE-slot PBR+EMISSIVE material with NO `TeamRegion` slot: slot 0 named `GoldNodePBR` assigned `MI_GoldNode_PBR` (from `M_AssetPBR`) with the warm-yellow emissive PRESERVED — either keep the existing authored `M_GoldGlow` emissive on a dedicated slot OR bake a `T_GoldNode_E` emissive channel wired into `MI_GoldNode_PBR` (art-director's call at TASK-171; §6 "gold glows warm yellow (emissive)" is the bar). Manifest `team_region:null`, BUILDING path (2048²/ground-center). Everything else follows the law (same-path overwrite of `/Game/Meshes/SM_GoldNode`, Nanite off, `UVMap`). Concept `Inbox/GoldNode.png`. **⚠️ AS-SHIPPED CORRECTION (2026-07-27, TASK-309 audit): the `MI_GoldNode_PBR` option was NOT what shipped — `SM_GoldNode` slot 0 carries `M_GoldGlow` directly and `T_GoldNode_*` are ORPHANED (referenced by nothing on screen). Same for CrystalTower / `MI_CrystalGlow` / `T_CrystalTower_*`. See "GoldNode / CrystalTower glow materials" below before touching either — a texture re-bake for these two changes NOTHING.**

## ⛔ ART-TOOLING HAZARD LAWS (2026-08-15) — namespace **`TL-§N`**

Added 2026-08-15 from TASK-566's two runs (the WAR-ROOM import leg) + TASK-582/TASK-584; ⭐ **extended the same day with `TL-§4` (the UMG design-time tree), from TASK-568 cross-read against TASK-355.** ⚖️ **Filed under the MECHANISM, ⛔ NOT under the feature that found them** — `WR-§` is a feature namespace and these four bind every future import and every future widget, in every batch. (The `(c)`-extension lesson: *a law indexed by one of its symptoms fails to cover the next one.*) Cite as `TL-§1`, never as a bare `§1`.

### TL-§1 ✅ THE ASCII-ONLY `pipeline_manifest.json` HOLD IS **RETIRED**, GLOBALLY — AND THE HAZARD IT PROXIED WAS RECORDED WRONG

- ✅ **RETIRED 2026-08-15 BY MANAGER RULING, ⛔ and only after it was EXERCISED, not merely fixed.** **TASK-582 landed `encoding="utf-8"` on both text reads in `Tools/reimport_meshes.py` (`:148` sidecar, `:162` manifest); `qa/TASK-584.md` criterion (6) PASSED it; and TASK-566 run 2 then READ A MANIFEST CONTAINING 251 NON-ASCII BYTES through `:162` and authored the castle's 25 collision boxes from it.** ⇒ ⚖️ **The retirement is discharged by a green run, ⛔ not by a diff.** ⭐ **`pipeline_manifest.json` was ALREADY non-ASCII (em-dash ×81, `±` ×2, `§` ×2 — all in prose fields, ⛔ none in `ucx.boxes`): the constraint had been silently violated before it was lifted, and the crash had simply not been rolled yet.**
- ⛔ **THE RETIREMENT IS GLOBAL, ⛔ NOT PER-SCRIPT, AND THAT WAS *SWEPT*, NOT ASSUMED:** every other manifest reader in the tree was ALREADY encoding-explicit (`Tools/ArtPipeline/refine_trellis_glb.py:213`, `Tools/ArtPipeline/rescale_refined_fbx.py:634`); `Tools/ArtPipeline/build_warroom_props.py` and `Castle.cpp:64` mention the manifest in COMMENTS ONLY. ⭐ **And a fact the sweep added that nobody had claimed: there is NO manifest WRITER anywhere in the tree — it is hand-authored.**
- ⚠️⛔ **THE CORRECTED HAZARD, BECAUSE THE ONE WE WROTE DOWN WAS WRONG AND WRONG IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION.** **cp1252 has exactly FIVE UNDEFINED BYTES — `0x81 0x8D 0x8F 0x90 0x9D` — and ONLY a character whose UTF-8 encoding contains one of them raises `UnicodeDecodeError`. Everything else MOJIBAKES SILENTLY.**
  - ⛔ **`⭐` (U+2B50 → `0x90`) CRASHES. `🔍` (U+1F50D → `0x8D`) CRASHES.** ✅ **`⛔` does ⛔ NOT crash. Neither does `—`, `±` or `§` — they corrupt quietly.**
  - ⚖️ **Of the twenty glyphs this pipeline uses in specs and handoffs, TWO crash and EIGHTEEN mojibake.** ⇒ ⛔ **THE RULE WE HAD WAS A PROXY FOR A FIVE-BYTE TRAPDOOR THAT TWO OF OUR MOST-USED SPEC GLYPHS FALL STRAIGHT THROUGH — and it named the wrong trigger character, so anyone testing the rule with `⛔` would have "disproved" a real hazard.**
- ⛔⭐ **THE STANDING LAW THAT REPLACES THE HOLD — IT IS AN OBLIGATION ON THE *CODE*, ⛔ NOT A CONSTRAINT ON THE *DATA*, WHICH IS WHY IT CANNOT ROT:** **every text-mode `open()` in `Tools/**` carries an explicit `encoding=` (`"utf-8"` for reads of repo data).** ⚠️ **UE's embedded Python on Windows defaults to `cp1252`; a bare `open()` is a latent decode crash on the first `⭐` anyone pastes.** ⛔ **A new `Tools/` script with a bare text `open()` is a QA finding.** ✅ **Writes are ⛔ NOT retro-fitted without a ruling — changing an output encoding changes bytes another tool consumes, which is a behaviour change wearing a bug-fix costume** (there are currently ZERO write-mode `open(` in `reimport_meshes.py`).
- ⚠️ **KNOWN, OPEN, ⛔ CANNOT FIRE TODAY (`qa/TASK-584.md` WARN-3, manager follow-up TASK-587): the fix flips the FAILURE DIRECTION for a non-UTF-8 manifest and the two call sites handle it ASYMMETRICALLY** — `_resolve_card_ids()` has no `try/except` (a decode error kills the batch before card #1) while `_load_manifest()` degrades to `{}` and continues. ⚖️ **⛔ The follow-up is NOT "make them symmetric": see `TL-§2`, which rules that `_load_manifest()`'s graceful degradation is the DANGEROUS one.**

### TL-§2 ⚠️ **HEADLINE PARTLY FALSIFIED 2026-08-15 (`W6-R3`)** — `UCX_` HULLS **DO** SURVIVE UE 5.8 IMPORT **WHEN THE NODE NAMES BIND**; THE MANIFEST STAYS THE COLLISION AUTHORITY **BY CHOICE, NOT BY NECESSITY**; AND A ZERO-COLLISION BUILDING IS **STILL A STOP**

- ⛔⛔ **READ THIS BEFORE THE CLAUSES BELOW — THE ORIGINAL HEADING WAS WRONG AND IS PRESERVED ONLY AS THE THING BEING CORRECTED (`W6-R3`, from TASK-567's throwaway probe).** ⭐ **MEASURED: `Castle.fbx`'s `UCX_SM_Castle_00..24` imported as **25 CONVEX ELEMS**, with **ZERO** manifest authoring.** ⇒ ⛔ **"UCX does not survive UE 5.8 import" is FALSE as a general claim, and TASK-566's WarTable observation ⛔ DOES NOT GENERALISE.**
- ⭐ **THE ACTUAL MECHANISM, WHICH IS AN *ASSET-AUTHORING* FAULT AND ⛔ NOT AN ENGINE LIMITATION: UE binds a hull to its render node BY NAME — `UCX_<render-node-name>_NN`.** ⚠️ **The WarTable FBX carries BOTH a `WarTable` node AND an `SM_WarTable` node, so `UCX_SM_WarTable_00`'s binding never resolved and the hull was dropped. `Castle.fbx` has ONE render node, `SM_Castle`, and its hulls bind exactly.** ⇒ ⛔ **The rule is NAME DISCIPLINE AT EXPORT: one render node per mesh, and the `UCX_` prefix matches it byte for byte.**
- ⚖️ **WHAT THIS CHANGES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT — stated so the correction is not over-read:**
  - ⛔ **UNCHANGED, AND STRENGTHENED: the SILENT-PATH STOP below.** ⭐ **The correction ADDS A SECOND WAY TO REACH ZERO HULLS BEHIND A GREEN RUN** (a name-mismatched `UCX_` node) **on top of the decode-failure path.** ⇒ **the readback-and-STOP rule is now covering two mechanisms, not one.**
  - ⛔ **UNCHANGED: `pipeline_manifest.json` remains the authoring authority for building-class collision, in-editor hand-editing stays BANNED, and `_apply_box_collision()` stays the sanctioned mechanism.** ⚠️⛔ **BUT THE JUSTIFICATION IS RE-WRITTEN: it is a DELIBERATE DETERMINISM CHOICE — boxes are reviewable, diffable and identical run to run — ⛔ NOT a workaround for an engine that eats hulls.** ⚖️ **A law kept for a reason that turned out to be false is a law the next batch will discard for the wrong reason.**
  - ⛔ **CHANGED: TASK-588's premise.** ⛔ **A manifest WRITER is no longer the obvious fix; an EXPORT-TIME NAME ASSERTION is the cheaper candidate. See the amended pointer at the end of this section.**

- ⚠️ **MEASURED TWICE, YEARS APART IN PIPELINE TIME: `UCX_SM_WarTable_00` was authored in Blender, exported in the FBX, and imported with **0 hulls under BOTH `combine_meshes` settings**, with ⛔ NO stray asset and ⛔ NO error.** ⭐ **PRE-EXISTING AND ALREADY KNOWN — `Tools/reimport_meshes.py:309-311` documents working around exactly this for the castle** (*"Bootstrap a body_setup deterministically (guarantees one exists even if the FBX's UCX did not import), then overwrite its geometry with boxes"*). **TASK-566 repaired the war table the same proven way: 1 box, centre `(0,0,55)`, `380×250×110`.**
- ⛔ **THE LAW (it restates `WR-§1`'s clause and generalises it past the castle): `pipeline_manifest.json`'s `ucx.boxes` is the SOLE collision authority for building-class and prop-class meshes. ⛔ The raw FBX is NEVER trusted for collision. ⛔ In-editor hand-editing of collision primitives stays BANNED.** ✅ **The sanctioned mechanism is `_apply_box_collision()`, and it is deterministic.**
- ⛔⭐ **THE PART THAT WAS MISSING AND IS THE REASON THIS CLAUSE EXISTS: THE SILENT PATH.** ⚠️ **`_apply_box_collision()` with no manifest boxes appends a `WARN` and returns `False` — the import still reports DONE.** ⇒ ⛔ **A building can ship with NO authored collision and the batch summary still reads green.** ⚖️ **Combined with `TL-§1`'s open WARN-3, the two compose into the worst available outcome: a manifest that fails to decode returns `{}`, `{}` means "no boxes", "no boxes" means a WARN, and a WARN means a castle you can walk through, with a successful-looking run behind it.**
- ⛔ **THE ACCEPTANCE RULE, BINDING ON EVERY IMPORT FROM NOW ON: a mesh's authored hull/box count is READ BACK AND REPORTED, and a count of ZERO is a STOP — ⛔ UNLESS the manifest DECLARES the mesh collisionless on purpose** (`ucx: null`; the unit path, and `SM_Torch`, which is *required* to carry zero collision). ⚖️ **"Zero" and "zero on purpose" are different facts and only the manifest can tell them apart** — ⛔ do not infer it from the asset.
- 📌 **The authoring-side repair — deriving the manifest box FROM the authored `UCX_` geometry at export time, so no future prop needs a hand-typed box — is boarded as TASK-588, DIAGNOSE-FIRST.** ⛔ **It is an ergonomics fix; the STOP above is the safety fix and does not wait for it.**
  - ⚠️⛔ **AMENDED 2026-08-15 (`W6-R3`): TASK-588's PREMISE IS PARTLY FALSIFIED AND ITS PRIORITY DROPS.** ⛔ **The clause it was justified by — _"after UE 5.8 silently drops the imported hull"_ — is FALSE for a correctly-named FBX.** ⇒ ⭐ **THE LEADING CANDIDATE IS NOW THE CHEAPER ONE: assert the NAME DISCIPLINE at export (exactly one render node; `UCX_<node>_NN` matching it), which fixes the WarTable class at its source and ⛔ adds NO writer to a hand-authored file.** ⚖️ **The manifest-writer question stays OPEN and stays REFUSABLE — ⛔ and "the engine ate my hull" may no longer be used as its argument.**

### TL-§2a ⛔⛔ `auto_generate_collision=False` GATES WHETHER COLLISION IS PROCESSED **AT ALL** — THE COMMENT AT `reimport_meshes.py:275-278` IS **FALSE**, AND THE SCRIPT'S OWN `agg_geom` OVERWRITE IS **WHY NOBODY CAUGHT IT** (added 2026-09-01, TASK-742 integration)

> ### ⛔ **THE SHIPPED CLAIM, VERBATIM AT `Tools/reimport_meshes.py:275-278`: *"UCX_ collision nodes in the FBX are still recognized by the importer **regardless of** this flag; we overwrite the agg_geom afterwards."* — ⛔ FALSE.**

- ⭐ **MEASURED BY ISOLATING ONE VARIABLE AT A TIME** (same FBX, same options object, nothing else changed — `WatchTower.fbx`, 8 authored `UCX_SM_WatchTower_00..07`):

  | `auto_generate_collision` | hulls imported | `bIsGenerated` |
  |---|---|---|
  | **`False`** (the shipped value, `:278`) | ⛔ **0** | — |
  | **`True`** | ✅ **8** | ⛔ **false** on all 8 |

- ⭐⭐ **`bIsGenerated == false` IS THE DECISIVE READING, AND IT IS WHAT MAKES THIS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A GUESS: the flag did ⛔ NOT *fabricate* 8 hulls — it PERMITTED THE AUTHORED ONES TO BE PROCESSED.** ⇒ **the flag gates whether collision is processed AT ALL, ⛔ not merely whether it is auto-generated.** ⚠️ **Its name is the trap: it reads as *"do not invent collision"* and behaves as *"do not import collision."*** Cross-check: `qa`-grade evidence in `handoffs/TASK-737-artist.md` §8 (`8 / 0`, `bIsGenerated` false ×8, read back out of a real import).
- ⭐⭐ **WHY IT SURVIVED EVERY PRIOR RUN — AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: THE SCRIPT ALWAYS OVERWRITES `agg_geom` AFTERWARDS.** Both branches do it (`_apply_unit_hulls` → `remove_collisions()` + convex decomposition; `_apply_box_collision` → bootstrap a `body_setup` then write manifest boxes) ⇒ **the import's 0 hulls were replaced by authored geometry on every path that HAD authored geometry, so the false comment never produced a visible symptom.** ⛔⛔ **THE SAME OVERWRITE IS EXACTLY WHAT WOULD STRIP HAND-AUTHORED COLLISION AND REPORT `DONE`** — ⚖️ *the defect and its camouflage are the same line of code.*
- ⭐ **IT CORRECTS `TL-§2`'s MECHANISM WITHOUT OVERTURNING IT, AND THE DISTINCTION MATTERS:** name discipline (`UCX_<render-node>_NN` matching exactly one render node) is **NECESSARY and ⛔ NOT SUFFICIENT** — a byte-perfect name still yields **0 hulls** through this options object. ✅ **TASK-567's 25-convex-elem `Castle.fbx` probe STANDS**; it simply did not run through `_make_import_options()`. ⚖️ *Two true findings about the same path, taken from different entry points — ⛔ neither refutes the other.*
- ⚠️⛔ **A SECOND, INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENT THAT CHANGES A REIMPORT'S SAFETY MODEL: UE ***PRESERVES CUSTOMIZED COLLISION*** ACROSS A SAME-PATH REIMPORT.** The old ramp's **14** hulls **survived the first pass of the new FBX** and had to be **explicitly cleared** before the FBX could be the source of truth. ⇒ ⛔⛔ **A GREEN REIMPORT DOES ⛔ NOT PROVE THE SHIPPED HULLS CAME FROM THE FBX YOU JUST IMPORTED.** ✅ **Read back the COUNT *and* `bIsGenerated`, and CLEAR FIRST whenever the authored geometry changed** — otherwise the mesh silently keeps the previous design's collision under the new render mesh, which is the `TL-§2` walk-through-castle failure wearing the opposite costume.
- ⚖️ **THE PROCESS SIGNAL, STATED AS A SIGNAL AND ⛔ NOT AS BLAME: this is the SECOND defect in this ONE file's collision path** (the first is `TL-§2b`, still open). ⭐ **Two defects in one path means the path is UNDER-TESTED, ⛔ not that two authors were careless** — and both were found by someone **reading the code against a measurement**, never by a run going red. ⇒ **boarded as `TASK-765` + `TASK-766`, gated by `TASK-767`; the durable repair is a READBACK ASSERTION, ⛔ not a corrected comment.**

### TL-§2b ⛔ `_category_of()` DEFAULTS AN **ABSENT** CardID TO `"unit"` — WHICH **STRIPS AUTHORED HULLS AND REPORTS SUCCESS**. ⚠️ **STILL OPEN FOR THE ABSENT CASE**

- **At source, `Tools/reimport_meshes.py:180-186`:** `entry = manifest.get(card_id, {})` → `cat = entry.get("category", "unit")`. ⇒ a mesh with **no manifest entry** — a typo, a new asset, or a manifest that failed to load and degraded to `{}` (`TL-§1`'s open WARN-3) — takes the **unit** branch, which runs `remove_collisions()` + convex decomposition. ⛔ **A building's authored `UCX_`/box collision is DELETED and the batch summary still reads green.**
- ✅ **TASK-737 PROVED THE TRAP IS CLOSED FOR `WatchTower` BY SIMULATING THE SHIPPED FUNCTION — ⛔ not by reading it:**
  ```
  WatchTower                  -> category=building  boxes=[]  -> _apply_box_collision
                                 -> WARN + LEAVES imported collision      [TRAP CLOSED]
  CONTROL (no manifest entry) -> category=unit -> AUTO-DECOMPOSITION      [the trap]
  ```
  ⇒ ⭐ **the trap is REAL and its control is MEASURED; only the absent case is unfixed.**
- ⛔ **THE LAW UNTIL IT IS FIXED: AN ABSENT MANIFEST ENTRY IS A STOP, ⛔ NEVER A DEFAULT.** ⚖️ *`"unit"` is a guess wearing a default's clothes* — and `TL-§2`'s readback-and-STOP rule is the only thing standing between it and a castle you can walk through.

### TL-§3 ⛔ THE HEADLESS `-run=pythonscript` COMMANDLET CANNOT REACH `StaticMeshEditorSubsystem` — SO THE EXPLICIT LOD CHAIN IS AN **EDITOR-ONLY** STEP

- ⚠️ **MEASURED (TASK-566 run 2): `LOD_STEP_FAILED` on `SM_Castle` — the subsystem is unavailable in a headless commandlet, so the explicit `CASTLE_LOD_CHAIN` (`reimport_meshes.py:119-122`: LOD1 50 % @ 0.4 · LOD2 25 % @ 0.15 · ⛔ NO LOD3 — the landmark-silhouette law) was ⛔ NOT applied, and the mesh kept the chain it already had.** ✅ **Fixable over MCP in the RUNNING editor; ⛔ never from the commandlet.**
- ✅⭐ **THE FAILURE PATH IS *STATE-NEUTRAL*, AND THIS IS MANAGER-VERIFIED BY READING THE ARTIFACT, ⛔ NOT RELAYED: the `subsys is None` raise is at `:378-379`, ⛔ BEFORE the `lod_group = "None"` write at `:384`** — and the code says so in its own comment (*"only now that the options built — keeps the failure path state-neutral"*). ⇒ ⛔ **There is NO half-applied state: no orphaned `lod_group`, no truncated chain. The mesh is in a CONSISTENT PRIOR state, which is what makes the repair a measure-then-apply rather than a rescue.**
- ⛔ **THE LAW: `_apply_lods()` is NON-FATAL by design (the collision-helper precedent) — so a `LOD_STEP_FAILED` token in a headless run is EXPECTED, ⛔ NOT a build failure, and ⛔ MUST NOT be triaged as one.** ⛔ **But it may not be swallowed either: it is a DEBT that must be discharged in the editor before the batch's commit, and the discharge is a MEASURED readback per LOD (`lod_count`, `lod_group`, per-LOD `screen_size` + triangle count), ⛔ never a claim.**
- ⛔⭐ **THE INHERITANCE RULE, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS EXPENSIVE IF IT IS LEFT LATE: A DUPLICATE INHERITS THE SOURCE MESH'S LOD CHAIN.** ⚠️ **The crumble trio is duplicated FROM `SM_Castle`** ⇒ **a stale chain on the source becomes FOUR stale chains the moment the trio is derived.** ⛔ **And divergence is worse than staleness: if `SM_Castle` carries chain A and `SM_Castle_Crumble0N` carries chain B, the damage-state swap changes the LOD switch distance — a visible pop at a distance that has nothing to do with damage, on a mesh the whole `WR-§1` crumble law exists to keep visually stable.** ⇒ ⛔ **All four castle-class meshes carry the SAME chain, and the readback proves it mesh by mesh.**
- ⚖️ **PRIORITY, STATED SO NOBODY OVER-WEIGHTS IT: this is PERF/VISUAL POLISH. The castle ships a working 3-LOD chain today.** ⛔ **It may NOT block a commit, a nav measurement, or a playtest** — if the subsystem cannot be reached live either, ⛔ REPORT and board it, do not improvise a substitute.
- ✅⭐ **AMENDED 2026-08-16 (TASK-586) — `LOD_STEP_FAILED` IS **MORE** BENIGN THAN THE CLAUSE ABOVE STATES: ⭐ THE CHAIN SURVIVES THE FAILURE, AND THE MECHANISM IS WORTH KNOWING RATHER THAN RE-DISCOVERING.** **`replace_existing_settings=True` PRESERVES A PACKAGE'S REDUCTION SETTINGS ACROSS AN IN-PLACE OVERWRITE** ⇒ **an FBX re-derivation RE-COMPUTES the 50 % / 25 % reductions against the NEW LOD0 and KEEPS the authored screen sizes.** ⭐ **MEASURED ON ALL FOUR CASTLE-CLASS MESHES AFTER A HEADLESS `LOD_STEP_FAILED`: `lod_count 3`, thresholds `[1, 0.4, 0.15]`, per-LOD triangles `[28698, 14348, 7174]` — IDENTICAL across `SM_Castle` and the three crumbles.** ⇒ ⛔ **THE CORRECT DISCHARGE IS *MEASURE-THEN-APPLY*, AND *"THE READBACK ALREADY MATCHES, SO NOTHING WAS WRITTEN"* IS A COMPLETE RESULT** — ⛔ **do NOT manufacture a `set_lod_thresholds` / `generate_lods` call to prove the task did work; that dirties four packages and re-lands them in a commit for nothing.**
- ⚠️⛔ **AND ONE ROW THIS PROJECT'S LIVE LANE ⛔ CANNOT DELIVER, NAMED SO NO FUTURE SPEC ASKS FOR IT: `auto_compute_lod_screen_size` IS ⛔ NOT REFLECTED ON THE MCP SURFACE.** ⚠️ **The commandlet route is the other option and `TL-§3`'s own headline takes the subsystem out there** ⇒ **the only remaining instrument is a human in the Static Mesh Editor.** ⛔ **A spec that lists it as an ACCEPTANCE row is asking for something no agent can produce.** ✅ **What IS available, and is the right substitute: the thresholds read back EXACTLY `0.4` / `0.15` — auto-computed sizes are geometry-derived and do not land on authored round numbers — ⛔ but that is an INFERENCE and is reported as one, ⛔ never as a passed row.**
