- **Audit-method law (carry forward on EVERY building audit):** a **bleached roof is the `TeamRegion` slot painted `MI_TeamColor_Blue`, NOT wash-out** — ArrowTower and Barracks read near-white in flat-lit previews for exactly this reason. **NEVER commission a rebuild to "restore the red roof"**; the concepts' terracotta was deliberately traded for the team-colour identifier.

## Castle 3× HOLLOW (2026-07-28) — supersedes the Castle bounds/plinth laws above; adds the team-gated interior
Added 2026-07-28 (Jonathan directive: castle **27× volume (3× per dimension)**, HOLLOW walkable interior, own units enter AND spawn inside, enemy units cannot enter; NEW concept art; built through the Meshy pipeline — TASK-347..351). Everything in "Castle remaster" above stays law EXCEPT where this section supersedes it.
- **NEW BOUNDS LAW (supersedes the ~814×819×898 target):** bounds within **±10% of 2442×2460×2694 uu** (3× the shipped 814.5×820.6×894.9). Ground-centre origin, Nanite OFF, LOD law UNCHANGED (explicit 3-chain LOD1 50%@0.4 / LOD2 25%@0.15 — NOT `LargeProp`). **Tri budget raised for the hollow interior: target ≤30k, hard cap 40k** (the solid castle's ≤20k is not achievable with an authored interior; say so in the handoff if >30k).
- **⚠️ THE SHELL LAW (why Stage-2 authors the interior):** Meshy image3d produces closed SHELLS — the hollow interior, gate arch, and flat walkable interior floor are **AUTHORED in the Stage-2 Blender step** (Boolean hollow + gate cut + floor), never expected from generation. **The concept must DEPICT an open front gate** so the generated exterior matches the authored opening.
- **GATE + INTERIOR SPEC (numeric law, derived from the largest shipped agents — Ogre capsule hh145, Cavalry r45/205-deep):** gate clear opening ≥ **500 uu wide × 450 uu tall** (**the 450 is HELD LAW, re-affirmed 2026-07-28 against a delivered 412: it covers the Ogre (290) AND a hero JUMP-THROUGH at the threshold — hero ~190 capsule + ~250 jump apex ≈ 440 head height — plus future-taller-agent margin; do not re-litigate as arbitrary**); interior floor FLAT at ground level, threshold step ≤ **40 uu** (nav step height); interior clear height ≥ 450 uu across the walkable floor. Recast must generate navmesh INSIDE and through the gate (Dynamic RecastNavMesh regenerates at PIE — M6.6 lane knowledge; MCP has NO nav-build call, the editor-side bake/PIE regen is the lane).
- **⚖️ NAVMESH-REBUILD LAW (added 2026-07-29, from the TASK-349/350 loop-3 escalation, finding N2):** **a FOOTPRINT-CHANGING remaster ⇒ an EXPLICIT navmesh-rebuild ruling at decomposition time.** The SAVED level bake goes stale SILENTLY when an asset's footprint/collision changes under it (the 3× castle proved it: the saved `L_Arena` bake predated the hollow interior — a fresh boot had NO interior navmesh, and runtime-Dynamic regeneration is not a substitute for a stale SAVED bake). Any future footprint-class change (scale, hollow, new opening, moved hulls) must BUDGET the rebuild-and-save as a named step — and any `L_Arena` save remains a JONATHAN-APPROVED, one-time, nav-data-only exception with a tight diff gate (the 2026-07-29 escalation ruling is the template; the never-save law resumes immediately after each exception).
- **UCX DOOR-GAP LAW (supersedes "11 solid boxes"):** the authored `UCX_SM_Castle` set becomes door-gapped perimeter walls (boxes flanking the gate + a lintel above the clear height) + an interior floor slab + keep/tower hulls (expect ~16–24 hulls). UCX-DRIFT duties carry (measure hull-outer-face vs visual wall per side, report); the `pipeline_manifest.json` `ucx.boxes` lane is the ONLY edit path (in-editor hand-editing stays BANNED). **A crumble re-derivation must CARRY the door gap** — a damage-state swap may never seal the gate (or open it to enemies: the gating lives on ACTOR components, not the mesh — see below). **⚠️ FBX-COLLISION-GAP law (added 2026-07-29, TASK-350 flag 2): the raw `Castle.fbx` carries only 11 UCX boxes — the SHIPPED 22-hull door-gapped set is MANIFEST-AUTHORED and applied by the pipeline, NOT present in the FBX. Any future direct-FBX castle (re)import must NOT trust the FBX for collision — the manifest `ucx.boxes` set is the sole collision authority (the crumble trio inherits the 22 via byte-copy duplication, never via FBX import).**
- **PLINTH DEAD-ZONE — RETIRED (supersedes the M1 law + `CastlePlinthClearance` 420):** interior spawn/placement is now the FEATURE, so the plinth placement-refusal around the OWN castle is retired; placement truth = navmesh projection + collision + existing clearances (the interior floor is navmesh'd, so interior placement works by construction). The enemy interior is unreachable via the team gating below, not via a dead zone. The C++ task diagnoses every `CastlePlinthClearance`/`IsPointInsideCastlePlinth` call site and retires them cleanly — never a silent violation.
- **PAIRED-TUNABLE RE-DERIVATION:** `SpawnBoxHalfExtent` **(840,840) → (2460,2460)** at ALL THREE paired sites (`ACastle` ≡ `ASiegePlayerController` ≡ `ASiegeBotController` — the 3-way pairing law; cross-notes updated) — preserves the original intent (box half-extent ≈ the castle's full width). **The mid `ACaptureZone::ZoneHalfExtent` stays (840,840)** — its "same size as the spawn box" origin was descriptive, not a pairing law; scaling mid changes capture gameplay, which this directive does not touch (FLAGGED to Jonathan). `SpawnBoxAnchorInset` 40 unchanged. `DA_BattlefieldScatter` castle keep-clear radii re-derive ×3 (they were computed off the old ~814 bounds).
- **TEAM-GATED INTERIOR (naming + mechanism law — the belt-AND-braces ruling):** each castle admits its OWN team and blocks the enemy, via BOTH lanes because neither suffices alone — a collision blocker is invisible to Recast (enemy AI would path to the door and pile up), and a nav filter does nothing to the player-controlled hero (not pathed):
  - **Physical truth:** two new object channels in `DefaultEngine.ini` — **`ECC_SiegeTeamBlue` / `ECC_SiegeTeamRed`** (GameTraceChannel aliases). Every combatant capsule (`ASummonedUnit`, `AHeroCharacter`) sets its ObjectType by team at BeginPlay (via `ITeamAgent::GetTeamId`). `ACastle` owns **`GateBlockerVolume`** (UBoxComponent spanning the gate opening) configured at BeginPlay: Block the ENEMY team's channel, Ignore the own team's. Null-safe; projectiles/spells unaffected (channels are body-only).
  - **⚖️ IGNORE-ALL-BODY COLLISION LAW (adopted 2026-07-28 from `qa/TASK-349.md` F1 + the CMC-floor-sweep finding — manager-ratified):** **any body that blocks Pawn but runs an ignore-all custom-response default MUST also explicitly Block `ECC_SiegeTeamBlue` AND `ECC_SiegeTeamRed`.** Why: `UCharacterMovementComponent::FloorSweepTest` traces on the capsule's OBJECT TYPE as the channel — a team-stamped capsule (now GameTraceChannel1/2) FALLS THROUGH any walkable ignore-all body that doesn't list the team channels, while the project's `DefaultResponse=ECR_Block` covers every ordinary profile for free. The two shipped ignore-all walkable bodies (scatter hills + tree proxies, `BattlefieldScatter.cpp:618-619/740-741`) carry the 2×2 Block lines; **every FUTURE ignore-all Pawn-blocking body must too, and removing those lines is a regression, not a cleanup.**
  - **Pathing truth:** per-team NavAreas **`UNavArea_BlueCastleInterior` / `UNavArea_RedCastleInterior`** applied by the castle's interior **`InteriorNavModifier`** (UNavModifierComponent, team-selected at BeginPlay) + per-team query filters **`UNavFilter_TeamBlue` / `UNavFilter_TeamRed`** (each excludes the ENEMY castle's interior area) set as `DefaultNavigationFilterClass` on unit AI controllers by team — enemy units never PATH inside, so no door pile-up.
  - **Hero ruling (default, FLAGGED to Jonathan):** the hero IS a team combatant — **blocked at the enemy gate** like any unit (the physical blocker). If Jonathan wants hero raids inside the enemy keep, it is a one-line channel-response change.
- **CONCEPT REGEN + BACKUP LAW:** the new concept is FLUX-lane (`concept_generate.py`) and lands same-path at `Content/RawAssets/Concepts/Castle.png` — but the OLD concept is first preserved as a dated sibling (`Castle_pre3x.png`) because it anchors the existing retention/chroma records; **all retention/chroma measurements for the 3× castle anchor on the NEW concept (alpha-masked, per the method law)**. Albedo floor (UV-norm ≥ 0.2536), luma retention 0.85–1.25×, and the anti-bleach guard apply unchanged; chroma retention reported vs the new concept.
- **CRUMBLE LAW FIRES AGAIN (automatic):** a new `SM_Castle` + new `T_Castle_*` ⇒ `SM_Castle_Crumble01/02/03` re-derived (byte-copy duplicates, BOTH slots re-assigned — the full CRUMBLE-DERIVATION law), and the new base albedo AUTO-REOPENS the STAGE-LEGIBILITY spread check (base-relative law) — measurement-first, re-spread only on a real-render band FAIL, per the TASK-337 pattern. SAMPLER-TYPE sweep + hard LOD readback on every import.
- **Unbroken by 3× (verify, don't assume):** HP/crumble thresholds and the win condition are data-driven off `ACastle` HP — scale-independent; the HP-bar widget height and gate-distance camera read are VERIFIED at integration (raise `HPBarWidget` Z ~3× if C++-owned/authored).

## GoldNode / CrystalTower glow materials — as-shipped truth + the emissive brightness lever (2026-07-27)
Added 2026-07-27 (TASK-332/333; Jonathan ruling on the TASK-309 audit: *"dial back the goldnode glow"*). Corrects what the "Textured mesh law → GoldNode emissive economy-prop VARIANT" clause implies is shipping.
- **AS-SHIPPED TRUTH (audit-verified, TASK-309):** `SM_GoldNode` slot 0 carries the hand-authored **`M_GoldGlow`** directly, and `SM_CrystalTower` carries **`MI_CrystalGlow`** — neither uses a `M_AssetPBR` instance and neither samples `T_GoldNode_*` / `T_CrystalTower_*`. **Those baked texture sets are ORPHANED**: they are imported, committed, and referenced by NOTHING on screen. Consequence, recorded so no session wastes credits on it: **a texture re-bake for GoldNode or CrystalTower changes NOTHING visually.** The glow material is the ONLY lever on either asset. The M7 GoldNode-variant clause's `MI_GoldNode_PBR` single-slot option was specced but not the shipped outcome; it is not to be "restored" without a fresh ruling.
- **⚠️ `GlowIntensity` is a RESERVED, RUNTIME-DRIVEN scalar param — it is NOT the brightness lever.** `AGoldNode::UpdateGlowGauge()` creates a lazy MID on slot 0 and writes `GlowIntensity = Lerp(GlowIntensityDepleted 0.05, GlowIntensityFull 1.0, Reserve/InitialReserve)` every gauge tick (the depleting-mine reserve gauge, TASK-253/257). **Therefore the material's authored DEFAULT for `GlowIntensity` is overwritten at runtime and dialling it back is a NO-OP in play.** The param name `GlowIntensity` (exact string, `AGoldNode::GlowIntensityParamName`) must remain a live scalar parameter on `M_GoldGlow` forever — renaming or deleting it silently kills the reserve gauge (the MID write becomes visually inert, no error).
- **The BRIGHTNESS LEVER (law):** dial the **base emissive strength authored INSIDE `M_GoldGlow`** — the value the `GlowIntensity` parameter multiplies — never the parameter default and never the C++ `GlowIntensityFull`. This keeps the gauge's semantics intact (`GlowIntensityFull = 1.0` still means "the authored look", which is simply dimmer now), needs ZERO C++ change, and preserves the depleted-ember floor proportionally.
- **Must survive any glow edit (regression set):** the TASK-257 `GlowIntensity` scalar Multiply, the TASK-226 **0.1 Hz ±12 % sine emissive pulse**, and the TASK-296c "keep-both" superset that merged them. **Stock nodes and parameters only — the Custom-HLSL BAN applies** ("Material & Niagara lane laws").
- **Blow-out acceptance metric (reusable for any emissive asset):** fraction of the mesh rendering past **luma 0.85** in a flat `CaptureAssetImage`, measured the same way for the asset and its reference. Working reference = **CrystalTower 6.5 % blown** (still reads as a crystal). GoldNode shipped at **86.3 % blown** (a featureless cream blob that loses the grey-rock / gold-crystal / orange-crack separation). Target band for a tuned emissive prop: **≤ 15 % blown**, with the concept's material separation legible AND the prop still unmistakably glowing at gameplay camera distance.

## Delegates (C++)
- Pattern: `FOn<Owner><Event>`, declared in the owner's header; the UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable) member is named `On<Owner><Event>`. Existing: `FOnCastleDestroyed`, `FOnGoldChanged`, `FOnCastleHPChanged(float CurrentHP, float MaxHP)`
- Broadcast on every ACTUAL value change and on reset paths; never on refused/ignored mutations (e.g., friendly-fire damage)
- UI consumers must seed from a getter first, THEN bind (qa/TASK-005-report.md major 2 — a bind-only widget created at a pinned value stays stale)

## Logging (C++)
- Gameplay log categories are named `LogSiege<Domain>`, declared in the owning module. The M3 rule-based bot's decision trace uses **`LogSiegeBot`** — exactly one line per fired decision (which of the §4 ordered rules played, what card, and where), so the "logged decision trace" acceptance in GDD §4 is grep-able.

## Template-donor rule (Variant_* and other template Content)
- Template content is READ-ONLY. Reuse it exactly two ways: (a) direct soft-reference (montages, Niagara systems, camera shakes, anim BPs), or (b) duplicate into a /Game/ project folder and modify only the duplicate. Never edit a donor in place.
- UMG: MCP tooling cannot author widget trees from scratch — every new widget starts as a duplicate of a donor (e.g., `/Game/Variant_Combat/UI/UI_LifeBar`, `/Game/Input/Touch/UI_TouchSimple`) and is rewired incrementally.
- BP function params: enum-typed params are impossible via MCP — use byte (uint8) or float params instead.
- Approved donors so far: `AM_ComboAttack` / `AM_ChargedAttack` / `ABP_Manny_Combat` (hero attack anim), `NS_Damage` (hit impact VFX), `BP_CameraShake_Hit_Enemy` (hit shake), `UI_LifeBar` (health bars) — all under /Game/Variant_Combat/.

## Widgets with C++ bases
- Pattern: `U<Name>Widget` (UUserWidget subclass) in Source/GitClaudeUnrealTest/Siegebound/, files `<Name>Widget.h/.cpp`; the UMG asset `WBP_<Name>` in Content/UI/ is reparented to it. Widget-facing events are BlueprintImplementableEvents with float/int/bool/byte/FString params only (never enums). Examples: `UCastleHealthBarWidget` ↔ `/Game/UI/WBP_CastleHealthBar`, `UCardHandWidget` ↔ `/Game/UI/WBP_CardHand`
- UWidgetComponents on actors are named `<Purpose>Widget` (e.g., `HPBarWidget` on `ACastle`)

## Overhead combatant health bars — REBUILT from castle parity (2026-07-10)
Added 2026-07-10 (TASK-130..132; Jonathan directive: *"there is still the same issue with all the unit health bars … rebuild the entire feature from scratch, make sure to make enemy health bars red and friendly health bars blue"*). After 5 failed attempts on the poll system below, the unit/hero/building overhead bar is REBUILT ON THE WORKING CASTLE'S PUSH/DELEGATE MODEL. **This SECTION SUPERSEDES "Overhead unit health bars (M5.5)" below** (that poll system is RETIRED). The castle bar itself (`ACastle` + `UCastleHealthBarWidget` + `WBP_CastleHealthBar` + `FOnCastleHPChanged`) is the TEMPLATE and is left UNTOUCHED.
- **Model — PUSH / delegate (mirror the castle, NOT poll):** each combat actor owns a per-actor HP-changed delegate the bar BINDS to (seed-then-bind), exactly like the castle — no poll timer. Delegate `FOnCombatantHPChanged(float CurrentHP, float MaxHP)` (mirror `FOnCastleHPChanged`); `UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable) OnHPChanged` on `ASummonedUnit`, `ABuilding`, `AHeroCharacter`, BROADCAST on EVERY HP mutation (damage, heal/regen, reset/respawn — miss none, or the bar goes stale: qa/TASK-005 major-2).
- **Provider interface (replaces IHealthBarTarget):** `IHealthBarProvider` (`UHealthBarProvider`, header-only `Source/GitClaudeUnrealTest/Siegebound/HealthBarProvider.h`) — `FOnCombatantHPChanged& GetHPChangedDelegate()`, `float GetHealthCurrent() const`, `float GetHealthMax() const`, `bool IsHealthBarActorAlive() const`; team via the EXISTING `ITeamAgent::GetTeamId` (never duplicated). Implemented by the 3 base classes; `ACastle`/`AGoldNode` do NOT implement it.
- **Widget base (mirror `UCastleHealthBarWidget`):** `UCombatantHealthBarWidget` (`CombatantHealthBarWidget.h/.cpp`) — `InitForCombatant(TScriptInterface<IHealthBarProvider>)` seeds THEN binds; float-only BIEs `OnHPChanged(float,float)` (→ `SetPercent(Cur/Max)` guard Max>0) and `SetTeamColor(float,float,float)` (→ fill tint). The BIEs MUST be TRUE overrides (`bOverrideFunction=true`) — a `K2Node_CustomEvent` is DSL-indistinguishable and NEVER fires from C++ (the defect that hid the bug 5×; verify the node class).
- **Widget component:** `UCombatantHealthBarComponent` (`CombatantHealthBarComponent.h/.cpp`, `UWidgetComponent` subclass), added in-constructor as `HPBarWidget` on the 3 base classes (subclasses inherit; no per-BP rewiring). Screen space, DrawSize ~90×12, `BarHeightZ` (default 120). BeginPlay: set WidgetClass = `/Game/UI/WBP_CombatantHealthBar` (soft, null-safe), read owner as `IHealthBarProvider`+`ITeamAgent`, `InitForCombatant` (seed-then-bind), push `SetTeamColor` ONCE. **ALWAYS VISIBLE while alive** (no hide-at-full — the reversed law), HIDDEN on death/destruction; per-BP `bShowHealthBar` opt-out kept (EditDefaultsOnly, default true). Tint data: `BlueBarColor` (0.05,0.30,1.00) / `RedBarColor` (1.00,0.10,0.05).
- **Widget asset:** `/Game/UI/WBP_CombatantHealthBar` — a FRESH DUPLICATE of the WORKING `WBP_CastleHealthBar` (NOT the retired, tainted `WBP_UnitHealthBar`), reparented to `UCombatantHealthBarWidget`. **PRESERVE the castle's exact fill-brush setup** (diff against the castle; the rebuild premise is the old bar DIVERGED from it). Unfilled TRACK = neutral grey ~(0.03,0.03,0.03)@~0.7α. **Prime suspect if the fill still won't render:** the old bar's `DefaultWhiteGrid_Low` MATERIAL fill brush (a material brush may not visually respond to `SetPercent`/`FillColorAndOpacity` like a plain image) — fallback is a plain-image fill brush, but do not pre-emptively diverge from the working castle.
- **Colors are LAW:** RED = ENEMY, BLUE = FRIENDLY (both teams), the fill tinted by team via `SetTeamColor` (data, never hardcoded in the WBP); the bar reads team by color, damage by length — never green→red.
- **Verification is LAW (unlocked desktop):** the feature is fixed ONLY when a REAL GDI SCREENSHOT of a REAL-COMBAT PIE (units actually taking damage) shows the fill VISIBLY LOWER after damage AND correctly team-tinted, and an agent CONFIRMS it in the pixels (unit + hero + tower, both teams). Prove RENDERED PIXELS, not `GetPercent()` UPROPERTY values; prove EXECUTION, not graph structure; report the observation, not the conclusion. NO "machine checks pass, ship it."
- **RETIRED by this rebuild (deleted):** `IHealthBarTarget`/`HealthBarTarget.h`, `UHealthBarComponent`/`HealthBarComponent.h+.cpp`, `UUnitHealthBarWidget`/`UnitHealthBarWidget.h+.cpp`, `/Game/UI/WBP_UnitHealthBar`. The "Overhead unit health bars (M5.5)" section below is HISTORICAL REFERENCE only.

## Overhead unit health bars (M5.5) — RETIRED 2026-07-10 (superseded by "Overhead combatant health bars — REBUILT" above; kept for history)
Added 2026-07-09 (TASK-110..112; Jonathan directive: "add a health bar to every tower and character"). Broadens GDD §7 ("Enemy hero/units show floating health bars when damaged") to **every combat actor, both teams** — see the TASKBOARD "M5.5 manager decisions" rulings block for the binding scope/behavior calls. This is a SEPARATE system from the castle bar: castles keep `WBP_CastleHealthBar` + the `FOnCastleHPChanged` delegate (M1, TASK-018/019) UNCHANGED; the M5.5 system covers units, buildings, and the hero, which carry NO HP-changed delegate (ASummonedUnit::ApplyHealing comment: "Units carry no HP-changed delegate (only ACastle does)"), so the bar POLLS the HP getters instead of binding.
- **Shared read interface:** `IHealthBarTarget` (`UHealthBarTarget` UINTERFACE, `NotBlueprintable`), header-only `Source/GitClaudeUnrealTest/Siegebound/HealthBarTarget.h` (the `TeamId.h` one-concept-header precedent). Three pure-virtual const methods (the `ITeamAgent::GetTeamId` C++-interface shape, NOT BlueprintNativeEvent): `float GetHealthCurrent() const`, `float GetHealthMax() const`, `bool IsHealthBarActorAlive() const`. Implemented by `ASummonedUnit` (→ `GetCurrentHP`/`GetMaxHP`/`!IsUnitDead`), `ABuilding` (→ `GetCurrentHP`/`GetMaxHP`/`!IsBuildingDestroyed`), and `AHeroCharacter` (→ `GetCurrentHP`/`GetMaxHP`/`!IsDead`). Team is read through the EXISTING `ITeamAgent::GetTeamId` — never duplicated onto this interface. `ACastle` does NOT implement it (it keeps its delegate bar). `AGoldNode` does NOT implement it (not damageable — no bar).
- **WidgetComponent subclass:** `UHealthBarComponent` (a `UWidgetComponent` subclass), files `HealthBarComponent.h/.cpp` in `Source/GitClaudeUnrealTest/Siegebound/`. Exactly ONE instance is added in-constructor to each of the three base classes above, named `HPBarWidget` (reuses the `<Purpose>Widget` component-name convention and mirrors `ACastle::HPBarWidget`); subclasses (AMinerUnit, ATower, ABarracks, ADeepMine) inherit it automatically. The component owns: the soft widget class, the poll timer, the show/hide (hide-at-full) logic, and the one-time team-tint push. EditDefaultsOnly tunables (so BPs can tune with no code): `TSoftClassPtr<UUserWidget> HealthBarWidgetClass` (default `/Game/UI/WBP_UnitHealthBar`, null-safe — missing asset = silent no bar, never a crash), `float PollInterval` (default 0.15), `bool bShowHealthBar` (default true — per-actor/per-BP opt-out for anything a playtest flags as clutter, e.g. miners), `float BarHeightZ` (relative Z above the actor; default 120 units — buildings/hero BPs may raise it), `FLinearColor BlueBarColor` / `RedBarColor` (default to the §6 palette / `MI_TeamColor` linear values — Blue (0.05,0.30,1.00), Red (1.00,0.10,0.05); tint is data, never hardcoded in logic). WidgetComponent space = **Screen** (the `ACastle::HPBarWidget` precedent). DrawSize small (units read at ~150 px per the card-art bar) — pin ~90×12.
- **Widget C++ base + UMG asset:** `UUnitHealthBarWidget` (`UUserWidget` subclass), files `UnitHealthBarWidget.h/.cpp`; the UMG asset `WBP_UnitHealthBar` in Content/UI/ (`/Game/UI/WBP_UnitHealthBar`) is reparented to it (the `U<Name>Widget` ↔ `WBP_<Name>` law above). Two BlueprintImplementableEvents, **float params only** (MCP cannot author enum/struct BP params — CONVENTIONS widget rule): `OnHPChanged(float CurrentHP, float MaxHP)` — WBP implements it as ProgressBar `SetPercent(CurrentHP / MaxHP)` guarding `MaxHP > 0` (identical contract to `UCastleHealthBarWidget::OnHPChanged`, so `WBP_CastleHealthBar` is the fastest donor to duplicate); and `SetTeamColor(float R, float G, float B)` — WBP tints the FILL brush from the pushed RGB. The component drives BOTH: it seeds `SetTeamColor` once at init from the owner's team, and calls `OnHPChanged` each poll while the bar is shown.
- **Behavior law (ALWAYS-VISIBLE while alive, team-tinted fill) — REVERSED 2026-07-09 by Jonathan (playtest override of the shipped hide-at-full law from commit 9a8a75f):** the bar is VISIBLE the ENTIRE time the actor is alive (and opted-in via `bShowHealthBar`), at FULL HP included, and the FILL reflects `CurrentHP / MaxHP` live — it DROPS as the actor takes damage, exactly as a health bar is expected to behave (Jonathan verbatim: *"I want the health bar to be visible the entire time … see it drop as the character takes damage … it should drop, as you typically expect with a health bar"*). It is HIDDEN only on death/destruction (the component polls `IsHealthBarActorAlive`) and when `bShowHealthBar` is false. This SUPERSEDES the original M5.5 rule (bar shown only while `CurrentHP < MaxHP − epsilon`); the `HealthBarFullEpsilon` full-HP term is RETIRED from the show/hide decision (the show-gate becomes `bShowHealthBar && bAlive`). Team tints the FILL (blue friendly / red enemy per §6), fixed regardless of HP — the bar communicates team by color and damage by length; it never recolors green→red. Applies to BOTH teams. Donor unchanged: `/Game/UI/WBP_CastleHealthBar`; never author the tree from scratch (template-donor rule). Implemented by TASK-122 (component) + TASK-123 (WBP render).
  - **Bar colors (ITEM B, added 2026-07-10, Jonathan loop-1 playtest request: *"make the part of the bar that shows the health red if they are enemies and blue if they are friendly, and the background of the bar grey"*):** the FILL is team-tinted DATA (unchanged law): `UHealthBarComponent::BlueBarColor` (0.05, 0.30, 1.00) friendly / `RedBarColor` (1.00, 0.10, 0.05) enemy, pushed once via `SetTeamColor` → the WBP's `SetFillColorAndOpacity(Bar, …)` — never hardcoded in WBP logic. The fill's `fillImage.tintColor` MUST be neutral white (1,1,1 = identity multiply) so the pushed team color shows through undimmed. The BACKGROUND / unfilled TRACK brush is a FIXED neutral GREY authored ON `WBP_UnitHealthBar` — a STATIC widget style (like the bar's DrawSize / HitTestInvisible / no-baked-text), NOT per-actor data: it never varies by team or actor, so it is deliberately NOT a runtime-pushed C++ param (a background-color param would over-engineer a constant). **Manager ruling (delegated call): the grey lives as an authored WBP brush, RECORDED here as the canonical value** — dark neutral grey ~ linear (0.03, 0.03, 0.03) at ~0.7 alpha, which MUST contrast clearly with BOTH the blue and the red fill. This closes the round-1 contrast miss: TASK-123's WBP audit found the authored `Bar` `FillColorAndOpacity` AND `fillImage.tintColor` both set to WHITE, so a draining fill was near-invisible on a white/near-white track (the likely REAL round-1 bug — the C++ may only have been harmless hardening; see TASK-122 ITEM-A QA mandate). Implemented by TASK-127.
  - **OPEN QUESTION (flagged for Jonathan 2026-07-09, NOT silently decided) — does the `bShowHealthBar` opt-out survive?** The per-BP `bShowHealthBar` EditDefaultsOnly opt-out (default `true` — suppresses clutter on a flagged type, e.g. miners) is KEPT under the reversed law. Rationale: it is ORTHOGONAL to hide-at-full — it gates WHETHER a type carries a bar at all, not WHEN a bar shows — and always-on bars make a per-type opt-out MORE valuable, not less (60+ always-visible bars > 60+ damage-only bars in on-screen clutter, §6). Manager recommendation: KEEP, default `true`. If Jonathan wants literally EVERY actor's bar always-on with no exceptions, TASK-122 can drop the opt-out — his call; the recommended path ships either way (non-blocking).

## Deck-builder & saved decks (M6)
Added 2026-07-09 (TASK-113..121; GDD §7 deck-builder screen / §4 28-card pool + per-card MaxCopies / §8 average-cost guide / §9 milestone 6). The deck-builder READS/WRITES the EXISTING deck system — it never reinvents it. Audit of the existing infra (do NOT duplicate): `UDeckComponent` (DeckComponent.h/.cpp) builds the draw pile from the `DeckCount` column of `/Game/Data/DT_Cards` in `BuildAndShuffle()`; BOTH `ASiegePlayerController` and `ASiegeBotController` own a `DeckComponent` subobject named `DeckComponent` and call `BuildAndShuffle()` at match start / `ResetDeck()` on Play Again. Today every controller gets the SAME deck (the DeckCount column). M6 ADDS a per-controller override path; the DeckCount column stays the fallback.
- **Deck data types (C++):** header-only `Source/GitClaudeUnrealTest/Siegebound/DeckTypes.h` (the `TeamId.h` one-concept-header precedent):
  - `FDeckCardEntry` (USTRUCT, BlueprintType) — `FName CardID` + `int32 Count`.
  - `FDeckList` (USTRUCT, BlueprintType) — `FString DeckName` + `TArray<FDeckCardEntry> Cards`; helper `int32 TotalCount() const` (sum of entry Counts).
  - `static constexpr int32 SiegeLegalDeckSize = 50;` — the GDD §3.4 legal deck size, referenced by the validator and `UDeckComponent`.
- **Deck legality + average-cost library:** `UDeckLibrary` (UBlueprintFunctionLibrary), `Source/.../DeckLibrary.h/.cpp` — the ONE home for deck-rule math, shared by the deck-builder widget, the DeckComponent build path, and the bot. Data-driven from DT_Cards, never hardcoded (§3.0):
  - `static bool IsDeckLegal(const UDataTable* CardTable, const FDeckList& Deck, FString& OutReason)` — **⚖️ AMENDED IN PLACE 2026-08-28 (CARD-UNCAP, `UNCAP-§3`; signature BYTE-IDENTICAL):** true iff every entry's CardID exists in DT_Cards, every entry Count is `>= 0`, and `TotalCount() == SiegeLegalDeckSize` (50, EXACT). The per-CardID aggregate `MaxCopies` check (and its RunningCounts map + "the cap is %d (MaxCopies)" reason) is REMOVED — the relaxation is strictly WIDENING, so every previously legal deck stays legal. `OutReason` carries the first violation for HUD/log. Null table ⇒ false + reason. *(Superseded wording, for the record: "every entry Count is in `[0..that row's MaxCopies]`".)*
  - `static float GetDeckAverageCost(const UDataTable* CardTable, const FDeckList& Deck)` — sum(Cost×Count)/TotalCount (§8 guide — display only, no hard rule). 0 for an empty deck.
- **Player saved decks — SaveGame (cross-session persistence + cross-level handoff):** `USiegeDeckSaveGame` (USaveGame subclass), `Source/.../SiegeDeckSaveGame.h/.cpp` — `TArray<FDeckList> SavedDecks` + `FString ActiveDeckName`. Persisted with `UGameplayStatics::SaveGameToSlot/LoadGameFromSlot` to the FIXED slot name `"SiegeDecks"` (const, character-for-character), user index 0 → `Saved/SaveGames/SiegeDecks.sav`. Chosen over a DataAsset (not runtime-writable in a packaged build) and a hand-rolled `.json` (SaveGame is the idiomatic runtime-writable, cross-session, package-safe store). No file / unresolvable ⇒ empty deck list + empty ActiveDeckName (null-safe) → the match falls back to the curated DeckCount default. The SaveGame is ALSO the menu→match handoff: no deck is passed through the level-open URL.
- **DeckComponent override path (additive, backward-compatible):** `void UDeckComponent::SetPendingDeckList(const FDeckList& Deck)` sets a guarded pending list; `BuildAndShuffle()` uses the pending list when it is set AND `UDeckLibrary::IsDeckLegal` passes, else falls back to the existing DeckCount-column build (UNCHANGED behavior — the empty/illegal/unset case is exactly today's path, so nothing breaks). The pending list PERSISTS across `ResetDeck()`/Play Again (same match keeps the same deck). No new HP/gold coupling — pure card-flow, as today.
- **Curated default deck = the `DeckCount` column of `Docs/Data/cards.csv`** (re-authored in TASK-115 to a legal, intentional 50-card starter deck that SUPERSEDES the M4/M5 test spread; still `sum(DeckCount)==50`, each `DeckCount<=MaxCopies` — **the second clause dissolved 2026-08-28 by CARD-UNCAP (`UNCAP-§2`): only `sum==50` still binds; no data edit follows, the shipped composition already satisfies both**). This single edit satisfies GDD §9-6 "replace default deck with a legal curated one." It is BOTH the deck-builder's initial/"reset to default" template AND the match fallback when no legal saved active deck exists. cards.csv stays the single source of truth (§3.0).
- **Bot decks — 2 distinct, author-controlled:** `UPROPERTY(EditDefaultsOnly, Category="Siegebound|Bot") TArray<FDeckList> BotDecks` on `ASiegeBotController` (exactly TWO distinct legal curated decks, C++ constructor defaults, tunable per-BP — a deck composition is content, not a per-card stat, so it is NOT a CSV column; mirrors the mechanic-rule-as-UPROPERTY precedent). At spawn the bot RANDOMLY picks one of the two (`FMath::RandRange`), logs the choice on `LogSiegeBot` (one line, grep-able like the §4 decision trace), and pushes it via `SetPendingDeckList`; a missing/illegal BotDecks entry ⇒ fall back to the DeckCount default (null-safe).
- **Deck-builder widget:** `UDeckBuilderWidget` (UUserWidget subclass), `Source/.../DeckBuilderWidget.h/.cpp`; UMG asset `WBP_DeckBuilder` at `/Game/UI/WBP_DeckBuilder` reparented to it (the `U<Name>Widget` ↔ `WBP_<Name>` law). The C++ base owns ALL model/logic; the WBP is layout + calls. BlueprintCallable/Pure model API (UObject/struct returns allowed on these, unlike BIEs): `AddCopy(FName CardID)`, `RemoveCopy(FName CardID)`, `GetCountOf(FName CardID) const`, `GetTotalCount() const`, `GetAverageCost() const`, `IsCurrentDeckLegal() const`, `LoadDefaultDeck()` (seed working deck from the DeckCount curated default), `SaveDeckAs(const FString& Name)`, `LoadDeck(const FString& Name)`, `GetSavedDeckNames() const` (TArray<FString>), `SetActiveDeck(const FString& Name)`. BIEs are float/int/bool/FString params ONLY (MCP cannot author enum/struct BP params — the widget rule): e.g. `OnDeckModelChanged()` (widget re-reads the getters — seed-then-bind), `OnDeckSlotCountChanged(FString CardID, int32 Count)`. Donor: duplicate an existing multi-element widget (`/Game/UI/WBP_CardHand` or `/Game/UI/WBP_MainMenu`) — never author the tree from scratch (template-donor rule). MCP CAN author full widget trees (proven TASK-041 6-slot hand, TASK-111 health bar).
- **Deck-builder card tiles = the hand's card-face composition (added 2026-07-09, Jonathan playtest request: *"physical cards displayed … same displays … for the actual match … for now"*):** the per-card tiles in the browser grid are `WBP_DeckCardTile` (`/Game/UI/WBP_DeckCardTile`, created in TASK-118). They RENDER AS ACTUAL CARDS using the SAME card-face treatment as the in-match hand (`WBP_CardHand`): the `T_CardArt_<CardID>` texture as the BACKGROUND layer, with DisplayName + Cost overlaid legibly on top ("Card artwork (hand UI)" → Face composition law). **NO shared card-face sub-widget exists to extract** — the hand's face is INLINED per-slot inside `WBP_CardHand` (driven by its `OnHandSlotUpdated` BIE + `GetCardArtTexture` resolver); per Jonathan's explicit "for now" stopgap the composition is REPRODUCED in `WBP_DeckCardTile`, NOT factored out into a shared widget (a shared-card-face extraction is deferred to a later polish pass). **No new C++:** the tile pulls everything from the EXISTING `UDeckBuilderWidget` resolvers — `GetCardArtTexture(CardID)` (art), `GetCardDisplayName(CardID)`, `GetCardCost(CardID)`, plus `GetCountOf(CardID)` / `GetCardMaxCopies(CardID)` for the counter + cap-grey — and keeps its existing +/− (`AddCopy`/`RemoveCopy`) and count wiring (TASK-118). Additive-only to `WBP_DeckCardTile`; `WBP_CardHand` and `WBP_DeckBuilder`'s grid/legality logic are NOT disturbed. Implemented by TASK-125.
  - **Above-card in-deck copy count (added 2026-07-10, Jonathan sharpened request: *"add a number above each card that shows how many you have of it in the current deck build"*):** each tile shows a PROMINENT number ABOVE the card face = the copies of that card in the IN-PROGRESS working deck. Data source is the EXISTING resolver `UDeckBuilderWidget::GetCountOf(CardID)` (confirmed to read `WorkingDeck`, the deck being edited — NOT the saved deck; DeckBuilderWidget.cpp), so this is NO new C++. The count element is the tile's existing `CountText` TextBlock (TASK-118 — today rendered as "count/max" in the bottom `HBox[− CountText +]`) REPOSITIONED above the card and restyled to the plain in-deck count, OR a new sibling TextBlock named `CopyCountText`; either way driven by `GetCountOf`. The "/MaxCopies" ratio is dropped above the card (the "+"-greys-at-cap already signals the cap). **Legibility is law, not decoration:** the count and the name/cost overlay MUST read clearly ON TOP of the card art (contrast strip / outline / drop shadow) — a number present-but-invisible against the art is the same defect class as the M5.5 white-fill-on-white-track bug. On-screen legibility + the count updating live on +/− are human WATCH items when Slate pixels can't be captured headless (never inferred from the widget tree).
- **Deck-builder navigation:** the deck-builder shows as a WIDGET OVERLAY on `L_MainMenu` (no new level, no new game mode). The EXISTING greyed "Deck Builder" button on `/Game/UI/WBP_MainMenu` (authored disabled in TASK-049) is named `Btn_DeckBuilder` — reconcile with the actual name TASK-049 gave it; ENABLE it and wire `OnClicked` to remove `WBP_MainMenu` and add `WBP_DeckBuilder` to the viewport. `WBP_DeckBuilder` carries its own `Btn_Back` (return to `WBP_MainMenu`) and `Btn_PlayWithDeck` (enabled only when `IsCurrentDeckLegal()`; sets the active deck + `ASiegeGameMode::StartMatch`). Additive-only edits to `WBP_MainMenu` — do NOT disturb the Play-vs-Bot / Btn_Sandbox bindings (TASK-072 caution).

## Deck-builder card details — click-a-card "how it works" (2026-07-23)
Added 2026-07-23 (TASK-268..272; Jonathan directive verbatim: *"lets change the deck builder interface a bit. Make it to where when you click on the display for a card it displays a detailed description on how the card works."*). EXTENDS the M6 deck-builder section above — it does not replace any of it. **Every M6 rule survives untouched:** per-card `MaxCopies` enforcement, the live x/50 counter (`TotalText`), the §8 average-cost guide (`AvgText`), deck-legal-only-at-exactly-50 (`PlayBtn` gate), save/load/active-deck, and the TASK-125 physical-card tile face. **⚖️ CARD-UNCAP rider (2026-08-28, `UNCAP-§`):** the per-card `MaxCopies` enforcement named in this section (and every "cap-grey"/"greys-at-cap" mention in this and the M6 section above) is SUPERSEDED — the deck cap is abolished; `GetCardMaxCopies` becomes a compat shim returning `SiegeLegalDeckSize` so the WBP cap-grey wiring survives without a .uasset edit (`UNCAP-§4`). Everything else in these sections still binds.

- **ADD/REMOVE DOES NOT MOVE (manager ruling).** The tile's existing `AddBtn` "+" / `RemoveBtn` "−" (TASK-118, kept in TASK-125's bottom caption plate) stay EXACTLY where they are, still calling `UDeckBuilderWidget::AddCopy` / `RemoveCopy`, still cap-greying via `SetIsEnabled(AddBtn, GetCountOf < GetCardMaxCopies)`. There is NO whole-tile click handler today (the card art is `SelfHitTestInvisible` precisely so it never eats +/− clicks), so "click the display" is a NEW, previously-unbound gesture — not a conflict. Details-on-click is therefore purely ADDITIVE.
- **The new click target:** `Btn_CardFace` on `/Game/UI/WBP_DeckCardTile` — a transparent, style-less Button covering the card FACE (art region), inserted as the **FIRST/bottom-most child of the tile's root Overlay** so the count plate and the caption plate (which carry `+`/`−`) sit ON TOP and win hit-testing. Handler `OnCardFacePressed` → `OwnerBuilder->SelectCardForDetails(CardID)` (IsValid-guarded, the `OnAddPressed`/`OnRemovePressed` shape). It must never call `AddCopy`/`RemoveCopy`.
- **Selection model lives in C++** (the M6 "C++ base owns ALL model/logic" law). On `UDeckBuilderWidget`:
  - `UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable) void SelectCardForDetails(FName CardID)` — stores `SelectedDetailCardID`, fires `OnCardDetailsRequested(CardID.ToString())`. An unknown/None CardID clears the selection instead (and still fires, with an empty string).
  - `UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable) void ClearCardDetails()` — clears + fires with an empty string.
  - `UFUNCTION(BlueprintPure) FName GetSelectedDetailCardID() const`.
  - `UFUNCTION(BlueprintImplementableEvent) void OnCardDetailsRequested(const FString& CardID)` — BIE params stay float/int/bool/byte/FString ONLY (the widget rule). The WBP re-reads the getters; it never receives a struct.
  - Private `UPROPERTY(Transient) FName SelectedDetailCardID`.
- **The description is GENERATED FROM DT_Cards, never authored per card (binding ruling — anti-drift).** `UFUNCTION(BlueprintPure) FString GetCardDescription(FName CardID) const` composes a multi-line player-facing string from the row's structured fields. **NO `Description` CSV column is added, and the existing `Notes` column is NEVER surfaced to the player** — `Notes` stays "designer notes; not used by gameplay code" (it carries GDD/implementation refs like "(GDD 3.0)" / "UPROPERTY on ADeepMine" and is already PROVABLY STALE: the `Lightning` row says "in 400" while its `AoERadius` is 700). A balance pass is pending in the Standing backlog; generated text auto-survives it, authored prose would not.
  - **Composition order (omit any line whose source field is 0/None/not applicable):** (1) identity line `"<Type> · Cost <Cost> gold"` with Type prose Unit/Building/Economy/Spell/Hero Upgrade/Utility — **⚖️ AMENDED 2026-08-28 (CARD-UNCAP, `UNCAP-§5`): the `· Max <MaxCopies> per deck` clause is DELETED; with the cap abolished it would state a rule the game does not implement — exactly this section's truth-law FAIL class. The hero-upgrade RULES-tail stack-cap line ("up to %d stacks", fed by `MaxCopies`) is UNCHANGED — still true, still data-driven**; (2) blank; (3) STAT block from `HP`/`Damage`(+`AoERadius` splash)/`Cadence`/`Range`(+melee vs homing-projectile per `bRanged`)/`MinRange`/`Speed`; (4) blank; (5) RULES block — one plain-English line per applicable clause, drawn from the glossary below.
  - **Glossary clauses** (each interpolates the row's OWN numbers wherever the number exists in the row): `bCharge`, `bSlayer`, `bSuicide`, `SwarmCount`, `ChainTargets`/`ChainFalloff`, spawner (`SpawnCardID`/`SpawnInterval`/`Lifetime` — resolve the spawned card's `DisplayName`, never print a raw CardID), `SpellEffect` (all five values), spell delivery (resolve `Auto` through the EXISTING `USpellLibrary::GetEffectiveDelivery` — never re-implement the per-effect default), `Profile` (Siege / Support prose; Standard omitted), and castle-damage scaling.
  - **Glossary-mirror rule:** magnitudes that are NOT CSV columns because they are mechanic rules living as UPROPERTY defaults (Charge 2 s / 2×, Slayer 150 HP / 2×, castle scaling 50 % projectile & spell / 200 % Siege, Deep Mine +2 gold/s, Masons 300 HP over 10 s, hero-upgrade magnitudes, Rally) appear as **named string constants in ONE place in `DeckBuilderWidget.cpp`**, each with a `// mirrors <Class>::<Property>` comment. Changing that gameplay value obliges updating the constant. Anything in a CSV column is read from the row and NEVER hardcoded (§3.0).
  - **Truth law (QA gate):** every rules line must correspond to behavior the SHIPPING code actually implements — the author verifies each clause against the owning class before writing it. If a clause cannot be verified, OMIT it. A description that states a rule the game does not implement is a FAIL, not a nit. No GDD section refs, no class/property names, no CSV column names in player-facing text. Target ≤ ~12 lines per card.
  - Unknown/None CardID ⇒ empty string (the WBP shows its own static hint); missing table ⇒ empty string, logged once (reuse the existing `bWarnedMissingTable` / `WarnedMissingRowIDs` spam guards). Never a crash.
- **The details view = a NON-MODAL SIDE PANEL inside `/Game/UI/WBP_DeckBuilder`** (manager ruling: not a modal, not an expanded tile — the player must be able to click card after card and keep using `+`/`−` while reading). **NO new WidgetBlueprint asset is created**: the panel is built in `WBP_DeckBuilder`'s existing runtime-constructed tree (TASK-118 technique). ⚠ **A new WidgetBlueprint may NEVER be produced by duplicate+REPARENT** — that has silently broken RUNTIME repaint in this project (design-time looked fine; ~9 wasted fixes). Build fresh or build inline.
  - Element names, EXACT: `DetailsPanel` (the panel's root container), `DetailsArtBorder` (card art, driven by the existing `GetCardArtTexture`), `DetailsNameText` (`GetCardDisplayName`), `DetailsCostText` (`GetCardCost`), `DetailsBodyText` (`GetCardDescription` — the multi-line body, `AutoWrapText` ON), `DetailsHintText` (static empty-state hint, shown when no card is selected), `Btn_DetailsClose` (clears the selection via `ClearCardDetails`).
  - The grid keeps its full card inventory: since the panel takes horizontal space, the 28-tile `WrapBox` is wrapped in a ScrollBox named `GridScroll` (closes the TASK-118 flag #3 overflow risk). Nothing else in `WBP_DeckBuilder` is disturbed — `TotalText`/`AvgText`/`SavedNamesText`/`NameInput`/`PlayBtn`/Back/Save/Load/Reset bindings stay byte-identical.
  - Legibility is law, not decoration (the M5.5 white-fill-on-white-track defect class): the body text sits on an opaque/dark backing plate, never directly on card art.
- **Verification law:** UMG render/interaction correctness here closes on a **pixel or human check**, never on property/tree readback alone — MCP readback has repeatedly passed on visually-broken UMG in this project. The strongest available MACHINE evidence for the description text itself is a headless dump of `GetCardDescription` for all 28 CardIDs (best-effort `-run=pythonscript` route); QA additionally reads the composed strings against `Docs/Data/cards.csv` by hand.

## Input-mode ownership (level-travel law)
Added 2026-07-07 (TASK-074 bugfix chain). Input-routing state set via `APlayerController::SetInputMode` lives partly on the persistent `UGameViewportClient` and can SURVIVE `UGameplayStatics::OpenLevel*` travel — **a level must never trust the input posture it inherits from whoever traveled it in.** Each level's controller establishes its own posture at startup:
- **L_Arena / `ASiegePlayerController`:** match posture is GameOnly free-look + hidden cursor (M2 TASK-023 ruling), composed by `ApplyCursorInputState()` — the only cursor owners are placement mode, the Alt-held `IA_UICursor`, and `HandleMatchEnd`'s UIOnly end screen. The controller normalizes to this posture at `BeginPlay` (TASK-074) instead of assuming engine defaults.
- **L_MainMenu / `BP_MenuGameMode`:** menu posture is UIOnly + visible cursor (TASK-049) so `WBP_MainMenu` buttons stay clickable.
- The static travel entries (`ASiegeGameMode::StartMatch` / `::StartSandboxMatch`) stay posture-agnostic — they only open the level and never set input modes.

## Dev / test tooling (non-gameplay affordances)
- **Capture lane note (MCP/editor, TASK-249):** `CaptureViewport.captureTransform` overrides work in SIE but NOT in possessed-pawn PIE — SIE is the capture lane for framed shots. Evidence: handoffs/TASK-249.md.
Names for developer/test-bench features that are NOT GDD content and NOT part of any milestone. They must not disturb the shipping flow; every one is additive.
- **Sandbox (No Bot) mode** (added 2026-07-05, TASK-071/072) — opens `L_Arena` with the full card roster but **no enemy AI**, as a calm test bench for the 22-card roster. Mechanism is a **level-open URL option**, deliberately NOT a GameInstance (no `USiegeGameInstance`, no `GameInstanceClass` config change):
  - **Option token:** `Sandbox=1`, parsed with `UGameplayStatics::HasOption(OptionsString, TEXT("Sandbox"))`. The token string is `Sandbox` — code and any future consumer must use it character-for-character.
  - **Game-mode latch:** `ASiegeGameMode` reads the option in `InitGame` into a `bool bSandboxMatch` (persists for the life of the `L_Arena` world, so `PlayAgain` stays sandbox).
  - **Bot gate:** `ASiegeGameMode::SpawnBot()` early-returns when `bSandboxMatch` is true — no `ASiegeBotController` is spawned and no Red bot `ASiegePlayerState` is created. The Red `ACastle` (`Castle_Red`) remains as a static target dummy; Blue units/buildings still march on it.
  - **Menu entry:** `static void ASiegeGameMode::StartSandboxMatch(const UObject* WorldContextObject)` — mirrors `StartMatch` but appends the `Sandbox=1` option to `OpenLevelBySoftObjectPtr`. `StartMatch` (Play vs Bot) keeps its exact signature and behavior — untouched.
  - **Generous economy:** `UPROPERTY(EditDefaultsOnly) int32 SandboxStartingGold` on `ASiegeGameMode`, default `9999` (`// dev sandbox — full roster freely playable`), granted to the Blue player once at match start when `bSandboxMatch` is true, via the existing player-state gold API (never hardcode a gold mutation that bypasses it). Normal gold rate otherwise.
  - **Menu button:** `Btn_Sandbox` on `/Game/UI/WBP_MainMenu`, label text `"Sandbox (No Bot)"`, `OnClicked → ASiegeGameMode::StartSandboxMatch`. Placed as an additive sibling next to the existing Play-vs-Bot button (which calls `StartMatch`); the existing button and its binding are not disturbed.

- **Debug exec cheats (headless-verification affordance, added 2026-07-09, TASK-121):** `USiegeCheatManager` (`UCheatManager` subclass), `Source/GitClaudeUnrealTest/Siegebound/SiegeCheatManager.h/.cpp`, set as `ASiegePlayerController::CheatClass` in the controller constructor. The engine instantiates a `UCheatManager` ONLY in non-shipping builds with cheats enabled (never in Shipping), so these commands cannot leak into a shipped game — additive and non-shipping by construction. `UFUNCTION(exec)` dev commands, each null-safe and routed through the SAME shipping code paths (never a raw field write / never a bespoke spawn): `SummonTestUnit(FString CardID, bool bRed)` (spawns a card actor for the given team via the existing spawn path — drives PIE without card input on a locked desktop), `ApplyTestDamage(float Amount)` (applies damage to the actor under the crosshair / nearest enemy through the normal TakeDamage path — induces the health-bar + castle-HP changes build-master cannot otherwise trigger headless), `AddTestGold(int32 Amount)` (tops up the Blue player through the `ASiegePlayerState` gold API). Purpose: close the recurring locked-desktop WATCH debt (TASK-076/112 doctrine — no `SendInput`, so the Blue player cannot play cards during PIE) so build-master can fully drive verification headlessly. This is a dev/test affordance, NOT GDD content and NOT part of any milestone's playable slice.

## ⚖️ ACCOUNTS — local-first player accounts · profile-scoped saves · the cloud-backend ruling (2026-08-16) — namespace **`ACC-§N`**

Added 2026-08-16 (batch ACCOUNTS, TASK-599..610). **Jonathan's request, verbatim:** *"I want to add the ability to create an account that saves data. This can be a "login" button in the main menu that leads to a "create account" button and a "log into existing account" button. Eventually I want to make the accounts created saved in the cloud so that way people can log in from any device. These accounts will be able to track different deck builds that the user has created and saved, any setting adjustments, etc. Come up with a plan for how we can save that data in the cloud. If we need to use a website I would prefer to use github pages since I already have a github account with a website using github pages. If there is another method that you think is easier to manage and store this data in the could let me know."*

**The shape: THREE PHASES.** Phase 1 (this batch, fully decomposed) = a **LOCAL-FIRST account shell, backend-agnostic** — the UI he described, a profile model, and per-profile persistence of decks + settings layered on the EXISTING `USaveGame` systems. Phase 2 (gated one-liners, ⛔ no IDs) = cloud sync, pending his backend ruling. Phase 3 = cross-device polish one-liners. ⭐ **Phase 1 works fully offline and Phase 2 bolts on without UI rework — that is the design constraint, not an accident.**

### ACC-§0 ⛔ THE GITHUB-PAGES RULING — RULED OUT AS THE DATA STORE, ON THE RECORD, WITH THE MECHANISM

- ⛔ **GitHub Pages CANNOT be the accounts backend.** It is **static file hosting**: no server code, no database, no secure per-user auth. The only way a game client could WRITE to it is a GitHub API token **shipped inside the game binary** — which any player can extract and use to read/write EVERY account. That is not a hardening problem; it is structural. ⛔ **No task may propose a GH-Pages/gist/repo-commit data store; this ruling is cited, not re-argued.**
- ✅ **GitHub Pages MAY host a companion WEBSITE later** (landing page, account-portal front-end that talks to the real backend over HTTPS). Site ≠ store.
- **DEFAULT BACKEND FOR PHASE 2: Supabase** — hosted Postgres + built-in email/password auth (JWTs) + row-level security (each account reaches only its own rows) + a plain HTTPS/JSON REST API that UE's built-in `FHttpModule` + `Json` modules call with **no third-party SDK**. Free tier ample at this scale, and Jonathan's Claude environment already has a **Supabase connector wired**, so agents can create/manage the project, tables and RLS policies directly when Phase 2 opens. **Alternatives on record:** Firebase, PlayFab (both viable, more SDK friction), EOS (Epic-native, but its auth model fits Epic accounts/device IDs, not simple email/password). ⚠️ **FLAGGED A1 — the backend choice is JONATHAN'S, owed before Phase 2 decomposes. Nothing in Phase 1 depends on it.**
- ⚠️ **Environmental caveat, recorded now:** Norton MITMs HTTPS on this machine (the HF precedent) — `*.supabase.co` will likely need a Norton exclusion when Phase 2 goes live. **A dev-machine artifact, not a product defect, and a Jonathan hand-step.**
- ⭐ **DATED AMENDMENT 2026-08-23 — A1 IS RULED: SUPABASE (Jonathan, verbatim in ACC-§10).** The flagged default stood and the flag is discharged. Phase-2 law = **ACC-§10..§15** below; the GH-Pages ruling above is UNCHANGED.

### ACC-§1 ⛔ THE GUEST-DEFAULT LAW — LOGIN GATES NOTHING, AND THE ACCOUNTLESS GAME IS BYTE-IDENTICAL

- **Guest is the default.** With no account created and no login performed, every shipped flow behaves EXACTLY as today: decks read/write slot `"SiegeDecks"`, settings read/write slot `"SiegeSettings"`, all menus work. ⛔ **No task may gate Play, Sandbox, Deck Builder, Multiplayer or Settings behind login.**
- **Login surface = the MAIN MENU ONLY in Phase 1.** No in-match login/logout, no identity change during a live match (it would swap save slots mid-session and raise M8 questions nobody has answered). The subsystem crosses levels, so an in-match entry later is one widget task.
- **The guest slots are never mutated by account code.** Creating a profile SEED-COPIES the guest data into the new profile's slots once (ACC-§3; FLAGGED A6, default TAKEN); the guest originals stay untouched forever.

### ACC-§2 ⛔ THE HONEST-CREDENTIAL LAW — PHASE 1 CREDENTIALS ARE A CONVENIENCE, ⛔ NOT SECURITY, AND NO ARTIFACT MAY SAY OTHERWISE

- Phase 1 stores a **salted hash** locally: `CredentialHashHex = hex(FSHA1::HashBuffer(UTF8(CredentialSaltHex + ":" + Password)))`, salt = a fresh `FGuid` in `Digits` hex per profile. This stops shoulder-surfing and accidental plaintext on disk. **It is NOT a security boundary: anyone with disk access can edit `SiegeAccounts.sav`.**
- ⛔ **No task, handoff, QA report, or code comment may describe Phase-1 auth as "secure," "encrypted," or "protected."** The honest phrase is **"local convenience credential — real auth is the Phase-2 backend's job"** (Supabase GoTrue does server-side bcrypt; the client never stores a password).
- ⛔ **The plaintext password is NEVER persisted and NEVER logged** — not in the save game, not on `LogSiegeAccount`, not in a handoff. ✅ **QA CRITERION: grep the diff for any write/log of the password parameter and report ZERO.**

### ACC-§3 THE PROFILE MODEL + THE SLOT-NAME LAW

| Thing | Exact value |
|---|---|
| Profile identity | `FGuid ProfileId` — never the display name |
| Slot suffix derivation | `ProfileId.ToString(EGuidFormats::Digits)` — 32 hex chars, filename-safe; helper `USiegeAccountSubsystem::MakeProfileSlotSuffix` is the ONE implementation |
| Account registry slot | **`"SiegeAccounts"`**, user index **0** ⇒ `Saved/SaveGames/SiegeAccounts.sav` |
| Profile deck slot | **`"SiegeDecks_<Digits>"`** (guest: bare `"SiegeDecks"` — unchanged) |
| Profile settings slot | **`"SiegeSettings_<Digits>"`** (guest: bare `"SiegeSettings"` — unchanged) |
| Display name rules | trimmed; 3–24 chars; unique case-insensitive among local profiles; login lookup case-insensitive |
| Password rule (P1) | ≥ 4 chars, non-empty — a convenience bar, not a policy (ACC-§2) |

- ⛔ **A slot name is NEVER derived from the display name** (users type anything; filenames + collisions + renames).
- **Seed-copy on create (FLAGGED A6, default TAKEN):** `CreateAccount` — after registering the profile and making it active — copies the existing guest `"SiegeDecks"` / `"SiegeSettings"` payloads into the new profile's slots IF the guest slots exist (load → re-save under the profile slot). Once, at create only, never at login. His existing decks follow him into his first account; guest slots untouched.
- **Existing save CLASSES are NOT rewritten.** `USiegeDeckSaveGame` and `USiegeSettingsSaveGame` keep their exact fields; profile scoping is 100 % slot-name scoping (ACC-§4).

### ACC-§4 ⛔ THE SEAM LAW — EVERY SLOT NAME RESOLVES THROUGH `USiegeAccountSubsystem`, AND THE CALL-SITE SET IS ENUMERATED, NOT ASSUMED

**Verified first-hand at decomposition (manager, raw grep + read):** the deck slot has ONE definition (`SiegeDeckSaveGame.cpp:7`, `const FString USiegeDeckSaveGame::SlotName = TEXT("SiegeDecks")`) and exactly **FIVE consumer sites in TWO files** — `DeckBuilderWidget.cpp:589` (SaveDeckAs) · `:677` (SetActiveDeck) · `:744` (DoesSaveGameExist) · `:752` (LoadGameFromSlot) · `SiegePlayerController.cpp:253` (match-side active-deck load). The settings slot already funnels through ONE choke point: `USiegeSettingsSubsystem::ResolveSlotName()` (`SiegeSettingsSubsystem.cpp:177` — `SlotNameOverride.IsEmpty() ? SettingsSlotName : SlotNameOverride`), with a shipped test seam `SetSlotNameForAutomationTests` (`SiegeSettingsSubsystem.h:175`).

- **The seam:** `USiegeAccountSubsystem::GetDeckSlotName()` / `GetSettingsSlotName()` return the profile-scoped slot when a profile is active, the bare guest constant otherwise. **Fail-safe: an unresolvable account subsystem ⇒ the guest constant — today's behavior, never a crash** (the `USiegeDeckSaveGame` null-safety contract).
- **Deck lane (the five sites):** each resolves the slot name **at call time** through the seam. No cached slot, no reload machinery — `GameInstance` outlives `OpenLevel`, so a menu login is naturally live at `SiegePlayerController.cpp:253` when the match loads. `USiegeDeckSaveGame::SlotName` STAYS as the guest constant, byte-identical.
- **Settings lane:** `ResolveSlotName()` precedence becomes **`SlotNameOverride` (tests, unchanged) > account-profile slot > `SettingsSlotName`**. `USiegeSettingsSubsystem::Initialize` gains `Collection.InitializeDependency<USiegeAccountSubsystem>()` (the engine's sanctioned subsystem-ordering route) and subscribes to `OnActiveProfileChanged` → `ReloadForActiveProfile()` (reload via `ResolveSlotName()`, C++ defaults on missing slot, then broadcast the existing `OnSettingsChanged` so `USettingsMenuWidget` refreshes for free). ⚠️ **Dependency direction: Settings depends on Account. `USiegeAccountSubsystem` never includes a Settings header.**
- ⛔ **A literal `"SiegeDecks"` / `"SiegeSettings"` anywhere outside the two guest-constant definition sites and the tests is a QA FAIL.** ✅ **The shipped invariants SURVIVE UNTOUCHED:** `SiegeSettingsTest.cpp:120-121` asserts `SettingsSlotName == "SiegeSettings"` — true before and after, because the guest constant does not move.

### ACC-§5 🔨 THE UI RULING — `UAccountMenuWidget` IS A CODE-AUTHORED TREE. A **NEW, NARROW** EXCEPTION ARGUED ON ITS OWN FACTS — ⛔ NOT AN INHERITANCE FROM THE SETTINGS RULING

⚠️ The settings-lane ruling (§3 of "Settings screen + …", 2026-08-03) is scoped to `USettingsMenuWidget` ONLY and says citing it for another widget is misuse. **So this is a fresh ruling, same facts, equally narrow:** a forms panel (text boxes + buttons); the duplicate+reparent `WBP_` route is this project's most expensive UI failure mode (~9 wasted fixes, runtime repaint silently broken); the fresh-hand-authored route is a Jonathan hand-step not owed for a form. `UAccountMenuWidget` builds its tree in `RebuildWidget()` via `WidgetTree->ConstructWidget<>` and ships with **no `.uasset`**. The five conditions are cloned as QA criteria:
- **(a) SCOPE:** `UAccountMenuWidget` ONLY. Citing this clause for a fourth widget is the same misuse.
- **(b) THE ORDER (the corrected law, already paid for once):** build the tree and set `WidgetTree->RootWidget` **FIRST**, then `return Super::RebuildWidget();` — the TASK-444 shipped shape. ⛔ Anything constructed after Super is discarded (`UserWidget.cpp:1214`) and the widget renders empty **while passing every property readback.** Every child is `UPROPERTY(meta=(BindWidgetOptional))`; construct only if still null.
- **(c) RESERVED NAME:** `/Game/UI/WBP_AccountMenu` may be used by nothing else (✅ verified absent at decomposition). A later authored WBP wins automatically with zero C++ change.
- **(d) CONTRACT:** `BindWidgetOptional` members · `BlueprintCallable` wrappers · FString/int32/bool/uint8-only BIEs — the shipped `USessionMenuWidget`/`USettingsMenuWidget` contract.
- **(e) VERIFICATION IS A HUMAN PIXEL CHECK.** No `.uasset` to read back; MCP readback has repeatedly passed on visually-broken UMG here. Rendering correctness closes on **Jonathan's pixels** (TASK-609), never tree/property readback.

**Pinned child names** (C++ and any future WBP both read this line): `RootPanel` (`UVerticalBox`) · `BackdropBorder` (`UBorder`) · `TitleText` · `StatusText` · `CreateAccountButton` + `CreateAccountLabelText` · `LoginExistingButton` + `LoginExistingLabelText` · `NameInputBox` (`UEditableTextBox`) · `PasswordInputBox` (`UEditableTextBox`, `SetIsPassword(true)`) · `ConfirmPasswordInputBox` (`UEditableTextBox`, `SetIsPassword(true)`) · `SubmitButton` + `SubmitLabelText` · `LogoutButton` + `LogoutLabelText` · `BackButton` + `BackLabelText`.

- ⚠️ **`BackdropBorder` is HIT-TEST **VISIBLE** — a correctness requirement, not styling.** The panel overlays `WBP_MainMenu`; an invisible plate lets clicks fall through to Play/Quit while the panel looks modal (the settings lane's click-through-into-Quit lesson, same geometry).
- **Modes (internal `enum class EAccountMenuMode : uint8` — C++-only, never a BIE param):** `Chooser` (the two buttons Jonathan named: **Create Account** / **Log into existing account**) → `CreateForm` (name + password + confirm) or `LoginForm` (name + password) → `LoggedIn` (StatusText shows `Logged in as <DisplayName>` + Logout + Back). Opening while logged in lands on `LoggedIn`. Submit failures render `OutReason` in `StatusText` — never a crash, never a silent no-op.
- **Navigation = the settings §4 overlay law, cloned:** `Btn_Login` on `WBP_MainMenu` does `CreateWidget(UAccountMenuWidget)` → `AddToViewport(ZOrder 10)`; it does NOT remove the main menu; `Back` removes only itself. **Main-menu order becomes: Play (vs Bot) → Sandbox (No Bot) → Deck Builder → Multiplayer → Settings → Login → Quit** — spliced before the Quit block, shipped idiom character-for-character (font 28, `MakeMargin(24,12,24,12)`, `HAlign_Fill`, granular ops never `write_graph_dsl`, `add_event`-first), pre-existing entries proven character-identical by full-graph DSL diff.

### ACC-§6 NAMING + FOLDER LAW (the cross-task contract)

| Thing | Exact name | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Profile struct | `FSiegeProfileInfo` (USTRUCT, BlueprintType) | in `SiegeAccountSaveGame.h` |
| Account registry | `USiegeAccountSaveGame` (`USaveGame`) — statics `SlotName = "SiegeAccounts"`, `UserIndex = 0` | game — `SiegeAccountSaveGame.h/.cpp` (new) |
| Account owner | `USiegeAccountSubsystem` (`UGameInstanceSubsystem`) | game — `SiegeAccountSubsystem.h/.cpp` (new) |
| Log category | **`LogSiegeAccount`** | declared/defined in `SiegeAccountSubsystem.h/.cpp` |
| Profile-changed delegate | `FOnSiegeActiveProfileChanged` (dynamic multicast, no params) — member `OnActiveProfileChanged` | on `USiegeAccountSubsystem` |

### ACC-§11 ⛔ THE KEY LAW + THE CLIENT TRUST MODEL + THE CONFIG HOME (2026-08-23)

- ⛔ **THE `service_role` KEY NEVER TOUCHES THE REPO, THE GAME BINARY, ANY COMMITTED FILE, ANY FILE THE GAME READS, OR ANY HANDOFF/QA/BOARD TEXT.** It exists only inside Supabase's own dashboard and the orchestrator-held MCP surface. ✅ **QA CRITERION (every P2 diff): grep for `service_role` and for secret-key material (`sb_secret`, JWTs beginning `eyJ` other than the anon key's ruled home) — ZERO hits.**

The anon key is **public-by-design** (RLS is the security boundary, not key secrecy) — ⛔ but it still has exactly ONE ruled home (below); a hardcoded anon key in a `.cpp` is a QA FAIL.
- **THE CONFIG HOME:** gitignored **`Config/SiegeCloudDev.ini`** — section `[SiegeCloud]`, keys `ProjectUrl=` / `AnonKey=` (+ an optional `; DbPassword=` custody comment line the game NEVER reads). Committed template **`Config/SiegeCloudDev.ini.example`** with placeholders; `.gitignore` gains the exact line `Config/SiegeCloudDev.ini`. **Missing/unparsable config ⇒ cloud OFF and the game behaves byte-identically to Phase 1** — this extends ACC-§1: cloud gates NOTHING, ever.
  - ⭐ **DATED AMENDMENT 2026-08-23 — THE CONFIG FORMAT LAW (TASK-649 loop-2 finding; the `ProjectUrl=`/`AnonKey=` key pin above stands — this rider governs the VALUE format):** **`ProjectUrl` MUST be double-quoted** in `Config/SiegeCloudDev.ini` AND the committed `.example` (`ProjectUrl="https://…"`). UE's ini parser swallows an unquoted `//` as an inline comment on BOTH parse paths — file load (`FConfigFile::Read`) and buffer combine (`CombineFromBuffer`) feed the same line reader with `SwallowDoubleSlashComments` set unconditionally; engine citations in the STEP-1 evidence table of `handoffs/TASK-647-programmer.md` "LOOP 2 FIX" — truncating `https://…` to `https:` while `FSiegeCloudConfig::IsValid()` (a non-empty conjunction) STILL PASSES. That is a **silent cloud-misconfiguration** (`IsCloudConfigured()==true`, every request targeting garbage `https:/…` URLs) — strictly worse than the clean cloud-OFF degrade this section mandates. Quotes are stripped on read (`FParse::QuotedString`), so the quoted value round-trips byte-identically to the client — quoting costs nothing. **`AnonKey` stays UNQUOTED**: the base64url alphabet cannot contain `/` (quoting it would be harmless, but it is not the law). ⛔ The suite's `Siegebound.Cloud.ConfigIniParseSeam` hazard-pin now ENFORCES this format mechanically — it asserts the unquoted form truncates to exactly `https:` and still composes `IsValid()==true` — so no future task may "simplify" the quotes away without that test failing loudly; treat any such failure as this law firing, not a test bug. 📜 **THE RECORD:** production shipped with the unquoted form for ~1 session (every launch came up `Cloud configured: https:.`) and was caught by the OFFLINE seam test BEFORE any live smoke ran (TASK-650 still pending — zero user-visible impact). The seam test caught exactly the failure class it exists for.
- ⭐ **LOCAL-FIRST REMAINS THE LAW.** The local `USaveGame` files stay the on-device source of truth; the cloud is a SYNC LAYER (ACC-§13). ⛔ No gameplay or menu flow may block on an HTTP round trip; every cloud failure degrades to the local Phase-1 behavior with a `LogSiegeCloud` line and a `CloudStatusText` message.
- **Auth transport:** Supabase GoTrue REST (`/auth/v1/signup`, `/auth/v1/token?grant_type=password` / `?grant_type=refresh_token`, `/auth/v1/logout`) via `FHttpModule` + `Json` — ⛔ no third-party SDK (ACC-§0). Real credential hashing is server-side (GoTrue bcrypt).
- ⛔ **THE P1 LOCAL HASH NEVER UPLOADS.** Cloud signup/link takes a **fresh typed password**; the local `FSHA1` convenience hash and salt never leave the machine (ACC-§2 extends to the wire).
- **THE TOKEN LAW (honest, per ACC-§2's lens):** the access token (JWT) lives in MEMORY only. The refresh token MAY persist per-profile as `FSiegeProfileInfo::CloudRefreshToken` — **stored plaintext-on-disk in the local save, the same trust level as every launcher's local session file; ⛔ no artifact may call it "encrypted" or "secure."** Cloud sign-out clears it. ⛔ Neither token is ever logged.
  - ⭐ **DATED ADDITION 2026-08-23 (rider R1, qa/TASK-648.md §6):** the persisted refresh token now has exactly ONE lawful READER — `USiegeAccountSubsystem::GetCloudRefreshToken()` (the ACC-§15 P2.1 seam, TASK-653), consumed ONLY by the `UAccountMenuWidget` re-auth path. Before this addition NO lane could read it — the recorded post-restart re-auth gap. Still ⛔ never logged, never displayed, never sent anywhere but the GoTrue refresh grant.

### ACC-§12 THE SCHEMA + RLS LAW — MIGRATIONS ARE FILES, REVIEWED, THEN APPLIED (2026-08-23)

- ⛔ **NO AD-HOC DDL.** Every schema change is a numbered SQL file in **`Tools/Supabase/migrations/`** (`0001_init_accounts.sql`, `0002_…`), QA-reviewed BEFORE it is applied, applied to the live project via the MCP migration tool by build-master, and the applied-vs-file text must be identical (paste the tool echo in the handoff).
- **The three tables (ACC-§6 reserved names, now live):**
  - `public.profiles` — `id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade` · `display_name text not null` · `updated_at timestamptz not null default now()`
  - `public.decks` — `id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid()` · `user_id uuid not null references auth.users(id) on delete cascade` · `deck_name text not null` · `payload jsonb not null` · `updated_at timestamptz not null default now()` · `unique (user_id, deck_name)`
  - `public.settings` — `user_id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade` · `payload jsonb not null` · `updated_at timestamptz not null default now()`
- **RLS:** `enable row level security` on ALL three; one policy per operation (`select` / `insert` / `update` / `delete`), named **`<table>_<op>_own`**, each bound `auth.uid() = user_id` (`profiles`: `auth.uid() = id`) in `using` AND `with check` as the operation requires. ⛔ No table without RLS; ⛔ no policy referencing `service_role` (it bypasses RLS by definition — a policy naming it is a design smell and a QA FAIL).
- **`updated_at` is SERVER time — the sync clock (A3):** one trigger function **`public.touch_updated_at()`** + a `before update` trigger per table. ⛔ The client never writes `updated_at`.
  - ⭐ **DATED AMENDMENT 2026-08-23 (TASK-640 ruling — the invariant binds over the letter):** the binding trigger wording is **`before insert or update`** — the PostgREST upsert's INSERT branch would otherwise accept a client-supplied `updated_at` and forward-date the A3 last-write-wins clock. The `before update` letter above stands as originally written; this amendment is the operative wording for `0001_init_accounts.sql` (as shipped) and every migration `0002+`. Ruling: `qa/TASK-640.md` §(c)1.
- **Post-apply gate:** the MCP security advisors run must report **zero RLS findings** on these tables; any finding blocks the lane and is escalated, never waived in-task.

### ACC-§13 THE SYNC LAW — EXPLICIT SURFACE, HONEST CONFLICT SHAPE (2026-08-23; A3/A4 defaults live)

- **Granularity:** per-deck row (`unique (user_id, deck_name)`) + ONE settings row per user. Payloads = jsonb projections of the EXISTING save classes' data — ⛔ `USiegeDeckSaveGame` / `USiegeSettingsSaveGame` are NOT rewritten (ACC-§3 survives; serialization is a projection, never a schema change to the save classes).
- ⭐ **THE SYNC SURFACE IS EXPLICIT — exactly three triggers, ⛔ no per-save hooks in P2:** (1) **cloud-login pull** — rows with `updated_at > LastSyncUtc` land locally; (2) **first-link upload** (A4) — the active profile's decks + settings push up once; (3) **Sync Now** (manual button) — pull-newer, then push-all, then `LastSyncUtc = server now`. ⇒ **ZERO edits to the deck/settings lanes' shipped files** — the ACC-§4 enumerated call-site set does not move. Per-save auto-push is a P3 candidate, recorded, not smuggled in.
- **The honest A3 shape:** last-write-wins lands in P2 as *push-wins-at-write / pull-newer-at-sync*. **Recorded limitations (⛔ not bugs):** a row edited on two devices between syncs resolves to the most recent WRITER, not a field merge · deck DELETION does not propagate (no tombstones) — both are P3 work.
- **Guest NEVER syncs** (ACC-§1 — guest has no cloud identity). Sync acts only on the ACTIVE, CLOUD-LINKED profile's slots.
- **Every sync outcome is visible:** `CloudStatusText` states the last result; failures log once on `LogSiegeCloud` and leave local state untouched.

Failure ⇒ one honest `CloudStatusText` line ("cloud session expired — sign in again to re-link"); ⛔ ZERO state mutation on failure (a transient network error must never destroy the link — local-first).

3. **footage-analyst is DIAGNOSE-ONLY** (the qa-reviewer model): never edits code/assets, never opens the editor or any engine/Blender MCP surface, never runs git. The manager consumes the finished report to board EVERY fix; fixes then follow the normal routing rules.

### FR-§1. NAMING + FOLDER LAW (the cross-task contract)
| thing | law |
|---|---|
| video inbox | `<git-root>/testvideo/` (NOT the project folder). Filenames accepted VERBATIM — ⛔ never parse tokens from them, ⛔ never assume a TASK-### (Game Bar names carry double spaces + parentheses); every consumer quotes paths / uses list argv. Default selector = newest mtime among `*.mp4|*.mkv|*.mov`. |

| reports | `.claude/pipeline/footage/VID-###-<symptom-slug>.md` — **VID-###** sequential (next = highest existing + 1); the ID is the join key manager-boarded fix tasks and Slack posts cite |
| evidence | `.claude/pipeline/playtest-evidence/<YYYY-MM-DD>/VID-###[-t<MM>m<SS>s]-<symptom>.png` — written ONLY via the tool's `promote` (the naming law lives in code). This EXTENDS the 2026-08-17 precedent: video-derived frames carry ID+timestamp provenance; manual screenshots keep the old `<location>-<symptom>.png` shape; `handoffs/TASK-###-…` screenshots unchanged |

### FR-§2. TOOL LAW — `Tools/VideoReview/extract_frames.py`
System Python 3.14, stdlib + `subprocess`→ffmpeg only; Pillow OPTIONAL (labeled sheets + `crop` degrade gracefully without it). ⛔ No venv, ⛔ no numpy, ⛔ `Tools/ArtPipeline/.venv` never touched. ⛔ `shell=True` BANNED — list argv everywhere (the double-space law). ### FR-§3. THE TWO-PASS DOCTRINE + BUDGET
Coarse = labeled contact sheets (default 4x3 @ 480px tiles, interval `clamp(duration/48, 0.5, 10)` s — legibility VERIFIED on a real capture 2026-08-26: HUD gold counter readable per tile). Fine = full-res `frames --at` around candidates (0.5–1 s steps; `--run N` is the flicker instrument). Jonathan-given timestamps ⇒ ⛔ skip coarse, go fine at t±2 s. **Budget ≤ ~40 image Reads per video** — at the limit, report what you have and NAME the unexamined. ⛔ No UI-text claims from sheet tiles — `crop --scale 2` first. Pixel-proof doctrine inherited verbatim: report the observation with frame ref + measurement, never the conclusion; motion claims are frame-delta inferences and must say so.

### FR-§4. REPORTING + ROUTING LAW
The report template is pinned in `.claude/agents/footage-analyst.md` (Symptoms → Timeline table → promoted evidence → **Suspected mechanism — HYPOTHESIS, NOT VERDICT** (SC-§20 inheritance) → Routing recommendation → Not examined). Files are the contract; Slack (the 🎬 Footage Review standing thread) is visibility only. The manager boards ALL fixes from the report; downstream QA/compile/commit law unchanged (max-3-loop, never push). Evidence bullets use the path + dense pixel-description shape the manager already consumes.

### FR-§5. ⚠️ KNOWN LIMITATIONS — ⛔ NONE OF THEM ARE BUGS
- **No audio analysis** — anything audible-only is invisible; Jonathan's terminal description is the authoritative symptom source.
- **Temporal resolution is bounded by sampling** — coarse tiles are ±interval/2 (Game Bar captures are VFR); sub-interval events can be missed; `--run` is the instrument for suspected flicker.
- **Claude reads stills, not motion** — stutter/velocity judgments are frame-delta inferences and are labeled as such.
- **Capture compression can mimic rendering defects** — low-confidence findings are flagged, not asserted.
- **Sheet legibility is bounded by the model's image downscale** (~1568 px long edge); the 4x3 default was gate-verified with autocrop on 992×576 content — bigger content or subtler defects may need `--grid 3x2 --tile-width 640` or fine frames.

### DECK-§5 ⛔ THE RIGHT-CLICK MECHANISM — a fresh, narrow, code-authored-widget ruling (ACC-§5's five conditions, argued on THIS widget's facts)

- **Therefore the deck-bar entry is `UDeckSlotEntryWidget` — a CODE-AUTHORED tree, NO `.uasset`** (the `UAccountMenuWidget` route, re-argued fresh as ACC-§5(a) demands): 10 uniform buttons need `NativeOnMouseButtonDown` (C++-only), the duplicate+reparent `WBP_` route is this project's most expensive UI failure mode, and a hand-authored WBP is a Jonathan hand-step not owed for a row of buttons. Conditions cloned as QA criteria: **(a)** scope = `UDeckSlotEntryWidget` ONLY — citing this for another widget is the same misuse; **(b)** tree built and `WidgetTree->RootWidget` set FIRST, then `return Super::RebuildWidget()` (the TASK-444 order — anything after Super is discarded and passes readback while rendering empty); **(c)** reserved name `/Game/UI/WBP_DeckSlotEntry` may be used by nothing else; **(d)** children are `BindWidgetOptional`, construct only if null; **(e)** render/interaction correctness closes on PIXELS/Jonathan, never tree/property readback.

RMB: `NativeOnMouseButtonDown` checks `EKeys::RightMouseButton` → fires `OnRightClicked(SlotIndex)` → returns `FReply::Handled()`; everything else returns `Super`'s reply so LMB still reaches the inner button.
